# Arithmetic Dirichlet series and Tauberian methods, Part II: analytic number theory and zeta functions

This roadmap is the analytic number theory of the atlas: zero-free regions and exceptional zeros, explicit formulas and
zero density, the analytic comparisons for Dedekind, Hecke and Artin L-functions, mean values of multiplicative
functions, the complex-parameter Hurwitz and Lerch functions, two several-variable zeta functions, and spectral and
Bost–Connes zeta functions. The accepted restructuring RS-07 makes it the Part II of the Tau Ceti roadmap *Arithmetic
Dirichlet series and Tauberian methods*: it starts where that roadmap stops (ideal arithmetic functions, norm
regrouping, Euler products, Abel and Perron summation, Landau positivity, Wiener–Ikehara and the generic
prime-number-theorem transfer) and where the pinned Mathlib stops (arithmetic functions, `LSeries`, the Mellin
transform, the Riemann zeta and Dirichlet L-functions with continuation, functional equations and nonvanishing on
Re s ≥ 1, Hurwitz and exponential zeta functions with a circle-valued parameter, the Selberg sieve carrier).

Its consumers are the effective arguments of the atlas’s papers (Bennett–Siksek, Tsimerman, Koymans–Pagano,
Lemke Oliver–Wang–Wood, Skorobogatov–Sofos, Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma, Ghosh–Sarnak, Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth,
Gross–Zagier, Chenevier–Taïbi, Lipnowski–Tsimerman, Shankar–Shankar–Tang–Tayou, Yun–Zhang), and the roadmaps that
import its layers: SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns (SV.3), ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod (ES.4), ArithmeticStatistics
(ST.3), ComputationalNumberTheory (CN.4), ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (ML.3), AdditiveCombinatorics (AC.4) and
PeriodsAndSpecialValues.

The baseline is Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti
`f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`; a library citation names the declaration at those pins, read in its source
file. The current TauCetiRoadmap main (`0d144d0`) and the current Tau Ceti library (`a91d3aa`) were also read, so that
nothing they now contain is planned again. The roadmap is planned at target level: each target below has its exact
statement, hypotheses, a proof sketch citing its source, its direct prerequisites, and, for a definition or
construction, its uses, API and unit tests. Smaller steps are proof ingredients, listed at the end with their
statements and the targets that use them. The [suggested Lean file](../suggested/AnalyticNumberTheory.lean) states the
part of this roadmap that the pinned libraries can already express; the statements below are definitive.

## Scope and boundaries

**Imported, never planned here.**

- Mathlib: `ArithmeticFunction`, `LSeries` and its convergence, derivative and convolution API, `AbelSummation`, the
  Mellin transform and its inversion, `riemannZeta`, `completedRiemannZeta₀`, `DirichletCharacter.LFunction` with its
  completed functional equation and nonvanishing on Re s ≥ 1, `RiemannHypothesis`, `NumberField.dedekindZeta` with its
  real one-sided residue, `hurwitzZeta` and `expZeta` with a `UnitAddCircle` parameter, Chebyshev’s ψ and θ,
  `Nat.primeCounting`, `Nat.smoothNumbers` and the `SelbergSieve` carrier.
- Tau Ceti roadmaps: ArithmeticDirichletSeries (Layers 0–10; current Tau Ceti also proves the prime ideal theorem
  unconditionally), Chebotarev (qualitative Chebotarev in density and prime-counting form, with the
  arithmetic-progression specialization), GlobalNumberFields (Layer 9: Hecke and ray class characters; Layer 3: ray
  class ideal counting), ClassFieldTheory (reciprocity and conductors), NumberFieldArithmetic (Frobenius and
  ramification), ContourIntegration and ConformalMapping (residue theorem and argument principle),
  RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction (Artin and Brauer induction).
- Proposed roadmaps: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0–AL.1 (adelic Poisson summation, Tate’s local and global
  zeta integrals, continuation and functional equations of Hecke L-functions) and AL.3 (Rankin–Selberg L-functions);
  ArithmeticStatistics ST.0–ST.1 (integral orbit parametrizations); SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2–SV.4 (large sieve,
  Bombieri–Vinogradov, prime tuples); AutomorphicSpectralTheory and ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces (spectral and
  trace-formula inputs); LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.3 and AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 (local densities and
  adelic measures for AN.8). Each import is a `requests` entry with its exact need.

**Not owned here.** The qualitative prime number theorem and its fixed-progression form (Tau Ceti); the
arithmetic-scheme Chebotarev theorem (proposed as a Part II of Tau Ceti Chebotarev, see the red-team section);
Bombieri–Vinogradov and stronger distribution hypotheses (SV.3) and prime-tuple statements (SV.4); arithmetic-family
distributions (ST.3–ST.5); multiple zeta values (PeriodsAndSpecialValues); crossed products and factor classification
of operator algebras (requested from an OperatorTheory Part II).

**Owned here.** Everything the layers below state: the effective and quantitative analytic theory that the Tau Ceti
Chebotarev and ArithmeticDirichletSeries roadmaps assign to a roadmap they call “Zeros of L-functions”, which does not
exist upstream.

## Conventions

- **chebyshev.** ψ(x) and θ(x) are Mathlib’s Chebyshev.psi and Chebyshev.theta with inclusive cutoff ⌊x⌋; θ(x;a,q) restricts θ to primes p ≡ a mod q with gcd(a,q) = 1. ψ₀ in explicit formulas gives half weight to x when x is a prime power.
- **characters.** Dirichlet characters are Mathlib DirichletCharacter ℂ N; L(s,χ) is DirichletCharacter.LFunction, which for imprimitive χ keeps the missing Euler factors. Conductor-uniform statements use the conductor of the primitive character, never the modulus.
- **zeros.** Zeros are counted with analytic multiplicity (analyticOrderNatAt). Nontrivial zeros of ζ are the zeros of the entire Riemann xi function; trivial zeros and the junk value of riemannZeta at 1 are excluded explicitly.
- **exceptionalZero.** An exceptional zero is a real zero β of L(s,χ), χ primitive real nonprincipal of conductor N > 1, with 1 − c/log N < β < 1 for a stated c; ineffective constants (Siegel) are labelled as such.
- **perron.** Perron inversion is ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 6: the finite-height kernel at x = 1 is π⁻¹ arctan(T/c), and 1/2 is only its limit.
- **hurwitzLerch.** Mathlib’s Hurwitz zeta takes a parameter in UnitAddCircle; the complex-parameter Hurwitz series is a separate object here. With Φ(z,s,a) = Σ_{n≥0} zⁿ (n+a)^{−s}, Mathlib’s exponential zeta is z·Φ(z,s,1).
- **conditional.** RH, GRH, the extended RH, Artin holomorphy and the moment conjecture are Prop-valued predicates used only as hypotheses of conditional theorems; no unconditional target depends on them.
- **gamma.** Real and complex gamma factors are Mathlib Complex.Gammaℝ s = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Complex.Gammaℂ s = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s).

## AN.2 — Prime number theorems

RS-07 narrows this layer to what the qualitative Tauberian route does not give. The qualitative prime number theorem and its version for a fixed coprime progression are now proved in Tau Ceti (the prime ideal theorem of ArithmeticDirichletSeries and the prime-counting form of Chebotarev); one target restates them in Mathlib’s vocabulary and imports them. Everything else here is quantitative or effective. The analytic core is the theory of entire functions of finite order: canonical factors, Hadamard factorization in order one, and the Riemann ξ function written through Mathlib’s entire completed zeta function, which together give the logarithmic derivative of ζ in the strip and the de la Vallée Poussin zero-free region at large height. From there the layer builds the effective error term in the prime number theorem, the conductor-uniform region for Dirichlet L-functions with its possible exceptional real zero, Landau–Page and Siegel, the Siegel–Walfisz theorem, and the explicit numerical bounds (Rosser–Schoenfeld, Schoenfeld, Ramaré–Rumely) that Bennett–Siksek, Bary-Soroker–Koukoulopoulos–Kozma and Koymans–Pagano quote. Effective and ineffective constants are labelled in every statement.

**Layer acceptance.** The AP statement requires coprime residue class and specifies whether modulus is fixed; ineffective constants and possible exceptional zeros are labelled.

### Pole-cancelled Riemann xi

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/riemann-xi` (definition) · planet: *Riemann xi function*.

ξ(s)=1/2+(1/2)s(s−1)completedRiemannZeta₀(s). This is the entire extension of (1/2)s(s−1)π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2)ζ(s) away from the completed poles, not the pointwise pole-multiplication convention at s=0,1.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define xi directly as 1/2+(s*(s-1)/2)*completedRiemannZeta0 s, reusing its pinned entire carrier.
2. Entirety and reflection are finite algebra applied to the pinned differentiability and reflection of completed0; at 0 and 1 the polynomial term vanishes.
3. For s!=0,1, use completedRiemannZeta_eq and multiply the rational correction terms to obtain the comparison with the regular completed zeta; use the separate gamma nonvanishing condition before comparing to gamma times zeta.

**API.**

- `riemann_xi.entire` (structure): ξ is entire by differentiability of the pinned pole-subtracted completion.
- `riemann_xi.reflection` (relation): ξ(1−s)=ξ(s) for all complex s.
- `riemann_xi.comparison` (compatibility): For s≠0,1, ξ(s)=(1/2)s(s−1)completedRiemannZeta(s).
- `riemann_xi.endpoints` (simp): ξ(0)=ξ(1)=1/2.

**Unit tests.**

- `riemann_xi.zero` (computation): ξ(0)=1/2, not0.
- `riemann_xi.one` (computation): ξ(1)=1/2, not0.
- `riemann_xi.reflection` (computation): ξ(2)=ξ(−1), checking the centre1/2.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/classical-zero-free-region: The genus-one product is applied to the entire xi, not to ζ with its pole..

**Checks.** ξ(0)=1/2, not0. ξ(1)=1/2, not0. ξ(2)=ξ(−1), checking the centre1/2.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:completedRiemannZeta₀`, `mathlib:differentiable_completedZeta₀`, `mathlib:completedRiemannZeta₀_one_sub`, `mathlib:completedRiemannZeta_eq`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §5.1 (5.1.4), xi definition and reflection, printed pp.34–35; Lemma8.3 p.47: The paper motivates xi; the actual definition uses the pinned pole-subtracted completion and therefore has correct endpoint values.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-entire-order-at-most"></a>

### Entire order at most ρ

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/entire-order-at-most` (definition) · planet: *Finite-order entire functions*.

For a complex function f and real ρ, orderAtMost(f,ρ) means ρ≥0, f is entire, and for every b>ρ there is C_b>0 with |f(z)|≤C_b exp(|z|^b) for all z. At ρ=0 this is the same infimum-order convention, including polynomials and the zero function; the latter is excluded in factorization theorems. It is an upper-order predicate, not an exact-order or exponential-type predicate.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the displayed conjunction on the existing complex-function carrier. Compact continuity turns the source's large-radius bound into the global bound; conversely the global bound implies the asymptotic bound.
2. For products at exponent b>ρ choose ρ<b′<b; absorb 2r^b′ into r^b outside a fixed ball and use compact boundedness inside it.

**API.**

- `entire_order_at_most.bound` (projection): Every exponent strictly larger than ρ has its own global multiplicative growth constant.
- `entire_order_at_most.mono` (compatibility): If ρ≤ρ′ and orderAtMost(f,ρ), then orderAtMost(f,ρ′).
- `entire_order_at_most.polynomial` (example): Every polynomial has order at most 0.
- `entire_order_at_most.product` (structure): Products of entire functions of order at most ρ≥0 again have order at most ρ.

**Unit tests.**

- `entire_order_at_most.exp` (computation): exp(z) has order at most 1.
- `entire_order_at_most.exp_square` (non-example): exp(z²) does not have order at most 1.
- `entire_order_at_most.polynomial` (degenerate): 1−z² has order at most 0.
- `entire_order_at_most.xi` (compatibility): For every entire f and real C, if |f(z)|≤exp(C|z|log(2+|z|)) for every z, then orderAtMost(f,1). This upper bound alone asserts neither exact order one nor failure of finite exponential type.
- `entire_order_at_most.zero` (degenerate): The identically zero function has order at most zero.

**Uses.** PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/47: Uniform canonical-product genus and polynomial degree..

**Checks.** exp(z) has order at most 1. exp(z²) does not have order at most 1. 1−z² has order at most 0. For every entire f and real C, if |f(z)|≤exp(C|z|log(2+|z|)) for every z, then orderAtMost(f,1). This upper bound alone asserts neither exact order one nor failure of finite exponential type.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Differentiable`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), Definition 8.1, printed p.47; extension to ρ=0 by the same growth condition: The predicate restates the infimum-order convention. Entirety and nonnegative ρ are part of it; the polynomial boundary case is explicit.

### Genus-one canonical factor

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/genus-one-factor` (definition).

E₁(w)=(1−w)exp(w), for every complex w.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the displayed object on the specified domain using the existing carriers; prove the listed API before its analytic applications.

**API.**

- `genus_one_factor.value` (characterisation): The function is exactly (1−w)exp(w).
- `genus_one_factor.entire` (structure): E₁ is entire.
- `genus_one_factor.zeros` (characterisation): Its only zero is w=1 and that zero is simple.
- `genus_one_factor.pair` (relation): E₁(w)E₁(−w)=1−w².

**Unit tests.**

- `genus_one_factor.origin` (computation): E₁(0)=1.
- `genus_one_factor.root` (computation): E₁(1)=0.
- `genus_one_factor.derivative` (computation): E₁′(0)=0, which excludes the uncorrected factor 1−w.

**Uses.** PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/47: Order-one canonical product..

**Checks.** E₁(0)=1. E₁(1)=0. E₁′(0)=0, which excludes the uncorrected factor 1−w.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Complex.exp`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), Theorem 8.7, (8.2.3), printed p.49; corrected quadratic sign in E6: The factor is (1−w)exp(w). The same factor is E₁ in Yun–Zhang Appendix B.1.

### Hadamard factorization in order at most one

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard` (theorem) · planet: *Hadamard factorization*.

For nonzero entire f of order at most1, f(z)=z^m exp(a+bz)∏_αE₁(z/α), with locally uniform convergence, exact zero multiplicities and finite/empty zero sets permitted.

**Hypotheses and scope.** f is entire, not identically zero, and has order at most one; m is the finite analytic order at zero.

**Proof.**

1. Assemble the origin factor, the canonical product, its entire quotient logarithm and the affine-log theorem.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Hadamard factorization in order at most one.

**Checks.** f(z)=z²exp(z) has the empty nonzero-zero product and m=2. f(z)=1−z² has two simple nonzero zeros; the paired factors give exactly 1−z². Every zero occurrence family is locally finite, and convergence is locally uniform for the net of finite subsets, not merely pointwise.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.2/plan/entire-order-at-most`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-entire-order-at-most), [`AN.2/plan/genus-one-factor`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-genus-one-factor), `mathlib:Complex.borelCaratheodory`, `mathlib:Complex.exists_continuousOn_eqOn_exp_comp`, `mathlib:AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_eq_natCast`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq`, `mathlib:AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_ne_top`, `mathlib:TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.differentiableOn`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.sum_divisor_le`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_or_eventually_ne_zero_of_preconnected`, `mathlib:IsCompact.finite_sdiff_of_mem_codiscreteWithin`, `mathlib:Complex.norm_log_one_add_sub_self_le`, `mathlib:Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_neg_log`, `mathlib:analyticAt_clog`, `mathlib:Complex.exp_eq_one_iff`, `mathlib:Complex.norm_iteratedDeriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le`, `mathlib:is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero`.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-classical-zero-free-region"></a>

### Classical high-height zero-free region

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/classical-zero-free-region` (theorem) · planet: *Classical zero-free region*.

There exist real c>0 and t₀>1 such that ζ(s)≠0 whenever Im(s)≥t₀ and Re(s)≥1−c/log(Im(s)). This is the high positive-height conclusion of Kedlaya's proof, not a full-height effective region or a conductor-uniform Dirichlet region.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The constants c,t₀ are absolute existence constants, not certified numerical values.

**Proof.**

1. Use the nonnegative trigonometric polynomial 3+4 cos θ+cos 2θ with the absolutely convergent logarithmic derivative for Re(s)>1.
2. The simple pole at 1 bounds the real-axis term by 1/(σ−1)+O(1). The corrected Hadamard/Gamma identity bounds the σ+2it term by O(log t). Keeping a zero β+it bounds the σ+it term by O(log t)−1/(σ−β).
3. Combine to obtain 4/(σ−β)≤3/(σ−1)+C log t. Choose σ=1+A/log t with A sufficiently small relative to C to derive β<1−c/log t for t≥t₀.
4. Hadamard factorization, logarithmic differentiation, Gamma estimates, zero summability and effective choices are unresolved named inputs, not hidden routine steps; see the gaps.

**Checks.** t₀>1 avoids division by log 1. This node alone does not control negative or bounded heights. No RH or Siegel-effectivity assumption is inserted.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-exceptional-real-zero"></a>

### Exceptional real zero

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/exceptional-real-zero` (definition).

For c>0 define the c-exceptional predicate for a nontrivial primitive quadratic character χ of conductor N>1 by L(β,χ)=0 and 1−c/log N<β<1, with β real. The exceptional zero used in Proposition 7.1 is this predicate specialized to its effective absolute c_star>0; its conductor is called exceptional. The general parameter does not assert the existence of any zero.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the actual continued primitive quadratic Dirichlet L-function; this predicate does not assert existence of a zero.

**API.**

- `ExceptionalRealZero.iff` (characterisation): For c>0 and N>1, the predicate holds exactly when χ is primitive, nonprincipal and quadratic, L(β,χ)=0, and 1−c/log N<β<1. Equivalently, for arbitrary c,N it is the conjunction of all these conditions, including c>0 and N>1.
- `ExceptionalRealZero.bounds` (projection): An exceptional β lies strictly below 1 and strictly above the specified logarithmic cutoff.
- `ExceptionalRealZero.mono` (compatibility): For 0<c≤c′ the c-exceptional predicate implies the c′-exceptional predicate, with N>1.

**Unit tests.**

- `ExceptionalRealZero.one` (non-example): β=1 is excluded even if a chosen totalized function vanishes there.
- `ExceptionalRealZero.lower_endpoint` (non-example): β=1−c/log N is excluded by the strict inequality.
- `ExceptionalRealZero.principal` (non-example): The principal character and N=1 are outside the domain; log 1 is never used as a denominator.
- `ExceptionalRealZero.supplied_zero` (computation): Given c>0, N>1, a primitive nonprincipal quadratic χ, a real β with L(β,χ)=0 and 1−c/log N<β<1, the c-exceptional predicate holds. This is conditional and makes no existence assertion.

**Uses.** PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/41: Track the distinguished real zero and its conductor, without replacing conductor by a modulus.. PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/88: Track the distinguished real zero and its conductor, without replacing conductor by a modulus.. PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/89: Track the distinguished real zero and its conductor, without replacing conductor by a modulus..

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction`.

**Source.** Reviewed extraction: A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums (Atlas extraction and independent review; original authors: Michael A. Bennett and Samir Siksek), Section 7, Proposition 7.1 and following paragraph, pp. 373-374: Literal title and precise corrected statement of accepted extraction PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/40. The original external proof is not certified by its acceptance.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-theta-ap"></a>

### Chebyshev sum in a residue class

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/theta-ap` (definition).

For q≥1 and a∈ZMod q, θ(x;a,q)=Σ_{p prime, p≤x, p≡a mod q} log p. Inclusive real cutoff, empty for x<2. This specializes the pinned Chebyshev sum; a coprimality hypothesis is required by asymptotic theorems, not by the finite sum.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Construct the displayed object on the specified domain using the existing carriers; prove the listed API before its analytic applications.

**API.**

- `theta_ap.sum` (characterisation): Evaluation is the finite filtered prime sum just displayed.
- `theta_ap.level_one` (compatibility): θ(x;0,1)=Chebyshev.theta x.
- `theta_ap.sum_classes` (relation): For q≥1, summing over all residue classes modulo q gives Chebyshev.theta x. The finite sum is not specified at q=0, where ZMod 0 is infinite.

**Unit tests.**

- `theta_ap.below_two` (computation): θ(1;a,q)=0.
- `theta_ap.mod_eight` (computation): θ(5;3,8)=log 3 and θ(5;5,8)=log 5.
- `theta_ap.noncoprime` (non-example): θ(x;0,2)=log 2 for x≥2; the noncoprime class cannot satisfy x/φ(2) asymptotics.

**Uses.** PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/78: The same class and level occur at both interval endpoints..

**Checks.** θ(1;a,q)=0. θ(5;3,8)=log 3 and θ(5;5,8)=log 5. θ(x;0,2)=log 2 for x≥2; the noncoprime class cannot satisfy x/φ(2) asymptotics.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Chebyshev.theta`.

**Source.** Reviewed extraction: A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums (Atlas extraction and independent review; original authors: Michael A. Bennett and Samir Siksek), §§6–9, especially p. 369: Exact target or stated specialization; unresolved proof inputs are named in the gap ledger.

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/two-real-zero-separation` (theorem).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-exceptional-conductor-repulsion"></a>

### Repulsion of exceptional conductors

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/exceptional-conductor-repulsion` (theorem).

With c_star from Proposition 7.1, two distinct exceptional quadratic conductors N1<N2 satisfy N2>N1^2.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the two-real-zero inequality at the same effective c_star.
2. If N₂≤N₁² then log(N₁N₂)≤3 log N₁, contradicting both strict exceptional cutoffs.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Repulsion of exceptional conductors.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-prime-power-interval-margin"></a>

### Prime powers do not erase the character-sum margin

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/prime-power-interval-margin` (theorem).

Put ε=0.002811. For real k≥2*10^10, the prime-power mass M=psi(k)−theta(k)−psi(k/2)+theta(k/2) is smaller than (((1−3*ε)/8)−0.1239)*k. For b:ℕ→ℂ with |b(n)|≤1 whenever k/2<n≤k, put P=Σ_{k/2<p≤k, p prime}b(p)log p and V=Σ_{k/2<n≤k}b(n)Λ(n). Then |V−P|≤M, so |P|≥(1−3*ε)*k/8 implies |V|>0.1239*k.

**Hypotheses and scope.** k is real and k≥2*10^10; ε=0.002811. b:ℕ→ℂ and |b(n)|≤1 on the summation interval k/2<n≤k; the two sums use the same b and endpoints.

**Proof.**

1. Bound the powers p^j with j≥2 by a sum of theta(k^(1/j)), and subtract endpoints before estimating.
2. Insert the certified constants from the source; retain the strict inequality.
3. On prime terms Λ(p)=log p, and on higher prime powers use |b(p^j)|≤1. The triangle inequality gives |V−P|≤M and |V|≥|P|−M.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Prime powers do not erase the character-sum margin.

**Checks.** Check the certified strict mass bound at the minimum k and all larger k; its original numerical proof remains an open source obligation. The weighted implication requires the same coefficient sequence in both sums and the bound |b(n)|≤1 at higher prime powers, not only at primes.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Chebyshev.psi`, `mathlib:Chebyshev.theta`.

**Source.** Reviewed extraction: A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums (Atlas extraction and independent review; original authors: Michael A. Bennett and Samir Siksek), §6 end of Case I, pp. 369–370; Schoenfeld Theorem 6*, (5.3*)–(5.4*): Literal title and precise corrected statement of accepted extraction PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/79. The original external proof is not certified by its acceptance.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-mertens-first-theorem"></a>

### Mertens's first theorem and Σ_{p | N} log p/p = O(log log N)

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/mertens-first-theorem` (theorem).

For X≥2, Σ_{p<X}(log p)/p=log X+O(1), with an absolute implied constant.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Sum the pinned identity log n=Σ_{d|n}Λ(d) over 1≤n≤x and interchange the finite sums: Σlog n=Σ_{d≤x}Λ(d)floor(x/d). Chebyshev psi(x)=O(x) bounds the floor replacement error by O(x).
2. Use the log-summatory estimate Σ_{n≤x}log n=x log x−x+O(log x); its precise Abel/integral-comparison input is retained in the Mertens first theorem gap. Divide by x to obtain Σ_{d≤x}Λ(d)/d=log x+O(1).
3. The higher-prime-power contribution Σ_pΣ_{k≥2}log p/p^k is bounded by the convergent integer majorant Σ_{m≥2}log m/(m(m−1)). Its convergence/comparison input is also named in that gap.
4. Remove higher prime powers and pass from p≤x to p<x; an endpoint contributes at most log x/x, uniformly bounded for x≥2.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Mertens's first theorem and Σ_{p | N} log p/p = O(log log N).

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_sum`, `mathlib:Chebyshev.psi_le_const_mul_self`, `mathlib:sum_mul_eq_sub_sub_integral_mul`.

**Source.** The Distribution of Prime Numbers (Dimitris Koukoulopoulos), Theorem3.4(a) and proof, printed p.40: The elementary proof uses the convolution identity, Chebyshev upper bound and a log-summatory estimate, not merely qualitative PNT. The strict endpoint differs by a uniformly bounded single term.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-mertens-prime-reciprocal"></a>

### Mertens sum and product inputs

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/mertens-prime-reciprocal` (theorem).

There is a real B such that Σ_{p≤x}1/p=log log x+B+O(1/log x) for real x≥2, with an absolute implied constant.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Replace the strict endpoint in Mertens first theorem by the inclusive one; a possible endpoint contributes at most log x/x, hence a bounded change. Set R(t)=Σ_{p≤t}log p/p−log t, which is bounded for t≥2.
2. Apply pinned Abel summation with weight 1/log t and coefficient (log p)/p at primes, zero otherwise. Obtain Σ_{p≤x}1/p=log log x+B+R(x)/log x−∫_x^∞R(t)/(t(log t)^2)dt, for a single real B.
3. The improper integral defining B converges absolutely; the remaining integral is bounded by sup|R|/log x. This yields the claimed real range x≥2.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Mertens sum and product inputs.

**Checks.** One B and one absolute error constant work for every real x≥2. At x=2 the prime 2 is included; changing the endpoint convention only changes the bounded remainder.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.2/plan/mertens-first-theorem`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-mertens-first-theorem), `mathlib:sum_mul_eq_sub_sub_integral_mul`.

**Source.** The Distribution of Prime Numbers (Dimitris Koukoulopoulos), Theorem3.4(b) and its proof, printed pp.40–41: Direct source statement and bounded-remainder Abel proof; no quantitative PNT is used.

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/mertens-prime-product` (theorem).

3. After κ=γ, exponentiate the O(1/log x) logarithmic error; multiplication by log x gives an additive O(1). This step is not supplied by a mere two-sided comparison.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-qualitative-prime-number-theorems"></a>

### Prime number theorem, and in fixed progressions, from Tau Ceti

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems` (theorem) · planet: *Prime number theorem*.

(i) As x → ∞, ψ(x) ~ x, θ(x) ~ x and π(x) ~ x/log x, where ψ = Chebyshev.psi, θ = Chebyshev.theta and π(x) = Nat.primeCounting ⌊x⌋. (ii) Fix q ≥ 1 and a ∈ ℤ with gcd(a,q) = 1. As x → ∞, θ(x;a,q) ~ x/φ(q) and π(x;a,q) ~ (1/φ(q))·x/log x, where π(x;a,q) counts primes p ≤ x with p ≡ a mod q. The modulus is fixed: the statement has no error term and no uniformity in q.

**Hypotheses and scope.** In (ii), q ≥ 1 is fixed and gcd(a,q) = 1.

**Proof.**

1. (i) is the K = ℚ case of the unconditional prime ideal theorem of ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 10.4 (current Tau Ceti TauCeti.primeIdealTheorem). Transport it along the bijection between height-one primes of 𝓞 ℚ and rational primes: the absolute norm of (p) is p, the ideal von Mangoldt weight of (n) is Λ(n), and the inclusive cutoff of ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 4 is the ⌊x⌋ cutoff of Chebyshev.psi and Chebyshev.theta.
2. (ii) For q ≢ 2 mod 4, apply Chebotarev Layers 13–14 to ℚ(ζ_q)/ℚ and the class of a under Gal(ℚ(ζ_q)/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/qℤ)ˣ, whose Frobenius prime set is the set of primes p ≡ a mod q not dividing q (the arithmetic-progression specialization of the Chebotarev roadmap). For q ≡ 2 mod 4 and a odd, the primes p ≡ a mod q are the primes p ≡ a mod q/2 other than 2, and φ(q) = φ(q/2).
3. The finitely many primes dividing q change θ(x;a,q) by O(log q) and π(x;a,q) by O(1). Convert Li(x) ~ x/log x by ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 6.2.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/rosser-schoenfeld-pi: the qualitative form that the explicit bounds refine. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5/plan/dickman-fixed-u: prime counts in the smooth-number recursion.

**Checks.** q = 1 recovers (i). q = 4: primes ≡ 1 mod 4 and primes ≡ 3 mod 4 each get density 1/2. The coprimality hypothesis is essential: for q = 4, a = 2 the progression contains only the prime 2. q = 6, a = 5 (q ≡ 2 mod 4) agrees with q = 3, a = 2 away from the prime 2. No error term and no growing modulus: the uniform statement is the Siegel–Walfisz target of this layer.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-10-generic-prime-number-theorem-transfer`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-6-abel-and-perron-summation`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-13-ϑ_c-and-π_c`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-14-natural-density-and-consistency-theorems`, `mathlib:Chebyshev.psi`, `mathlib:Chebyshev.theta`, `mathlib:Nat.primeCounting`, `mathlib:Nat.totient`, [`AN.2/plan/theta-ap`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-theta-ap).

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.2/zeta-pole-log-derivative`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §1.3, Lemma 1.7, p. 6; §4.4, Theorem 4.12, p. 27: Lemma 1.7 states the prime number theorem as π(x) ~ x/log x and its equivalence with ϑ(x) ~ x; Theorem 4.12 gives natural density 1/φ(N) for primes in a coprime residue class (its printed hypothesis omits “= 1”, recorded as a misprint). Roadmap: the Chebotarev density theorem (Tau Ceti project), Scope; Layers 11–14; Interfaces supplied to other roadmaps: The Tau Ceti Chebotarev roadmap owns the qualitative prime-counting form of Chebotarev and its arithmetic-progression specialization, and leaves every error term to a separate effective theory. Roadmap: arithmetic Dirichlet series and Tauberian methods (Tau Ceti project), Layer 10 (10.1–10.4): The Tau Ceti ArithmeticDirichletSeries roadmap turns a residue-δ von Mangoldt boundary package into ψ, ϑ and π asymptotics, and states the prime ideal theorem from the all-prime boundary export.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-exceptional-squareclasses"></a>

### Exceptional quadratic squareclasses

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/exceptional-squareclasses` (definition).

For 0<c<1/2 let S(c) consist of nonzero squarefree d≠1 such that the primitive quadratic character of Q(√d) has a real zero β∈[1−c/log(|d|+4),1]. The conductor is |d| or 4|d| as dictated by its fundamental discriminant. Enumerate any finite initial segment by nondecreasing |d|; an infinite enumeration requires infinitude, which is not asserted.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import the Q-specialization character of the quadratic field with fundamental discriminant D(d)=d for d≡1 mod4 and D(d)=4d otherwise. Its positive-integer values are the Kronecker symbol (D(d)/n); primitivity gives conductor |D(d)|.
2. In the supplier prototype, separate the 2-primary part of n before applying the pinned Jacobi symbol to the odd denominator. A plain Jacobi-symbol definition would mishandle even n. The admitted construction is constrained by all character values and primitivity; no arbitrary quadratic character is supplied as data.
3. Take the canonical continued Dirichlet LFunction, not the totalized LSeries outside its convergence domain, and quantify a real zero in the closed interval [1−c/log(|d|+4),1]. Height-bounded selections are finite; no infinite enumeration or zero existence is asserted.

**API.**

- `exceptional_squareclasses.membership` (characterisation): Membership is the stated near-one zero condition for the primitive field character.
- `exceptional_squareclasses.mono` (compatibility): If 0<c≤c′<1/2 then S(c)⊆S(c′).
- `exceptional_squareclasses.finite_height` (data): For each B there are finitely many d∈S(c) with |d|≤B.
- `exceptional_squareclasses.conductor` (compatibility): Every estimate uses the field’s fundamental discriminant conductor, retaining the possible factor 4.

**Unit tests.**

- `exceptional_squareclasses.trivial` (non-example): d=1 is excluded, so a principal pole cannot be called an exceptional zero.
- `exceptional_squareclasses.minus_one` (computation): d=−1 has conductor 4, not conductor 1.
- `exceptional_squareclasses.two` (computation): d=2 has conductor 8, not 2.
- `exceptional_squareclasses.finite` (computation): The definition permits an empty or finite S(c); it does not fabricate an infinite sequence.

**Uses.** PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO/182: Repulsion applies to successive existing entries of the ordered set..

**Checks.** d=1 is excluded, so a principal pole cannot be called an exceptional zero. d=−1 has conductor 4, not conductor 1. d=2 has conductor 8, not 2. The definition permits an empty or finite S(c); it does not fabricate an infinite sequence.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-10-archimedean-characters-infinity-types-and-cyclotomic-arithmetic`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction`.

**Source.** On Stevenhagen’s conjecture (Peter Koymans, Carlo Pagano), §7.2 Definition7.5 and its enumeration paragraph, p.61: Closed near-one interval and+4 denominator checked. Nonzero/nontrivial field and finite-enumeration conventions are made explicit; its canonical quadratic-character carrier remains unresolved.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-squareclass-exceptional-repulsion"></a>

### Landau repulsion for exceptional squareclasses

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/squareclass-exceptional-repulsion` (theorem).

There is an effective absolute0<c_Landau<1/2 such that distinct d,e∈S(c_Landau) with |d|≤|e| satisfy |d|²≤|e|. This pairwise form applies to every existing finite ordered segment; no infinitude of S(c_Landau) is asserted.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Let Q_d be the fundamental-discriminant conductor. For nonzero squarefree d≠1, |d|≤Q_d≤4|d| and |d|≥1. Distinct squareclasses have distinct primitive field characters even when their absolute radicands agree.
2. If |e|<|d|², then Q_d Q_e<16|d|³. For a=|d|≥1, log(16a³)≤5log(a+4), since16a³≤(a+4)^5. Also log(|e|+4)≥log(|d|+4).
3. Both near-one zeros are at least1−c_Landau/log(|d|+4). Since log(Q_d Q_e)≤5log(|d|+4), choose c_Landau≤3c_star/5; both are then at least1−3c_star/log(Q_d Q_e), contradicting two_real_zero_separation.
4. Choose c_Landau effectively small enough to lie in(0,1/2). The strict two-real-zero theorem is still an unverified source input; the elementary conductor-log deduction introduces no new analytic theorem.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Landau's theorem on the repulsion of exceptional real zeros.

**Checks.** The conclusion is pairwise and vacuous for an empty/singleton exceptional set. Retain Q_−1=4 and Q_2=8; replacing conductor by |d| breaks the cited analytic input. Use the explicit slack c_Landau≤3c_star/5 and log(Q_d Q_e)≤5log(|d|+4). This keeps the factor4 and the+4 height convention.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.2/plan/exceptional-squareclasses`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-exceptional-squareclasses), [`AN.2/plan/two-real-zero-separation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-two-real-zero-separation).

**Source.** On Stevenhagen’s conjecture (Peter Koymans, Carlo Pagano), §7.2 Definition7.5 and following paragraph, p.61: Printed square-growth assertion checked. The pairwise proof and explicit conductor-log constant are reviewer deductions conditional on the existing two-real-zero supplier.

### Strict derivative positivity requires nonpolynomiality

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/paired-product-strict-derivatives` (theorem).

If the preceding f is not a polynomial, every derivative f^(k)(x) with k≡m mod2 is strictly positive for x>0, and the same-parity Taylor coefficients from degree m onward are positive.

**Proof.**

1. Nonpolynomiality forces infinitely many pairs, so for every coefficient beyond m choose sufficiently many positive factors.
2. The nonnegative convergent derivative series gives strict positivity for x>0.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Strict derivative positivity requires nonpolynomiality.

**Checks.** cosh(z) has infinitely many purely imaginary zero pairs and strictly positive same-parity Taylor coefficients. The polynomial 1+z² satisfies the pairing hypotheses but its fourth derivative is zero; nonpolynomiality is essential. Coefficients of degree below m vanish, including same-parity ones; positivity starts at degree m.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.deriv`, [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard), [`AN.2/plan/genus-one-factor`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-genus-one-factor).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-canonical-factor"></a>

### Elementary canonical factors of every genus

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/canonical-factor` (definition).

For n≥0 define E_n(w)=(1−w)exp(Σ_(j=1)^n w^j/j), with an empty sum for n=0. This is an entire function with a simple zero exactly at1. Genus1 agrees with the existing E₁.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the finite polynomial sum and exponential. On |w|≤1/2 cancel the first n Taylor coefficients of log(1−w); the remaining series is O_n(|w|^(n+1)).

**API.**

- `canonical_factor.zero_genus` (simp): E₀(w)=1−w.
- `canonical_factor.one_genus` (compatibility): E₁(w)=(1−w)e^w equals genus_one_factor.
- `canonical_factor.entire` (structure): E_n is entire for every n.
- `canonical_factor.zeros` (characterisation): E_n(w)=0 iff w=1, and its vanishing order there is1.
- `canonical_factor.log_tail` (relation): There is C_n>0 with |log(1−w)+Σ_(j=1)^n w^j/j|≤C_n|w|^(n+1) for |w|≤1/2, using the principal analytic log.

**Unit tests.**

- `canonical_factor.origin` (degenerate): E_n(0)=1 for every n.
- `canonical_factor.root` (computation): E_n(1)=0 for every n.
- `canonical_factor.genus_zero` (computation): E₀(w)=1−w, with no exponential factor.
- `canonical_factor.genus_one` (computation): E₁(w)E₁(−w)=1−w².

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Elementary canonical factors of every genus.

**Checks.** Verify the stated constants, endpoints and conventions against the source and discriminating examples.

### Finite-order Hadamard factorization

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/finite-order-hadamard` (theorem).

For nonzero entire f of finite order at most ρ≥0, set n=floor ρ. Its nonzero zeros α with multiplicity satisfy Σ|α|^(−n−1)<∞ and f(z)=z^m exp(h(z))∏E_n(z/α), where E_n(w)=(1−w)exp(Σ_{j=1}^n w^j/j), h is a polynomial of degree≤n and the product converges locally uniformly. Finite/empty zero sets are allowed.

**Proof.**

1. Generalize the Jensen annulus and canonical-log-tail proofs from n=1 to n=floorρ.
2. Use a good-circle lower bound, Borel–Carathéodory and Cauchy estimates to kill derivatives of order>n.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Finite-order Hadamard factorization.

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit.

### Classical PNT remainder

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error` (theorem).

There are absolute effective c,C>0 such that |ψ(x)−x|≤C x exp(−c√log x) for all sufficiently large x; ψ is the inclusive pinned function.

**Proof.**

1. Use the truncated ψ₀ formula with analytic multiplicities, conjugation of Riemann zeros and the high positive-height zero-free region. For |Imρ|≥t₀ this gives β≤1−c/log|Imρ|.
2. The low-height critical zeros form a finite multiset. Pinned line-one nonvanishing and nonzero xi endpoints give a positive margin δ from β=1 and nonzero ρ; sum their finitely many |1/ρ| separately, never dividing by Imρ=0.
3. For high zeros the dyadic zero-weight bound gives O(log²T); hence their sum is O(x exp(−c log x/log T) log²T).
4. Choose T=exp(a sqrt(log x)) for one fixed a>0. The Perron endpoint/nearest-prime-power term is at most log x; absorb this, the finite low-zero O(x^(1−δ)) and powers of log x into a weaker exp(−c′sqrt(log x)) bound. Effectivity of the compact margin/constants remains an explicit gap.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Classical PNT remainder.

**Checks.** Inclusive ψ and half-weight ψ₀ differ by at most (1/2)log x, already absorbed. Real zeros, if treated before excluding them, are in the finite low-height sum and never divided by ordinate0.

### Siegel–Walfisz theorem

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/siegel-walfisz` (theorem) · planet: *Siegel–Walfisz theorem*.

For every A,B>0, uniformly for q≤(log x)^B and gcd(a,q)=1, π(x;a,q)=Li(x)/φ(q)+O_{A,B}(x(log x)^−A) as x→∞. The constant and threshold may be ineffective.

**Proof.**

1. Use the conductor-uniform character estimate including its exceptional contribution, reduce imprimitive characters with their finite Euler corrections, and apply exact finite orthogonality to the progression Λ coefficient.
2. Derive an ineffective separation 1−β≥c_ε q^(−ε) for primitive real characters from Siegel’s L(1,χ) lower bound together with a conductor-controlled derivative estimate near1. The L-value lower bound alone is not a zero-separation theorem; this adapter remains a gap.
3. For q≤(log x)^B choose ε<1/B (for example 1/(2(B+1))). Then x^β/x≤exp(−c_ε (log x)^(1−Bε)), which absorbs any fixed power of log x. Character averaging cannot increase the uniform coefficient bound.
4. Dominate higher prime powers by pinned ψ−θ, then apply the generic ADS Abel transfer. The constants and threshold may be ineffective and depend on A,B before quantifying over q,a,x.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2: Siegel–Walfisz theorem.

**Checks.** For B=1 one may take ε=1/4; the exceptional relative term is ≤exp(−c(log x)^(3/4)). The assertion is restricted to reduced classes and logarithmic modulus growth; it is not an effective uniform theorem for every modulus.

## AN.3 — Explicit formulas and density estimates

RS-07 keeps this layer whole until the reversal of its edge with the large sieve can be applied, and gives it the RH/GRH statement register of the dropped AN.6. Zeros of ζ are counted with analytic multiplicity through the zeros of ξ; the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula counts them; the truncated explicit formula for ψ₀ comes from the Perron formula of ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 6, with every residue, horizontal integral and the nearest-prime-power error accounted for. Weil’s explicit formula is stated in Mestre’s axiomatic form with its test-function hypotheses. Zero-density estimates (Selberg’s input and the ray-class family estimate of Lemke Oliver–Wang–Wood), the Montgomery–Vaughan mean value of Dirichlet polynomials, Davenport’s Möbius cancellation and the Eisenstein–Weyl bound of Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth complete the unconditional part. RH and GRH are propositions; the conditional error terms carry them as hypotheses and no unconditional target uses them.

**Layer acceptance.** A contour shift accounts for poles, trivial zeros and horizontal integrals; no GRH estimate is imported into an unconditional theorem.

### Finite zero multiset

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/zeta-zero-multiset` (definition) · planet: *Zeros with analytic multiplicity*.

For T≥0, Z(T) is the finite multiset of nontrivial zeros of ξ in 0≤Re ρ≤1 and |Im ρ|<T, with each ρ repeated analyticOrderNatAt ξ ρ times. The strict height cutoff and finite analytic orders are mandatory; the compact enclosing rectangle proves finiteness.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use xi entirety and nonzero endpoints, and its strict zero-strip lemma. The closed rectangle0≤Reρ≤1,|Imρ|≤T is compact, so isolated zeros and finite analytic orders give a finite support.
2. Restrict to the strict height cutoff and use a Finsupp over complex points whose value is the analytic order; Multiset repetition is an equivalent presentation.
3. The xi/zeta multiplicity comparison on the open strip multiplies zeta by analytic nonzero elementary/gamma factors. The Mellin comparison gives conjugation of xi; conjugation preserves analytic orders.
4. For T≤0 the strict-height support is empty. Prove the monotonicity and endpoint tests without confusing the enclosing closed rectangle with the actual strict cutoff.

**API.**

- `zeta_zero_multiset.multiplicity` (characterisation): The multiplicity of ρ in Z(T) is its finite analytic order if it lies in the stated rectangle, and0 otherwise.
- `zeta_zero_multiset.mono` (functoriality): If T≤U then Z(T) is a submultiset of Z(U).
- `zeta_zero_multiset.conjugation` (relation): Conjugation preserves the zero multiset and multiplicities.
- `zeta_zero_multiset.xi_zeta` (compatibility): On 0<Re ρ<1, ξ and ζ have the same zeros and analytic multiplicities.

**Unit tests.**

- `zeta_zero_multiset.zero_height` (computation): Z(0) is empty, using the strict height inequality.
- `zeta_zero_multiset.double` (computation): A double analytic zero occurs twice, not once.
- `zeta_zero_multiset.endpoint` (non-example): A zero with |Im ρ|=T is excluded from Z(T).
- `zeta_zero_multiset.poles` (computation): s=0 and1 are not xi zeros since ξ has value1/2 there.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error: The residue sum uses multiplicities and an unambiguous height cutoff..

**Checks.** Z(0) is empty, using the strict height inequality. A double analytic zero occurs twice, not once. A zero with |Im ρ|=T is excluded from Z(T). s=0 and1 are not xi zeros since ξ has value1/2 there.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.2/plan/riemann-xi`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-riemann-xi), `mathlib:AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_eq_natCast`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq`, `mathlib:AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_zero_or_eventually_ne_zero_of_preconnected`, `mathlib:IsCompact.finite_sdiff_of_mem_codiscreteWithin`, `mathlib:AnalyticAt.analyticOrderAt_ne_top`, `mathlib:analyticOrderNatAt`, `mathlib:differentiable_completedZeta₀`, `mathlib:riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`, `mathlib:riemannZeta_eq_completedRiemannZeta₀`, `mathlib:Complex.Gamma_ne_zero_of_re_pos`, `mathlib:HurwitzZeta.evenKernel`, `mathlib:HurwitzZeta.hasSum_int_evenKernel`, `mathlib:HurwitzZeta.hurwitzEvenFEPair`, `mathlib:HurwitzZeta.completedHurwitzZetaEven₀`, `mathlib:WeakFEPair.f_modif`, `mathlib:WeakFEPair.Λ₀`, `mathlib:mellin`.

### Truncated von Mangoldt formula

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error` (theorem) · planet: *Von Mangoldt explicit formula*.

For x≥2 and T≥2, let ψ₀(x)=∑_{1≤n<x}Λ(n)+(1/2)∑_{1≤n=x}Λ(n), and let d(x)>0 be the distance to the nearest prime power other than x. There is an absolute C such that ψ₀(x)−x=−∑_{ρ:0≤Reρ≤1, |Imρ|<T}x^ρ/ρ−ζ′(0)/ζ(0)−(1/2)log(1−x⁻²)+R(x,T), with zeros counted with analytic multiplicity and |R(x,T)|≤C[x log²(xT)/T+(log x)min(1,x/(T d(x)))]. Powers of positive x use exp(ρ log x). The PNT-error corollary formerly bundled under this ID is a separate remaining target.

**Hypotheses and scope.** x≥2; T≥2; zeros counted with multiplicity; symmetric strict height cutoff; half-weight at a prime-power endpoint.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the ADS truncated arithmetic Perron formula to the half-weight ψ₀.
2. Shift the contour using the residue lemma, horizontal bound and left-contour limit.
3. Adjust from a good height to the stated strict cutoff with multiplicity-weighted local zero counting; include the nearest-prime-power error.

**Checks.** At a prime power m, ψ₀(m)=Chebyshev.psi(m)−Λ(m)/2; at x=2 the value is (log2)/2, not log2. Multiplicity cannot be replaced by a set of distinct zeros. At a zero height T, a strict cutoff must agree with the height-adjustment error, not silently switch to ≤.

### Uniform Stirling bounds for Γ on vertical strips

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/uniform-complex-stirling` (theorem).

Fix real numbers a ≤ b. (i) As |y| → ∞, |Γ(x + iy)| = √(2π) |y|^{x−1/2} e^{−π|y|/2} (1 + o(1)) uniformly for x ∈ [a, b]. (ii) Consequently, for fixed real α, β there are C, c > 0 with c |t|^{α−β} ≤ |Γ(σ + α + it)/Γ(σ + β + it)| ≤ C |t|^{α−β} for σ ∈ [a, b] and |t| ≥ 1 (with σ + α + it and σ + β + it away from the poles), the exponential factors cancelling. (iii) Every finite product of such ratios, and of the gamma blocks of the completed Dedekind, Hecke and Shintani functions, is bounded by C(1 + |t|)^N on each closed vertical strip away from its poles.

**Hypotheses and scope.** a ≤ b fixed; the implied constants depend on a, b, α, β.

**Proof.**

1. From the Stirling series for Ln Γ in |ph z| ≤ π − δ (DLMF 5.11.1) at z = x + iy, the real part of (z − 1/2) Ln z − z gives (x − 1/2) ln|y| − π|y|/2 + O(1/|y|) uniformly for bounded x; this is DLMF 5.11.9.
2. (ii) and (iii) follow by taking quotients and products; the bounded-height region is a compact set on which the functions are continuous and nonzero away from the poles.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/critical-line-gamma-quotient: the quotient bound on Re s = 1/2. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation: growth of the gamma blocks of the reflection matrix. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.8/plan/cubic-pole-cleared-convexity: vertical growth for Phragmén–Lindelöf.

**Checks.** x = 1/2: |Γ(1/2 + iy)| = (π / cosh(π y))^{1/2}, whose asymptotic is √(2π) e^{−π|y|/2}, matching (i). α − β = 1/2 recovers the critical-line quotient of this layer, |Γ((s+α)/2)Γ((s+β)/2)/Γ(s)| ≪ |s|^{1/2}.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Complex.Gamma`.

**Source.** NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §5.11 Gamma function: asymptotic expansions (F. W. J. Olver, A. B. Olde Daalhuis, D. W. Lozier et al. (eds.); Chapter 5 by R. A. Askey and R. Roy), §5.11(i), equations (5.11.1) and (5.11.9): Equation (5.11.1) is the Stirling series for Ln Γ in a sector, and (5.11.9) is the resulting asymptotic for |Γ(x + iy)| as |y| → ∞, uniform for bounded x.

### Eisenstein Weyl sums bounded by Dirichlet L-values

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/eisenstein-weyl-lvalue-bound` (theorem).

There is an absolute C > 0 such that, for every ε > 0, every fundamental D = d'd ≠ 1 with genus character χ, and every s with Re(s) = 1/2: Weyl(E(·,s),χ) ≪_ε |s|^C |L(s,χ_{d'})L(s,χ_d)| |D|^{1/4+ε}. The paper prints the left side as 'Weyl(s,χ)'.

**Hypotheses and scope.** d,d′ are coprime fundamental discriminants with fundamental product D≠1, and s=1/2+it for t∈ℝ. Weyl is the three-branch class sum of DIT (5.12): twice the core-area integral for negative factors, the boundary arc-length integral over ∂F_A for positive factors (compared separately to C_A), and the CM point sum weighted by 1/ω_D for mixed signs. All branches retain the genus character and multiplicities. The implied constant depends only on ε; the height exponent C is absolute.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the appropriate one of the three genus-period identities.
2. Use the precise gamma quotient and reciprocal-zeta bounds; polynomial height factors and |D|^(1/4+ε) remain visible.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-weil-test-function"></a>

### Admissible Weil test function

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/weil-test-function` (definition) · planet: *Weil test functions*.

For c≥0 and F:R→R, weil_test_function(c,F) means that some ε>0 makes G(x)=F(x)exp((1/2+c+ε)|x|) Lebesgue integrable and of bounded variation on R, that F(x)=(F(x−)+F(x+))/2 at every x, and that the difference quotient q(x)=(F(x)−F(0))/x for x≠0, set to0 at x=0, has bounded variation on R. The quotient may have distinct finite one-sided limits at0; no differentiability at0 is imposed. These symmetric-tail hypotheses are a strengthening of Mestre’s printed one-signed weight. They supply both F and its reflection in the contour proof.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the pinned real bounded-variation and strict one-sided-limit notions, not a replacement variation or limit carrier. Finite weighted variation implies local finite variation of F and genuine one-sided limits.
2. Use ordinary real division at x=0 to choose q(0)=0; changing this single finite value does not affect integrability or finite variation. Bound q near0 to obtain F(x)−F(0)=O(|x|).
3. For the transform on −c≤Re s≤1+c, dominate its norm by |G(x)|exp(−ε|x|). Reflection and real linear combinations retain the conditions after decreasing ε.

**API.**

- `weil_test_function.transform` (data): Define Φ_F(s)=∫_R F(x)exp((s−1/2)x)dx with the complex exponential. For an admissible F, the integrand is absolutely integrable whenever −c≤Re s≤1+c; totalized integration is never a convergence claim.
- `weil_test_function.reflection` (functoriality): x↦F(−x) is admissible with the same c,ε.
- `weil_test_function.add` (structure): Real linear combinations of admissible functions are admissible, after decreasing ε if needed.
- `weil_test_function.normalization` (projection): F equals the mean of its two one-sided limits, fixing boundary values in the summation formula.
- `weil_test_function.mono` (compatibility): If F is admissible for c and 0≤c′≤c then F is admissible for c′, using ε′=ε+c−c′.
- `weil_test_function.continuous_at_zero` (characterisation): Admissibility implies a finite constant C≥0 with |F(x)−F(0)|≤C|x| for all x, hence continuity at0; the one-sided derivatives need not agree.

**Unit tests.**

- `weil_test_function.zero` (computation): F=0 is admissible and Φ=0.
- `weil_test_function.gaussian` (computation): For c≥0, F(x)=exp(−x²) is admissible and Φ_F(1/2)=√π.
- `weil_test_function.one_tail` (non-example): F(x)=exp(−2x) on all R satisfies neither two-tail integrability nor the required Fourier transform; a one-tail test is rejected.
- `weil_test_function.kink` (computation): F(x)=exp(−|x|) is admissible for c=0, although (F(x)−F(0))/x has one-sided limits1 and−1 at0. A removable-continuous-quotient requirement would wrongly reject it.
- `weil_test_function.asymmetric_tail` (non-example): F(x)=exp(x/4) for x<0 and exp(−2x) for x≥0 satisfies Mestre’s one-signed weighted integrability/BV conditions at c=0, ε=1/4 and the difference-quotient condition, but is not admissible here and its ordinary transform integral at s=0 diverges.

**Uses.** PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20/mestre-explicit-formula: Controls both prime-power directions and the symmetric zero sum.. Mestre§I.2, pp.213–214, reflected vertical contour; Chenevier–Taïbi§2.3 p.275: Both vertical sides require the negative tail. CT uses even c=0 functions; that specialization avoids the printed asymmetric-tail defect..

**Checks.** F=0 is admissible and Φ=0. For c≥0, F(x)=exp(−x²) is admissible and Φ_F(1/2)=√π. F(x)=exp(−2x) on all R satisfies neither two-tail integrability nor the required Fourier transform; a one-tail test is rejected. F(x)=exp(−|x|) is admissible for c=0, although (F(x)−F(0))/x has one-sided limits1 and−1 at0. A removable-continuous-quotient requirement would wrongly reject it. F(x)=exp(x/4) for x<0 and exp(−2x) for x≥0 satisfies Mestre’s one-signed weighted integrability/BV conditions at c=0, ε=1/4 and the difference-quotient condition, but is not admissible here and its ordinary transform integral at s=0 diverges.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:BoundedVariationOn`, `mathlib:Function.leftLim`, `mathlib:Function.rightLim`, `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Integrable`, `mathlib:MeasureTheory.integral`.

**Source.** Formules explicites et minorations de conducteurs de variétés algébriques (Jean-François Mestre), §I.2, pp.212–214: The symmetric weight is an explicit correction/strengthening; bounded variation of q does not require its two one-sided limits at0 to coincide. E20 records the printed negative-tail omission.

### Weil's explicit formula (Mestre's formalism)

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/mestre-weil-explicit-formula` (theorem).

Let A, B > 0, a_i, a′_i ≥ 0 (1 ≤ i ≤ M) with Σ a_i = Σ a′_i, b_i, b′_i ∈ C with non-negative real parts, and Λ_1, Λ_2 meromorphic on C with (i) Λ_1(1 − s) = wΛ_2(s) for some w ∈ C^×; (ii) finitely many poles; (iii) Λ_i minus its singular parts bounded in every vertical strip of finite width; (iv) for some c ≥ 0 and Re s > 1 + c, Λ_1(s) = A^s Π_{i=1}^M Γ(a_i s + b_i) Π_p Π_{i=1}^{M′} (1 − α_i(p)p^{−s})^{−1} and Λ_2(s) = B^s Π_{i=1}^M Γ(a′_i s + b′_i) Π_p Π_{i=1}^{M′} (1 − β_i(p)p^{−s})^{−1} with |α_i(p)|, |β_i(p)| ≤ p^c. Let F satisfy weil_test_function(c,F). For every zero gamma slope a_i=0 (respectively a′_i=0), assume b_i≠0 (respectively b′_i≠0), so its constant gamma factor is finite and nonzero. Then Σ_ρ Φ(ρ) − Σ_μ Φ(μ) + Σ_{i=1}^M I(a_i, b_i) + Σ_{i=1}^M J(a′_i, b′_i) = F(0) log(AB) − Σ_{p,i,k≥1} (α_i(p)^k F(k log p) + β_i(p)^k F(−k log p)) log p / p^{k/2}, where ρ (resp. μ) runs over the zeros (resp. poles) of Λ_1 with −c ≤ Re ≤ 1 + c, with multiplicity, Σ_ρ Φ(ρ) = lim_{T→∞} Σ_{|Im ρ|<T} Φ(ρ), Φ(s) = ∫_R F(x) e^{(s−1/2)x} dx, I(a, b) = a ∫_0^∞ (F(ax) e^{−(a/2+b)x}/(1 − e^{−x}) − F(0) e^{−x}/x) dx and J(a, b) is the same with F(−ax). For a>0 the displayed I,J are ordinary convergent combined integrals (do not integrate the two individually divergent subtraction terms separately). For a=0 set I(0,b)=J(0,b)=0 after removing its constant gamma factor; this is not0 times an undefined integral.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Remove finite nonzero constant gamma factors (zero slopes); their logarithmic derivatives are0 and rescaling the dual functions changes only w. Preserve A,B and the equal positive gamma-slope sums.
2. Use pole-clearing and vertical-strip bounds to obtain polynomial strip growth, locally finite zeros and safe heights with a logarithmic-derivative bound. The needed general strip may be wider than the −1<σ<2 printed in Remark1.1.3.
3. Integrate Φ_F(s)Λ′_1(s)/Λ_1(s) on a rectangle and count orders of zeros/poles. The functional equation converts the left edge to the reflected F term; symmetric-tail hypotheses justify both edges.
4. Fourier inversion yields each prime-power term. For a>0 the combined gamma integral uses Lemma1.2.1 and the Poitou pairing Lemma1.2.2; near0 use the bounded difference quotient for cancellation before integrating.
5. Pass to the symmetric zero-sum limit with the exact multiplicities. The original Poitou/good-height/uniform Fourier-limit inputs are recorded gaps, not routine algebra.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3: Weil's explicit formula (Mestre's formalism).

**Checks.** For F=0 every term vanishes. For the completed Riemann zeta take c=0, a=a′=1/2, b=b′=0, A=B=π^(−1/2), α=β=1. Its two pole terms are Φ_F(0)+Φ_F(1), and the prime side has both ±k log p contributions. Adding a finite nonzero constant gamma factor with slope0 changes no explicit-formula term; a zero-slope Γ(0) is excluded. The asymmetric F in test weil_test_function.asymmetric_tail is excluded: Φ_F(0) in the Riemann pole term would diverge under the printed one-signed conditions.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.3/plan/weil-test-function`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-weil-test-function), `tauceti:Completed/ContourIntegration#layer-4-the-hungerbühlerwasem-generalized-residue-theorem-hw-theorem-33`.

**Source.** Formules explicites et minorations de conducteurs de variétés algébriques (Jean-François Mestre), §I.1–I.2, pp.211–215; Remark1.1.3, Lemmas1.2.1–1.2.2: Full source argument read; exact I,J signs/subtractions and symmetric zero summation checked on images. Negative-tail and zero-slope conventions are corrected explicitly; Poitou’s proof remains unread. Discrete series multiplicities for classical groups over Z and level 1 algebraic cusp forms (Gaëtan Chenevier, Olivier Taïbi), §2.3 pp.275–276, (2.3.5): The motivating automorphic specialization is even with c=0, not an arbitrary asymmetric test.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula"></a>

### Half-interval explicit formula and low-zero-safe bound

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula` (theorem).

There are absolute C>0 and k₀≥2 such that for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet characterχ of conductor q, integer k≥k₀ and real2≤T≤k, Σ_(k/2<m≤k)χ(m)Λ(m)=−Σ_(nontrivial zeros |Imρ|≤T)mρ(k^ρ−(k/2)^ρ)/ρ+E, with |E|≤C[k log²(qk)/T+log²(qk)]. Endpoint sums are over positive integers; powers use exp(ρ log x).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Establish the primitive conductor-uniform finite-height explicit formula, with its exact near-zero parity term and safe-height adjustment. KedlayaTheorem10.2 cites Davenport§19; this original proof remains required.
2. Subtract the formulas at k and k/2 before taking absolute values. The character constant b(χ) cancels, and the even-character logarithm difference is a bounded log2 term after using the corrected parity convention.
3. For integer k both endpoints have nearest-other-prime-power distance at least1/2. Apply the two finite Perron remainder bounds; since T≤k,log(qkT)≤2log(qk).
4. Convert endpoint half weights to the unweighted(k/2,k] sum at cost O(log k). Adjust a safe strict cutoff to the stated inclusive |Imρ|≤T using the conductor-uniform local count and the low-zero-safe kernel.
5. Apply the bounded-weight zero sum to consumers requiring an absolute bound. Imprimitive characters require separate deleted local Euler factors and are not included in this signature.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-generalized-riemann-hypothesis"></a>

### Riemann and generalized Riemann hypotheses as statements

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/generalized-riemann-hypothesis` (definition) · planet: *Generalized Riemann hypothesis*.

For a Dirichlet character χ modulo N ≥ 1, DirichletGRH χ is the proposition: for every s ∈ ℂ with Re s > 0, (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1) and L(s,χ) = 0 imply Re s = 1/2, where L(s,χ) is DirichletCharacter.LFunction χ s. GRH is the proposition that DirichletGRH χ holds for every N ≥ 1 and every χ modulo N. The Riemann hypothesis is Mathlib’s RiemannHypothesis. These are statements, never assumptions of an unconditional theorem; a theorem that uses one carries it as an explicit hypothesis.

**Hypotheses and scope.** N ≥ 1; χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition. The restriction Re s > 0 removes the trivial zeros (Re s ≤ 0) and, for imprimitive χ, the zeros of the missing Euler factors 1 − χ*(p)p^{−s}, which lie on Re s = 0; the clause (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1) removes the junk value at the pole of the principal character.
2. By Mathlib’s nonvanishing on Re s ≥ 1 (DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re), only zeros in the open critical strip are constrained.

**API.**

- `DirichletGRH` (data): The proposition defined above, for one character.
- `GRH` (data): For all N ≥ 1 and all χ modulo N, DirichletGRH χ.
- `DirichletGRH.re_eq_half` (projection): If DirichletGRH χ, 0 < Re s, (χ ≠ 1 or s ≠ 1) and L(s,χ) = 0, then Re s = 1/2.
- `dirichletGRH_one_iff_riemannHypothesis` (compatibility): For the trivial character modulo 1, DirichletGRH holds if and only if RiemannHypothesis holds: L(s,1) = ζ(s), and ζ has no zeros with Re s ≤ 0 other than the trivial zeros −2, −4, ….
- `DirichletGRH.of_primitive` (relation): DirichletGRH χ holds if and only if DirichletGRH holds for the primitive character inducing χ: the two L-functions differ by finitely many Euler factors, whose zeros lie on Re s = 0.
- `GRH.riemannHypothesis` (relation): GRH implies RiemannHypothesis.

**Unit tests.**

- `DirichletGRH.trivial_zero_excluded` (non-example): For the trivial character modulo 1, the trivial zero s = −2 of ζ does not contradict DirichletGRH: Re(−2) ≤ 0 is outside the constrained region.
- `DirichletGRH.euler_factor_zero_excluded` (non-example): For the principal character modulo 2, L(s,χ) = (1 − 2^{−s})ζ(s) vanishes at s = 2πi/log 2; this zero has real part 0 and is not constrained, so a definition over Re s ≥ 0 would be wrong.
- `DirichletGRH.pole_excluded` (degenerate): For χ = 1 the value of the totalized LFunction at s = 1 is not constrained.
- `dirichletGRH_one_iff_riemannHypothesis` (compatibility): DirichletGRH (1 : DirichletCharacter ℂ 1) ↔ RiemannHypothesis.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/conditional-prime-error-terms: the hypothesis of the conditional error terms for ψ and ψ(x;a,q). PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20/grh-rankin-selberg: the Rankin–Selberg form of the hypothesis is requested from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3; this register fixes the Dirichlet and Riemann instances it must specialize to. RS-07 (drop of AN.6): AN.3 receives the RH/GRH statement register of the dropped layer, reusing the existing RH proposition.

**Checks.** The predicate is used only as a hypothesis: no node of this packet proves it or depends on it unconditionally.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:RiemannHypothesis`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`, `mathlib:riemannZeta`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §7.3, Conjecture 7.8, p. 45; §10.3, Conjecture 10.4 and Remark 10.5, pp. 60–61: Conjecture 7.8 is the Riemann hypothesis for the nontrivial zeros of ζ; Conjecture 10.4 is the same statement for every Dirichlet L-function, and Remark 10.5 warns that a theorem conditional on “GRH” must say which L-functions are included.

### Prime error terms under RH and GRH

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.3/plan/conditional-prime-error-terms` (theorem).

(i) If RiemannHypothesis holds, then for every ε > 0, ψ(x) − x = O_ε(x^{1/2+ε}) as x → ∞. (ii) Fix q ≥ 1. If DirichletGRH χ holds for every character χ modulo q, then for every ε > 0 and every a with gcd(a,q) = 1, ψ(x;a,q) − x/φ(q) = O_{q,ε}(x^{1/2+ε}), where ψ(x;a,q) = Σ_{n≤x, n≡a mod q} Λ(n). The hypotheses are explicit; neither conclusion is used by an unconditional target.

**Hypotheses and scope.** (i): RiemannHypothesis. (ii): DirichletGRH χ for every χ modulo q; gcd(a,q) = 1.

**Proof.**

1. (i) Insert Re ρ = 1/2 into the truncated explicit formula of this layer, bound Σ_{|γ|<T} 1/|ρ| by O(log² T) using the Riemann–von Mangoldt count, and take T = x.
2. (ii) Expand ψ(x;a,q) by orthogonality of characters modulo q into φ(q)^{−1} Σ_χ χ̄(a) ψ(x,χ); the principal character gives ψ(x) up to O(log q · log x), and each nonprincipal χ is handled by the explicit formula for ψ(x,χ) (character-half-interval explicit formula of this layer) with its zeros on Re s = 1/2.

**Checks.** The hypothesis appears in the statement; dropping it leaves only the de la Vallée Poussin error of AN.2. (ii) fixes q: the implied constant may depend on q, and no Bombieri–Vinogradov-type average is claimed (that is SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns:SV.3).

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.3/plan/generalized-riemann-hypothesis`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-generalized-riemann-hypothesis), [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/riemann-von-mangoldt-count`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-riemann-von-mangoldt-count), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula), `mathlib:Chebyshev.psi`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.sum_char_inv_mul_char_eq`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §7.3, equation (7.3.1), p. 46; §10.3, equation (10.3.1), p. 61: Under the Riemann hypothesis the explicit formula gives ψ(x) − x = O(x^{1/2+ε}); under the generalized hypothesis the character explicit formula gives ψ(x,χ) = O(x^{1/2+ε}) and the corresponding prime number theorem in progressions.

## AN.4 — Hecke, Dedekind and Artin analytic interfaces

RS-07 narrows this layer to comparisons between arithmetic series and analytic continuations over number fields, boundary nonvanishing and its prime-ideal applications, and the Artin interface. Tate’s continuation and functional equations come from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1 and the Hecke character carriers from GlobalNumberFields Layer 9; this layer proves that those continuations agree with the ideal series (Dedekind, Hecke, primitive and imprimitive), that Hecke L-functions do not vanish on Re s = 1 (including the quadratic case at s = 1, which current Tau Ceti leaves open), and it builds Artin Euler series with inertia invariants, their Brauer meromorphic continuation and their continuation near Re s ≥ 1, keeping Artin holomorphy as a hypothesis. The paper inputs are quadratic and CM: Tsimerman’s bounded-degree Brauer–Siegel and Colmez-family estimates, Duke–Imamoḡlu–Tóth’s partial ideal zeta functions and Hecke periods, Gross–Zagier’s genus factorization and class-number values, Heilbronn’s theorem on real zeros, Louboutin’s residue bound and Zaman’s effective prime-ideal bound.

**Layer acceptance.** Verify real/complex gamma factors, residue constants and ramified Euler factors against reciprocity/Frobenius conventions.
