<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-l-function-euler-product-comparison"></a>

### Hecke series and Tate integral comparison

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/hecke-L-function-euler-product-comparison` (comparison).

Let K be a number field, c a unitary idele-class character unramified outside a finite set S containing every archimedean place, and χ its ideal-character presentation from GlobalNumberFields Layer9. Choose Tate's admissible factorizable f with f_v=1_{O_v} for v∉S. For Re(s)>1, Z(f,c|·|^s)=(∏_{v∈S}Z_v(f_v,c_v|·|_v^s))(∏_{v∉S}N(d_v)^(−1/2))L_S(s,χ), where L_S(s,χ)=∑_{a integral, prime to S}χ(a)N(a)^(−s)=∏_{v∉S}(1−χ(v)N(v)^(−s))⁻¹. d_v is the local different; its product is finite because d_v is a unit at almost all places. Haar and Fourier normalizations are Tate's, not silently normalized unit volumes.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K a number field; c unitary and trivial on K×; S finite containing infinity and all ramification of c; f admissible in Tate's Z1–Z3 class with the stated local factors; Re(s)>1.

**Proof.**

1. Import the canonical Hecke character and its local/ideal dictionary from GlobalNumberFields Layer9.
2. At v∉S, compute the local integral as the convergent geometric series N(d_v)^(−1/2)∑_{j≥0}χ(v)^j N(v)^(−js).
3. Import the AL.1 global zeta-integral factorization, with the AL.0 measures and Fourier convention, and multiply the local formulas.
4. Use ADS Layer3 to identify the ideal Euler product with the absolutely convergent ideal series. Exact norm regrouping and admissibility hypotheses are required imports, not new carriers here.
5. The completed functional equation is now AN.4/hecke-primitive-functional-equation, stated as an identity of meromorphic functions from AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation; no local factor is cancelled at its zeros.

**Checks.** For K=ℚ and trivial c, the unramified arithmetic series is ζ with exactly the S Euler factors removed. Ramified different factors N(d_v)^(−1/2) are retained. The character is an imported idele-class character, not an arbitrary list of local factors.

**Prerequisites.** `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.0`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/global-zeta-integral`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/completed-hecke-l-function`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-3-local-factors-and-euler-products`.

**Source.** Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (John Tate), §4.5, thesis p.(4.23), scan p.57; comparison and continuation discussion scan pp.58–59: Fresh page-image verification of the displayed Euler comparison. Character construction and full admissibility proofs remain imported, with exact unread boundaries recorded.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-landau-nonnegative-logarithm"></a>

### Hecke boundary adapter for Landau positivity

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/landau-nonnegative-logarithm` (comparison).

For a continued Hecke product F meromorphic near Re s≥1, with no poles except a pole of order at most one at 1, nonnegative norm-regrouped logarithmic coefficients on Re s>1 imply: F has no zeros at regular points of Re s≥1, and its meromorphic order at 1 is ≤0. A pole is not a nonzero finite value.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Coefficients a_n real and nonnegative; the Dirichlet series may be indexed by ideals after regrouping by norm.

**Proof.**

1. Import the generic Landau positivity and 3-4-1 boundary theorem from ADS Layer 8, rather than constructing it again.
2. Check that the Hecke product satisfies the imported pole-order and logarithmic-coefficient hypotheses; the separate ray-class orthogonality lemma supplies the coefficients.
3. At a regular point interpret order zero as nonvanishing; at 1 permit a pole, and use the real positive limit when the singularity is removable.

**Checks.** A simple pole at 1 is allowed; no value F(1) is asserted there. A removable value at 1 is at least 1 in the logarithmic normalization. No new generic Landau theorem is owned here.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-8-landau-type-positivity`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §3.3, Lemma 3.6 and Exercise 3.6.1, printed pp. 19 and 21: Lemma 3.6, whose proof is left as Exercise 3.6.1 (hint: adapt the case f = ζ); the proof steps here are that adaptation.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation"></a>

### Primitive Hecke functional-equation normalization

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation` (comparison).

For a primitive finite-order Hecke character χ with finite conductor f and the imported archimedean parity data, the canonical continued L-function, multiplied by the conductor/discriminant and the real/complex gamma factors in AL.1, satisfies Λ(s,χ)=ε(χ)Λ(1−s,χ̄) as a meromorphic identity. The principal character retains the two completed poles. Imprimitive deleted factors are a separate comparison.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K a number field; 𝔪 a modulus (an integral ideal times a set of real places); χ a character of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(K) (finite order), identified with a finite-order idele-class character ω_χ by GlobalNumberFields Layer 9; L(s, χ) = Σ_{(𝔞,𝔪)=1} χ(𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} for Re s > 1. χ primitive of conductor 𝔣 for the functional equation.

**Proof.**

1. Import AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation on its canonical completed carrier.
2. Use the Re s>1 comparison to identify the finite Euler product, retaining the different and Haar constants.
3. Transport the identity using the identity theorem; do not claim a new Tate functional-equation proof.

**Checks.** For K = ℚ and a primitive Dirichlet character χ of positive conductor N, distinguish the conductor-completed meromorphic function Λ(s,χ)=N^(s/2)·DirichletCharacter.completedLFunction χ s from Mathlib’s completedLFunction, which omits that conductor power. Mathlib states completedLFunction χ (1−s)=N^(s−1/2)·rootNumber χ·completedLFunction χ⁻¹ s. Multiplying by N^((1−s)/2) gives Λ(1−s,χ)=rootNumber χ·Λ(s,χ⁻¹); compare orientations before identifying ε(χ). At poles use meromorphic identities, not a product of totalized point values. Check that an imprimitive character's L-function acquires zeros on Re s = 0 from the removed Euler factors, which is why the functional equation is stated only for the primitive function.

**Prerequisites.** `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/hecke-l-functional-equation`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/completed-hecke-l-function`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/global-epsilon-factor`, [`AN.4/plan/hecke-L-function-euler-product-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-l-function-euler-product-comparison), `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`.

**Source.** Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (John Tate), §4.5, physical pp. 57–59 (read on page images, cc-39fac3): Tate's derivation of Hecke's functional equation for ζ(s, χ).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue"></a>

### Dedekind continuation and real-side comparison

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue` (comparison).

The Dedekind function supplied by the trivial-character Tate continuation agrees with NumberField.dedekindZeta K on Re s>1. Its complex residue at 1 equals NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue K, by agreement with the pinned real one-sided residue limit and uniqueness of a meromorphic residue. This is an agreement theorem on the convergence half-plane, not equality with the totalized LSeries everywhere.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K a number field with r₁ real and r₂ complex places.

**Proof.**

1. Import the trivial-character continuation from AL.1 and use the ideal Euler-product comparison on Re s>1.
2. Multiply the continued function by s−1 and remove the simple singularity.
3. Take its real right-hand limit using the pinned Dedekind residue theorem; uniqueness of the continuous extension identifies the complex residue.

**Checks.** No evaluation of the totalized LSeries at −2 is used. For Q(i), the positive residue expression is π/4. The completed functional equation and trivial zeros are separate declarations.

**Prerequisites.** `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/tate-global-functional-equation`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/global-zeta-integral`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/idele-class-volume`, `mathlib:NumberField.dedekindZeta`, `mathlib:NumberField.dedekindZeta_residue`, `mathlib:NumberField.tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT`, `mathlib:Complex.Gammaℝ`, `mathlib:Complex.Gammaℂ`.

**Source.** Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (John Tate), §4.4 Main Theorem 4.4.1 and §4.5, physical pp. 50–58 (read on page images, cc-39fac3): The residue −κf(0), κf̂(0) and the comparison of ζ(f, c|·|^s) with the classical ζ(s, χ).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one"></a>

### Hecke L-functions do not vanish on Re s = 1

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one` (theorem) · planet: *Nonvanishing of Hecke L-functions*.

For every character χ of Cl_𝔪(K): L(s, χ) ≠ 0 for Re s = 1, s ≠ 1; and L(1, χ) ≠ 0 if χ ≠ 1 (for χ = 1, L(s, 1) has a simple pole at s = 1).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K a number field; 𝔪 a modulus (an integral ideal times a set of real places); χ a character of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(K) (finite order), identified with a finite-order idele-class character ω_χ by GlobalNumberFields Layer 9; L(s, χ) = Σ_{(𝔞,𝔪)=1} χ(𝔞)N𝔞^{−s} for Re s > 1.

**Proof.**

1. Away from1 use the ray-character product and holomorphy of each factor.
2. At1 use the separate nonreal-character cancellation and quadratic Landau contradiction lemmas; the auxiliary zero at1/2 has order at least1, not necessarily exactly1.

**Checks.** Check K = ℚ against Mathlib: DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re. Check the need for a separate argument at s = 1 for real χ: χ = χ̄ gives only one zero against the pole, so the product argument alone does not decide it.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/landau-nonnegative-logarithm`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-landau-nonnegative-logarithm), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-3-local-factors-and-euler-products`, `mathlib:LSeries.positive`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.LFunction_ne_zero_of_one_le_re`, [`AN.4/plan/hecke-L-function-euler-product-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-l-function-euler-product-comparison), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-1-norm-fibres-and-mathlib-lseries`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-8-landau-type-positivity`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.4/ray-class-product-nonvanishing`, `AN.4/ray-character-log-coefficients`, `AN.4/nonreal-hecke-at-one`, `AN.4/quadratic-auxiliary-positive-factors`, `AN.4/quadratic-auxiliary-holomorphy`, `AN.4/quadratic-landau-contradiction`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-local-polynomial"></a>

### Artin local polynomial

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-local-polynomial` (definition).

For a finite Galois extension L/K, a finite-dimensional complex representation ρ of G=Gal(L/K), and a nonzero prime ideal p of K, choose P above p, its decomposition/inertia groups D_P,I_P and arithmetic Frobenius in D_P/I_P. On V^(I_P), Frobenius acts canonically. Define P_p(T)=det(1−T·Frob_P|V^(I_P)) in C[T]. The determinant is independent of P and of a Frobenius lift.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the actual representation of L≃ₐ[K]L, restrict it to the ideal inertia subgroup, and form Representation.invariants. The pinned existence theorem supplies an arithmetic Frobenius lift even at ramified primes. Restrict that lift to invariants; its reversed characteristic polynomial is det(1−T·F).
2. Restrict the existing Representation C G V to I_P and use its invariants submodule; I_P is normal in D_P, so each decomposition-group element preserves that subspace.
3. Any two arithmetic Frobenius lifts differ by inertia by pinned IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia, so their restrictions to V^I agree. Changing P conjugates both I and Frobenius; transport vectors through ρ(g) and apply LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj.
4. For the induced invariant-space automorphism A, define the polynomial as A.charpoly.reverse. Matrix.reverse_charpoly identifies it with det(1−T A) in any basis. Invertibility gives degree exactly dim V^I; finite order forces all eigenvalues and reciprocal polynomial roots onto the unit circle.
5. The carrier uses the prime-relative Frobenius coset, including ramified primes. NFA2 artinSymbol alone is available only at unramified primes and cannot define this full polynomial.

**API.**

- `artin_local_polynomial.independence` (compatibility): Changing P conjugates the invariant-space endomorphism and leaves P_p unchanged.
- `artin_local_polynomial.constant` (simp): P_p(0)=1.
- `artin_local_polynomial.unramified` (compatibility): For unramified p, P_p(T)=det(1−Tρ(Frob_p)) on all of V.
- `artin_local_polynomial.degree` (projection): natDegree P_p=dim_C(V^I)≤dim_C V; the Frobenius endomorphism on V^I has eigenvalues of modulus1 and every root of P_p has modulus1. The degree-zero polynomial1 has no roots.
- `artin_local_polynomial.basis` (extensionality): Changing the finite-dimensional basis does not change the polynomial.

**Unit tests.**

- `artin_local_polynomial.trivial` (computation): For the one-dimensional trivial representation, P_p=1−T at every prime.
- `artin_local_polynomial.zero` (computation): For the zero representation, P_p=1.
- `artin_local_polynomial.ramified_character` (computation): For a one-dimensional character nontrivial on inertia, V^I=0 and P_p=1; using the whole V would give a wrong factor.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy: Reinstate ramified factors before identifying Artin and Hecke products..

**Checks.** For the one-dimensional trivial representation, P_p=1−T at every prime. For the zero representation, P_p=1. For a one-dimensional character nontrivial on inertia, V^I=0 and P_p=1; using the whole V would give a wrong factor.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-2-frobenius-elements-and-the-artin-symbol`, `mathlib:Representation.invariants`, `mathlib:Representation.mem_invariants`, `mathlib:IsArithFrobAt.mul_inv_mem_inertia`, `mathlib:IsArithFrobAt.conj`, `mathlib:LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj`, `mathlib:Matrix.charpolyRev`, `mathlib:Matrix.reverse_charpoly`, `tauceti:NumberField.exists_isArithFrobAt`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §22.2 p.128 ramified-prime paragraph: The printed parenthesis supplies the ramified invariant-space prescription over Q. Extension to all nonzero prime ideals of K uses the precisely named NFA supplier and existing representation/characteristic-polynomial carriers; it is not a fresh original-proof receipt.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-euler-series"></a>

### Artin Euler series

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-euler-series` (definition) · planet: *Artin L-functions*.

For the preceding data and Re s>1, L_K(s,ρ)=∏_p P_p((Np)^−s)^−1, over all nonzero prime ideals of K, with complex powers using the positive real norm logarithm. Coefficients are the norm-regrouped reciprocal local-polynomial coefficients, not a completely multiplicative degree-one ideal weight.

**Construction or proof.**

1. For each prime polynomial P(T) with P(0)=1, recursively determine reciprocal coefficients a_0=1 and a_(n+1)=−Σ_(j=0)^n P_(j+1)a_(n−j). Unique ideal factorization extends these to the canonical multiplicative nonzero-ideal weight. Its normCoeff LSeries is the series compared with the all-prime unordered Euler product.
2. Expand each reciprocal local polynomial as the formal product of m geometric series, where m=dim V^I≤d. Assign these prime-power coefficients multiplicatively to the existing ideal arithmetic-function carrier; do not assert complete multiplicativity.
3. The absolute coefficient sum at a prime is bounded by (1−(Np)^−σ)^−d. Finite ideal-factorization products therefore admit the d-fold Dedekind-series majorant; prove the ideal-indexed absolute convergence in node162 before identifying the norm-regrouped LSeries.
4. Use ADS1 regroupByNorm and ADS3 EulerProductData to compare the single canonical coefficient LSeries and the unordered prime product on Re s>1. The trivial representation recovers the full Dedekind series, including every ramified prime; the zero representation is the constant1.

**API.**

- `artin_euler_series.local` (projection): Every local factor is the reciprocal of the inertia-invariant polynomial.
- `artin_euler_series.series` (compatibility): The absolutely convergent Euler product equals the norm-regrouped coefficient LSeries on Re s>1.
- `artin_euler_series.nonzero` (projection): The convergent Euler product is nonzero on Re s>1.
- `artin_euler_series.direct_sum` (relation): The direct-sum identity is exported by the separate lemma below.
- `artin_euler_series.deleted` (compatibility): Omitting a finite bad-prime set multiplies L_K by exactly ∏_{p bad}P_p((Np)^−s).

**Unit tests.**

- `artin_euler_series.trivial` (computation): The one-dimensional trivial representation gives the convergent Dedekind series, including ramified primes.
- `artin_euler_series.zero` (computation): The zero representation gives1.
- `artin_euler_series.ramified` (computation): A one-dimensional character ramified at p contributes local factor1 there.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy: Apply induction to one canonical Euler product with all local factors..

**Checks.** The one-dimensional trivial representation gives the convergent Dedekind series, including ramified primes. The zero representation gives1. A one-dimensional character ramified at p contributes local factor1 there.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/artin-local-polynomial`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-local-polynomial), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-1-norm-fibres-and-mathlib-lseries`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-3-local-factors-and-euler-products`.

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §22.2 pp.127–128 incomplete Euler product and ramified-factor prescription: The source initially deletes ramified rational primes. The packet deliberately reinstates them and works over K; the resulting full Dedekind test needs those factors and the imported ideal coefficient/product adapters.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy"></a>

### Artin continuation near the line one

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy` (theorem).

Let K/ℚ be finite Galois and ρ a finite-dimensional complex representation of Gal(K/ℚ). The incomplete Artin L-function, with precisely the ramified rational primes omitted, has a meromorphic continuation to an open neighbourhood of {Re(s)≥1}; it is holomorphic and nonzero on Re(s)=1 away from s=1, and its pole order at 1 is dim(V^G). This statement asserts neither global Artin holomorphy nor Chebotarev density.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Finite Galois K/ℚ; finite-dimensional complex representation; arithmetic Frobenius at unramified primes; omitted-prime set fixed.

**Proof.**

1. Import arithmetic Frobenius and conjugacy independence from NumberFieldArithmetic Layer2. AN.4 must supply determinant Euler factors and direct-sum/induction identities.
2. Import finite-group Artin rational induction; after clearing denominators express an m-fold representation as a virtual sum of induced one-dimensional characters.
3. Use ClassFieldTheory Layer 11 and GlobalNumberFields Layer 9 to identify one-dimensional factors with finite-order Hecke characters; their continuation is AN.4/hecke-primitive-functional-equation and their boundary nonvanishing, with the pole at 1 of the trivial character, is AN.4/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one.
4. On small discs about points of the line, take the m-th root agreeing with the Euler product on Re s > 1 and glue (AN.4/mth-root-gluing).
5. Separate the trivial summand to compute the pole order. Brauer integral induction can prove global meromorphy, whereas absence of extra poles is Artin holomorphy; the rational-root route here does not prove the global assertion.

**Checks.** For the trivial representation recover ζ times the omitted local factors and a simple pole at1. For a nontrivial one-dimensional character recover the Hecke near-line result. At ramified primes the complete local factor would act on inertia invariants; an arbitrary Frobenius lift on the whole representation is invalid. No natural-density conclusion is included; that theorem belongs to Chebotarev.

### Explicit residue bound for Dedekind zeta functions (Louboutin)

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/louboutin-dedekind-residue-upper` (theorem).

For every number field K of degree d>1 and absolute discriminant D_K, the residue κ_K of the continued Dedekind zeta function satisfies κ_K≤(e log D_K/(2(d−1)))^(d−1).

**Hypotheses and scope.** K is a number field; d=[K:ℚ]>1; D_K is the positive absolute discriminant; κ_K is the residue of the complex continuation at1, matched to the pinned real residue limit.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the original Louboutin upper bound to the continued Dedekind residue.
2. Keep d>1 and the exact degree-dependent exponent; this upper bound alone does not prove a lower bound.

### Global meromorphic Artin continuation

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation` (theorem) · planet: *Artin meromorphic continuation*.

Every finite-image complex Artin Euler series has a meromorphic continuation to C obtained from an integral Brauer expression as a finite product of integer powers of canonical Hecke continuations. This asserts global meromorphy, not Artin holomorphy.

**Proof.**

1. Request the integral monomial refinement of Brauer induction: χ_ρ=Σ_j n_j Ind_{H_j}^G χ_j with n_j∈Z and χ_j one-dimensional. The current upstream Layer6 only supplies elementary subgroup characters; their further induced-linear decomposition must be proved, not inferred from that wording.
2. Apply node163 and node164 to the character identity on Re s>1, obtaining a finite product of integer powers of canonical meromorphic Hecke continuations. Nonzero right-half-plane values ensure none of the denominator factors is identically zero.
3. Use the identity theorem to identify this meromorphic continuation independently of the chosen integral expression. Negative coefficients may introduce poles away from1, so no Artin holomorphy conclusion follows. Rational coefficients give only a meromorphic power and cannot replace this proof.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Global meromorphic Artin continuation.

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-hecke-cauchy-derivative"></a>

### A fixed small circle gives a subpolynomial derivative

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/quadratic-hecke-cauchy-derivative` (theorem).

Let E be a CM number field, F its maximal totally real subfield, [F:ℚ]=g≥1, and η=η_E/F the canonical nontrivial primitive quadratic Hecke character. Write D_K=|Disc(K)|, f_η for its finite conductor, and Q=D_F N(f_η)=D_E/D_F. For fixed g and every epsilon>0, |L_f prime(1,eta_E/F)| <<_(g,epsilon) D_E^epsilon. Set r=min(epsilon,1/4)>0. The closed circle |s-1|=r is in [-r,1+r] in real part, |t|<=r, and the convexity exponent is at most r. Hence its supremum is at most C_(g,r)*Q^r, and Cauchy gives |L_f prime(1)|<=C_(g,r)*Q^r/r. Holomorphy is required on the entire disk; a zero-free disk is unnecessary.

**Hypotheses and scope.** E/F is the CM quadratic extension specified in the statement; η is defined through global Artin reciprocity, rather than an arbitrary quadratic character. g and ε are fixed before varying E; implied constants depend only on those stated parameters.

**Proof.**

1. Choose r=min(ε,1/4), and apply the finite-order convexity bound on the complete circle |s−1|=r.
2. Use Cauchy on the holomorphic disk, with bound Q^r/r; no zero-free disk is assumed.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: A fixed small circle gives a subpolynomial derivative.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-hecke-log-functional-equation"></a>

### Logarithmic functional equation at zero and one

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/quadratic-hecke-log-functional-equation` (theorem).

Let E be a CM number field, F its maximal totally real subfield, [F:ℚ]=g≥1, and η=η_E/F the canonical nontrivial primitive quadratic Hecke character. Write D_K=|Disc(K)|, f_η for its finite conductor, and Q=D_F N(f_η)=D_E/D_F. For ell_j=L_f prime(j,eta)/L_f(j,eta), both denominators are nonzero and ell_0+ell_1=-log Q+g*(gamma+log(2*pi)), where gamma is Euler constant. Differentiate the completed functional equation; Gamma_R prime/Gamma_R at 1 and 2 sum to -gamma-log(2*pi). Nonvanishing at 0 follows from the functional equation and L_f(1)>0. Each real local component of η is the sign character, so the conductor-normalized completion is Q^(s/2) Γ_R(s+1)^g L_f(s,η), with Γ_R(s)=π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2). This odd archimedean formula is not asserted for a real quadratic extension of a totally real field.

**Hypotheses and scope.** E/F is the CM quadratic extension specified in the statement; η is defined through global Artin reciprocity, rather than an arbitrary quadratic character. g and ε are fixed before varying E; implied constants depend only on those stated parameters.

**Proof.**

1. Import AL.1/cm-quadratic-completion and cm-logarithmic-gamma-correction, rather than re-plan the CM completion. Differentiate the imported functional equation and evaluate at0 and1 after proving both endpoint values nonzero; this node exports the endpoint sum for the finite Hecke factor.
2. Use the gamma logarithmic derivatives at 1 and 2; keep the conductor Q separate from D_E until their arithmetic identification.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Logarithmic functional equation at zero and one.

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit. For E=ℚ(i), F=ℚ, Q=4: L_f(0,η)=1/2 and L_f(1,η)=π/4; the claimed sum becomes γ+log(π/2). Exclude E=ℚ(√2), F=ℚ: its even primitive character χ_8 has L_f(0,χ_8)=0, so the displayed logarithmic quotient at 0 is undefined.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-partial-ideal-zeta"></a>

### Partial ideal zeta series

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/partial-ideal-zeta` (definition) · planet: *Partial ideal zeta functions*.

For a number field K, choose its ordinary or narrow ideal class group, and a class A. Let a_A(n) count nonzero integral ideals of norm n in A, with a_A(0)=0. Define ζ_A(s)=LSeries a_A s on Re s>1, using the imported norm-indexed ideal arithmetic function and finite norm fibres. Quadratic period applications use narrow classes for real quadratic K and ordinary classes for imaginary quadratic K. Index ideals, not their generators. The finite class sum agrees with NumberField.dedekindZeta as an LSeries: the latter may have a different zeroth coefficient, which LSeries ignores.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose the pinned ordinary ClassGroup or NumberField.NarrowClassGroup carrier and its canonical nonzero-ideal monoid homomorphism. Apply normCoeff to the class indicator weight; the zero ideal is absent from the carrier and the zeroth arithmetic coefficient is zero.
2. Use finite norm fibres and the finite class-group sum to regroup coefficients. Class characters are monoid homomorphisms to complex units; their finite order supplies unit norm.
3. For quadratic conjugation, use the ring-of-integers equivalence and the pinned inversion theorem on narrow classes, then the ordinary-class quotient. Norm preservation induces the coefficient bijection. The native general adapter exposes this exact class-inversion hypothesis; the canonical quadratic specialization discharges it.

**API.**

- `partial_ideal_zeta.coeff` (data): a_A(n) is the finite cardinality of integral ideals of positive norm n in A; a_A(0)=0.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.sum_classes` (relation): The sum of ζ_A over all ideal classes is the Dedekind series on Re s>1.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.character_sum` (compatibility): For a class character χ, Σ_A χ(A)ζ_A(s) is its ideal-character LSeries on Re s>1.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.conjugation` (functoriality): For a ring-of-integers automorphism τ whose induced map on the selected class group is inversion, norm preservation gives ζ_A(s)=ζ_(A⁻¹)(s) on Re s>1. The quadratic specialization uses the canonical quadratic conjugation; its narrow-class inversion is already pinned.

**Unit tests.**

- `partial_ideal_zeta.q` (computation): For K=Q, the unique partial series equals the Riemann series on Re s>1.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.unit` (computation): a_A(1)=1 for the principal class and 0 otherwise.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.no_generators` (computation): The unit ideal contributes once, even when the unit group is infinite.
- `partial_ideal_zeta.zero` (computation): The zero ideal contributes to no coefficient; no norm-zero negative power occurs.

**Uses.** PAPER-DUKE-IMAMOGLU-TOTH-16/133: Identify the narrow partial-zeta Hecke periods.. PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/95: Use the same definition with the ordinary class group in the totally complex case..

**Checks.** For K=Q, the unique partial series equals the Riemann series on Re s>1. a_A(1)=1 for the principal class and 0 otherwise. The unit ideal contributes once, even when the unit group is infinite. The zero ideal contributes to no coefficient; no norm-zero negative power occurs. The ℚ test is in the domain of this general coefficient definition; a real/imaginary quadratic restriction applies only to the subsequent period identities. Class-sum coefficient agreement is required for n≥1; do not infer equality of the zeroth coefficients from equality of LSeries.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-cm-partial-zeta-period"></a>

### Hecke CM partial-zeta identity

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/cm-partial-zeta-period` (theorem).

For fundamental D<0, π^(−s)Γ(s)ζ_A(s)=(2^s/ω_D)|D|^(−s/2)E*(z_A,s), initially Re(s)>1 then by continuation. Here K=ℚ(√D), A is an ordinary ideal class, z_A is its associated CM lattice point in the upper half-plane, and ω_D=|O_K^×|/2 (thus ω_−4=2 and ω_−3=3). Here E(z,s)=(1/2)∑_(gcd(c,d)=1) (Im z)^s/|cz+d|^(2s) on Re s>1, and E*(z,s)=π^(−s)Γ(s)ζ(2s)E(z,s).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Identify integral ideals in A with the CM lattice quotient, including the exact unit stabilizer.
2. Match E* and the gamma/discriminant normalization on Re s>1.

### Hecke positive-sign real quadratic formula

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/real-even-partial-zeta-period` (theorem).

For fundamental D>1, π^(−s)Γ(s/2)²D^(s/2)(ζ_A+ζ_{JA})=2∫_{C_A}E*(z,s)ds, initially Re(s)>1 and then by continuation. The proof divides by the full norm-one unit action. ### Genus Hecke factorization

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/genus-lseries-factorization` (theorem).

(p.971.) Let D = d'd ≠ 1 be a fundamental discriminant, with d' and d fundamental discriminants (hence coprime), K = Q(√D), and χ the associated genus character of Cl^+(K). Either factor may be the trivial discriminant 1. For D > 0, χ(J) = sign d = sign d'. Kronecker's decomposition holds: L(s,χ) = L(s,χ_{d'})L(s,χ_d). Equivalently Λ(s,χ) = Λ(s,χ_{d'})Λ(s,χ_d), with Λ(s,χ) as in (7.4)–(7.5) and Λ(s,χ_d) as in (5.13).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Reuse the pinned genus character on the narrow class group and its coprime-ideal evaluation.
2. Compare Euler factors at split, inert and every ramified prime; continue only after the convergent identity.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Genus Hecke factorization.

**Checks.** Check every endpoint and the stated dependence of constants; no conjectural input is implicit. The field discriminant excludes D=1; this does not exclude a factor discriminant equal to1 in a genus decomposition.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-most-quadratic-many-split-primes"></a>

### Many split primes outside a small quadratic exception set

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/most-quadratic-many-split-primes` (theorem).

For ε₁ > 0 and X ≥ 2 there is E = E(k, X, ε₁) ⊂ {F/k quadratic, Disc(F/k) ≤ X} with |E| ≪_{[k:ℚ],ε₁} Disc(k)^{ε₁}X^{ε₁}, such that for F ∉ E and 4 ≤ Y ≤ X, π_k(Y; F, e) ≥ (1/8)π_k(Y/2) − C_{[k:ℚ],ε₁}Y^{σ₁}log²(X Disc(k)) with σ₁ = max(1 − ε₁/(4c), 1/2). E consists of the F whose character χ_{F/k} has a zero with ℜρ > σ₁, |ℑρ| ≤ X^{1/2}; the proof is the explicit formula with Lemma 4.1.

**Hypotheses and scope.** k is a number field of fixed degree n, D_k its absolute discriminant; quadratic F/k have relative discriminant norm≤X; ε₁>0 and X≥2. Take one positive degree-dependent c from the density theorem and σ₁=max(1−ε₁/(4c),1/2). E is fixed before Y ranges over4≤Y≤X, and a single constant C_{n,ε₁} works for all eligible k,F,X,Y. All prime-ideal counts include the norm endpoint.

**Proof.**

1. Use the unique primitive quadratic ray character of conductor the relative discriminant; define E by its nontrivial zeros with σ₁<Reρ<1 and |Imρ|≤√X. The density bound with Q=X,T=√X and an exponent parameter small relative toε₁ gives #E≪_{n,ε₁}D_k^ε₁X^ε₁; bound conjugate infinity types by degree.
2. For F outside E, use the ideal von Mangoldt coefficient and the nonnegative weight (1−N𝔞/Y). Away from ramification, (1+χ(𝔭))/2 is the split-prime indicator. Ramified primes and higher powers require their separate counting estimates.
3. The Hecke logarithmic-derivative series and smoothed Perron give the kernel Y^s/(s(s+1)). Shift at safe heights, accounting for all trivial/nontrivial zeros and double-pole residues at0 and−1; the literal source claim about every vertical line is not used as an integrability lemma.
4. LOW Lemma4.1 supplies the required unit-height zero count and local logarithmic-derivative targets. At T=√X, high zeros contribute O_n(Y log(XD_kT)/T) and low zeros O_{n,ε₁}(Y^σ₁ log(XD_kT)); use Y≤X. Original IK estimates, good-height selection, smoothed contour and residue calculations remain an explicit gap.
5. Use the imported inclusive counting carriers and partial summation to remove higher powers/ramification and the log norm weight, producing the stated1/8 lower bound with one uniform error constant. The exact quantitative adapter, stronger than qualitative PNT transfer, remains a gap.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Lemma 4.3 (most quadratic extensions have many small split primes).

**Checks.** The same set E and one degree/ε₁-dependent constant work simultaneously for every4≤Y≤X; allowing Y-dependent constants would make the target empty. When X<4 there are no eligible Y, but the exceptional-set cardinality assertion is still required. The source weights all prime powers before transferring to split unramified primes; its1/8 main factor cannot be replaced by1/2 without a separate argument.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.3/plan/ray-class-zero-density`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-ray-class-zero-density), [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-zeta-factorization`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-zeta-factorization), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-4-counting-carriers-and-local-finiteness`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-6-abel-and-perron-summation`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-5-ideal-and-prime-estimates`, [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one).

### Lemma 4.4 (Zaman's effective lower bound for prime ideals)

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/effective-prime-ideal-lower` (theorem).

For every fixed degree n there is a positive effective c_n and an absolute effective D₀ such that π_k(Y)≥c_n D_k^(−19)Y/log Y whenever [k:Q]=n, D_k≥D₀ and Y≥D_k^35.

1. Apply the degree-uniform effective Zaman prime-ideal bound with β=35 and γ=19.
2. Retain a discriminant threshold and Y≥D^35.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero"></a>

### Heilbronn's theorem on real zeros of Dedekind zeta functions

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero` (theorem).

If K/Q is finite Galois and the canonical continued ζ_K has a simple real zero β with0<β<1, then a quadratic subfield k⊆K satisfies ζ_k(β)=0. The conclusion uses meromorphic Artin continuation and the Aramata–Brauer entire-quotient theorem, not Artin holomorphy.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Heilbronn Theorem1 first puts the simple real zero in the compositum K₂ of all quadratic subfields. Meromorphic Artin continuation gives integral orders m_χ, possibly negative, for irreducible characters.
2. The Aramata–Brauer theorem says ζ_K/ζ_E is entire for every intermediate E (K/E remains Galois). Thus ζ_E has zero order0 or1 at β. This stronger holomorphy-of-a-quotient input is missing from the existing meromorphic Artin node.
3. Form the virtual character φ=Σ m_χχ. The subgroup averages S(H) are the intermediate zeta orders. If the maximal abelian subfield’s zeta is nonzero, choose a minimal subgroup H* of the commutator subgroup with S(H*)=0; proper subgroups have average1.
4. Möbius inversion over cyclic subgroups forces H* cyclic. Odd-prime cyclic quotients are ruled out by conjugate pairs of nonreal degree-one Hecke factors; hence H* is a nontrivial2-group.
5. Write the real virtual character as φ_+−φ_− with real genuine characters. Every determinant character is trivial on the commutator subgroup, so the multiplicities of eigenvalue−1 on a generator are both even. The subgroup-average difference forces their difference to be1, a contradiction.
6. In the maximal abelian extension, nonreal Hecke factors occur in conjugate pairs and cannot contribute a simple real zero. Over Q, ζ_Q is nonzero on(0,1), so the real factor is a nontrivial quadratic character; its quadratic field zeta vanishes. Original Aramata/Brauer and the finite-character/Möbius proof interfaces still need lemma-level supplier/decomposition.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Heilbronn's theorem on real zeros of Dedekind zeta functions.

**Checks.** K=Q cannot satisfy the premise: ζ_Q has no zero on(0,1). For K quadratic over Q the conclusion is its own field, by ζ_K=ζ_Q L(s,χ_K). An Artin factor may have a pole: nonnegative m_χ are never assumed in the virtual-character argument.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/artin-local-polynomial`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-local-polynomial), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-1-the-splitting-dictionary`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/NumberFieldArithmetic#layer-2-frobenius-elements-and-the-artin-symbol`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-3-the-mackey-decomposition-formula`, [`AN.4/plan/artin-euler-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-euler-series), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-1-norm-fibres-and-mathlib-lseries`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-3-local-factors-and-euler-products`, `mathlib:LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap`, [`AN.4/plan/hecke-L-function-euler-product-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-l-function-euler-product-comparison), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-11-the-global-class-formation-and-global-artin-reciprocity`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-7-the-absolute-local-artin-map-its-normalizations-and-conductors`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-zeta-factorization`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-zeta-factorization).

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.4/artin-direct-sum-factor`, `AN.4/artin-absolute-convergence`, `AN.4/artin-induction-factor`, `AN.4/artin-linear-hecke-comparison`, `AN.4/artin-local-reciprocal-bound`, `AN.4/artin-ramified-induction-polynomial`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** On real zeros of Dedekind ζ-functions (Hans Heilbronn), Theorem1 p.870; complete proof pp.871–873; postscript p.873: The original four-page proof was read. Its Aramata–Brauer entire-quotient and virtual-character parity arguments are explicit prerequisites still missing from the lemma-level packet. On Stevenhagen’s conjecture (Peter Koymans, Carlo Pagano), §8.3 p.92, proof following Theorem8.13: The application needs a quadratic subfield; the original theorem first passes through the quadratic compositum.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-gross-zagier-cm-eisenstein-comparison"></a>

### Eisenstein series at a CM point equals a partial zeta function

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/gross-zagier-cm-eisenstein-comparison` (theorem).

Let D<0 be a fundamental discriminant, K=Q(√D), u=#O_K^×/2 and A an ordinary ideal class. Choose its CM lattice point τ_A in the upper half-plane from a primitive positive-definite binary quadratic form of discriminant D. Let E(z,s)=(1/2)Σ_{gcd(c,d)=1}(Im z)^s/|cz+d|^(2s), the uncompleted level-one Eisenstein series. For Re s>1, E(τ_A,s)=2^(−s)|D|^(s/2)u ζ(2s)^(−1)ζ_K(A,s), equivalently2^s ζ(2s)E(τ_A,s)=u|D|^(s/2)ζ_K(A,s). All positive-base powers use the real logarithm. Changing A to A^(−1) leaves its partial zeta unchanged.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Reuse hecke_cm_partial_zeta_identity: E*=π^(−s)Γ(s)ζ(2s)E and ω_D=u. Substitute these definitions into its completed identity.
2. For Re s>1 cancel the nonzero π^(−s)Γ(s) factor, retaining ζ(2s), the primitive half-sum and exactly u=#units/2. This is the uncompleted normalization comparison of the existing CM identity, not a second CM-period construction.
3. The lattice-to-ordinary-class choice is the same as that of the supplier; inverse-class ambiguity is harmless only after its conjugation/partial-zeta equality is supplied. Nonfundamental order discriminants are outside this field formula.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Eisenstein series at a CM point equals a partial zeta function.

**Checks.** For D=−4, τ=i, u=2 and the single class, ζ_Q(i)(s)=2^s ζ(2s)E(i,s)/(2·4^(s/2))=ζ(2s)E(i,s). For D=−3 the unit factor is u=3, not1. A primitive form with nonfundamental discriminant−16 represents a nonmaximal order in Q(i); it cannot be substituted into this field-discriminant formula.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/cm-partial-zeta-period`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-cm-partial-zeta-period).

**Source.** Heegner points and derivatives of L-series (Benedict H. Gross, Don B. Zagier), ChapterII§4, p.248, immediately after(4.1): Normalization/units and the partial-class sum were checked as an image. Add fundamental-discriminant scope and derive the comparison from the existing DIT-normalized CM node to prevent duplicate construction.

### Imaginary quadratic genus-character classification

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/imaginary-genus-character-dictionary` (theorem).

For an imaginary quadratic field K of fundamental discriminant D<0, genus characters are homomorphisms Cl_K→{±1}, including the trivial homomorphism. They correspond bijectively to unordered fundamental-discriminant factorizations{D₁,D₂}, D=D₁D₂, one positive and one negative; permit the trivial discriminant1 with ε_1=1. For an integral ideal a prime to D, χ_{D₁,D₂}(a)=ε_{D₁}(N a)=ε_{D₂}(N a). This node is the arithmetic classification/compatibility dictionary. The analytic equality L_K(s,χ)=L(s,ε_{D₁})L(s,ε_{D₂}) is supplied by the existing genus_lseries_factorization node, not proved again here.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Use the pinned genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom only with its actual hypotheses: distinct prime-discriminant data with at most one even prime discriminant, total product the fundamentalDiscriminant of the squarefree radicand, a chosen quadratic generator and subset of those prime discriminants.
2. Transport the homomorphism via the pinned toClassGroupEquiv under IsTotallyComplex K; this equivalence itself constructs no imaginary-quadratic instance.
3. Match subset/complement factorizations to the unordered pair{D₁,D₂}; prove the full surjectivity/kernel classification in the existing quadratic arithmetic owner. The two pinned constructions alone do not prove that every quadratic class character is a genus character of this form.
4. Match the prime-to-D ideal evaluation to the Kronecker characters with ε_1=1; invoke the separately owned analytic genus-factorization theorem when an L-series product is required.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Genus characters of Cl_K and the factorization of their L-series.

**Checks.** For D=−4 only{1,−4} occurs and the genus character is trivial. For D=−15 the pairs{1,−15} and{5,−3} give the two genus characters. An ideal of norm2 (prime to15) has value ε_5(2)=ε_−3(2)=−1 in the nontrivial case. The prime-to-D condition is essential: extending a Dirichlet character by0 at ramified primes cannot define a{±1}-valued class character there.

**Prerequisites.** `tauceti:TauCeti.Multiquadratic.genusCharFunNarrowClassGroupHom`, `tauceti:NumberField.NarrowClassGroup.toClassGroupEquiv`.

**Source.** Heegner points and derivatives of L-series (Benedict H. Gross, Don B. Zagier), ChapterIV introduction after(0.3), p.268: Original classification is quoted without proof; literal norm/prime-to-D statement checked on image. Distinguish the arithmetic classification from the already planned analytic product.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one"></a>

### Imaginary quadratic completion and root number

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one` (theorem).

For negative fundamental D, put δ=|D| and let ε_D be the canonical primitive odd Dirichlet character of Q(√D), of conductorδ. On Re s>1, Λ(s,ε_D)=(δ/π)^((s+1)/2)Γ((s+1)/2)L(s,ε_D). Its canonical entire continuation is δ^((s+1)/2)·DirichletCharacter.completedLFunction(ε_D,s). The new quadratic normalization assertion is that the root number is+1 and Λ(1−s,ε_D)=Λ(s,ε_D). Entire continuation of a nontrivial Dirichlet completed function is already in Mathlib; no duplicate continuation construction is planned.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Import the nontrivial-character differentiability of the pinned completedLFunction and its primitive functional equation. The library completion omits the conductor power, so multiply byδ^((s+1)/2) with the real logarithm ofδ>0.
2. Compare ζ_K=ζ_Q L(s,ε_D), first on Re s>1 then as canonical meromorphic functions, to the number-field completed functional equation. Γ_C(s)/Γ_R(s) and the duplication identity give the oddΓ_R(s+1) branch. The canonical odd character/conductor identification is required.
3. Cancel on a nonzero open half-plane to obtain root+1, then use analytic continuation. Do not infer the sign from |rootNumber|=1 or evaluate a totalizedΓ·L product at a cancelled pole. The existing normalization gap records this comparison proof.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Functional equation of L(s, ε) with root number +1 (quoted input).

**Checks.** At D=−4 the conductor is4, the character is odd and Λ(0)=Λ(1)=1; at D=−3 both endpoints are1/√3. Mathlib’s unnormalized completed function alone has the conductor factorδ^(s−1/2) in its functional equation; that factor cancels only after multiplying by the specified conductor power. The completion is its canonical entire continuation. At negative odd integers, a divergent gamma factor times a vanishing L-value must not be assigned the naive product value0.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.differentiable_completedLFunction`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`, [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-zeta-factorization`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-zeta-factorization), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/tate-global-functional-equation`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/archimedean-local-theory`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/unramified-local-theory`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.4/dedekind-completed-functional-equation`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

### Imaginary quadratic class-number value at one

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-lvalue-one` (theorem).

For an imaginary quadratic field of fundamental discriminant D<0, δ=|D|, class number h and w=2u roots of unity, L(1,ε_D)=πh/(u√δ).

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Use the existing quadratic-residue quotient L(1,ε_D)=κ_K/κ_Q, where κ_Q=1 and the continued functions agree with the norm-indexed library series on Re s>1.
2. Read the pinned residue formula2^r₁(2π)^r₂ R_K h_K/(w_K√δ). For imaginary quadratic K, r₁=0,r₂=1,R_K=1,w_K=2u, giving πh/(u√δ).
3. Retain the arithmetic regulator/embedding-count dictionaries and continuation adapter; the library’s one-sided real residue limit alone does not prove all these comparisons.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Analytic class number formula for K: L(1, ε) = πh/(u√δ), L(0, ε) = h/u (implicit input).

**Checks.** D=−4 gives L(1,ε_−4)=π/4 (h=1,u=2). D=−3 gives L(1,ε_−3)=π/(3√3) (h=1,u=3). For h,u>0 this value is positive; confusing roots of unity w with half-units u loses a factor2.

### Imaginary quadratic class-number value at zero

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-lvalue-zero` (theorem).

With the same imaginary quadratic data, the canonical continued primitive Dirichlet function satisfies L(0,ε_D)=h/u.

**Hypotheses and scope.** Parameters, ranges, character normalization and constant dependence are those in the displayed statement.

**Proof.**

1. Use the canonical root-number-one continuation from imaginary_quadratic_root_number_one, not a pointwise product at a gamma pole.
2. At0 and1 the gamma factors are regular; Γ(1/2)=√π andΓ(1)=1 give Λ(0)=√δ L(0) andΛ(1)=(δ/π)L(1).
3. Insert L(1)=πh/(u√δ) from imaginary_quadratic_lvalue_one, obtaining L(0)=h/u. Both gamma values are pinned library declarations.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Analytic class number formula for K: L(1, ε) = πh/(u√δ), L(0, ε) = h/u (implicit input).

**Checks.** D=−4 gives L(0,ε_−4)=1/2; D=−3 gives L(0,ε_−3)=1/3. For D=−15, h=2,u=1, hence L(0,ε_−15)=2. This is for odd characters from negative fundamental discriminants. An even nontrivial quadratic character has a trivial zero at0 and cannot satisfy this formula.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-negative-even-zero"></a>

### Negative even zeros of the continuation

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/dedekind-negative-even-zero` (theorem).

For a number field K and every integer n≥1, the canonical holomorphic Dedekind continuation at −2n has a zero of exact order r₁+r₂, where r₁ and r₂ are its real-place and complex-pair counts. In particular ζ_K^cont(−2n)=0, since r₁+r₂≥1. This evaluates the continuation, not the pinned totalized ideal LSeries.

**Proof.**

1. At 1+2n the ideal series converges to a strictly positive real number: its terms are nonnegative and the unit ideal contributes 1. Gamma factors and the discriminant factor there are finite and nonzero.
2. Reflect via the completed meromorphic functional equation. Each Γ_R and Γ_C factor has a simple pole at −2n, with nonzero residue; the product has order −(r₁+r₂).
3. Add meromorphic orders to get order r₁+r₂ for ζ_K^cont, using r₁+2r₂=[K:Q]≥1. Pinned gamma junk values at the poles cannot substitute for this germ calculation.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Negative even zeros of the continuation.

**Checks.** For Q the order is 1, agreeing with the already implemented negative-even Riemann zeros. For a real quadratic field the order is 2, whereas for an imaginary quadratic field it is 1.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/tate-global-functional-equation`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/archimedean-local-theory`, `AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.1/unramified-local-theory`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.4/dedekind-completed-functional-equation`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (John Tate), §4.5 equation on scan p.58, with §2.5 archimedean factors; derived negative-even specialization: Order calculation from the reflected nonzero right-side value; exact zero multiplicity is a derived comparison, not a printed Tate theorem.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imprimitive-hecke-factors"></a>

### Imprimitive Hecke deleted factors

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/imprimitive-hecke-factors` (theorem).

Let χ be the ray ideal character modulo a modulus m induced from a primitive finite-order Hecke character χ₀ of conductor f₀ dividing m. If m_fin is the finite part, then L_m^cont(s,χ)=L^cont(s,χ₀)∏_{p|m_fin, p∤f₀_fin}(1−χ₀(p)exp(−s log Np)). Each prime occurs once even if its exponent in m grows; real-place conditions enter the conductor dictionary but do not delete finite Euler factors. Equality is meromorphic.

**Proof.**

1. Import the GlobalNumberFields ray-character/conductor dictionary and the primitive half-plane Hecke Euler-product comparison.
2. In the absolutely convergent half-plane Re s>1, remove exactly the Euler factors for finite primes dividing m but not f₀. Finite multiplicative regrouping retains one factor per prime.
3. Apply uniqueness of meromorphic continuation, keeping the possible trivial-character pole at 1 and removable zeros of the finite correction.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4: Imprimitive Hecke deleted factors.

**Checks.** For K=Q and primitive trivial character, agree with Mathlib’s principal-character finite Euler correction. Changing a finite modulus p to p² deletes the same single factor; an added real place creates no new finite prime factor.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, [`AN.4/plan/hecke-L-function-euler-product-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-l-function-euler-product-comparison).

**Source.** Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions (John Tate), §4.5, scan p.57, Euler product over finite primes outside S: The displayed product is restricted to primes outside S. Reinstating the primitive factors and deleting the additional modulus primes yields this finite comparison.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-holomorphy-hypothesis"></a>

### Artin holomorphy as a hypothesis

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/artin-holomorphy-hypothesis` (definition).

For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields and a finite-dimensional complex representation ρ of Gal(L/K), ArtinHolomorphy ρ is the proposition: the meromorphic continuation of the Artin Euler series L_K(s,ρ) of this layer (Brauer continuation) has no poles in ℂ ∖ {1}, and its order at s = 1 is minus the multiplicity of the trivial representation in ρ. The Artin conjecture is the proposition that ArtinHolomorphy ρ holds for every such ρ. Both are used only as hypotheses.

**Hypotheses and scope.** L/K finite Galois; ρ : Gal(L/K) → GL_n(ℂ) a representation.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition, on the continuation supplied by the Brauer meromorphic-continuation target; the continuation is unique, so the predicate does not depend on the Brauer expression chosen.
2. The Euler series here keeps the inertia-invariant factors at ramified primes. Deleting finitely many Euler factors multiplies by entire functions, so holomorphy of the complete series implies holomorphy of the incomplete one, but not conversely.

**API.**

- `ArtinHolomorphy` (data): The proposition defined above.
- `ArtinConjecture` (data): ArtinHolomorphy ρ for all L/K and all ρ.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.add` (relation): ArtinHolomorphy ρ₁ and ArtinHolomorphy ρ₂ imply ArtinHolomorphy (ρ₁ ⊕ ρ₂), since the Euler series multiply and the multiplicities of the trivial representation add.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.of_dim_one` (relation): A one-dimensional ρ satisfies ArtinHolomorphy, because its Euler series is a Hecke L-function (class field theory) with continuation from AL.1.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.induced` (functoriality): ArtinHolomorphy is invariant under induction: L_K(s, Ind_{L/M}^{L/K} σ) = L_M(s,σ), so ρ induced from a one-dimensional character satisfies it.

**Unit tests.**

- `ArtinHolomorphy.trivial` (computation): For the trivial representation of Gal(L/K), the Euler series is ζ_K, which has a simple pole at 1, matching multiplicity one; ArtinHolomorphy holds.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.regular` (compatibility): For the regular representation, L_K(s,ρ) = ζ_L(s), with a simple pole at 1, and the trivial representation occurs once.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.not_meromorphy` (non-example): Brauer meromorphy alone does not give ArtinHolomorphy: a virtual combination with negative coefficients may have poles, so the predicate is not a consequence of the continuation target.
- `ArtinHolomorphy.incomplete_converse` (non-example): For the incomplete series with a ramified factor deleted, holomorphy away from 1 does not imply holomorphy of the complete series, whose extra local factor can have poles on Re s = 0.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero: Heilbronn’s theorem is proved without Artin holomorphy; the predicate marks the boundary. RS-07 (drop of AN.6): conditional general continuation statements attach to AN.4 as visible hypotheses.

**Checks.** No unconditional target of this packet uses the predicate; it records the RS-07 obligation that general continuation statements stay visible hypotheses.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/artin-euler-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-euler-series), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation).

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §22.2–22.3, Conjecture 22.2, p. 128: Conjecture 22.2 asks that the Artin L-function extend meromorphically to ℂ with no poles away from s = 1 and with pole order at 1 equal to the multiplicity of the trivial representation; the list after it records the cases known (one-dimensional, induced from one-dimensional, solvable two-dimensional).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-extended-riemann-hypothesis"></a>

### Extended Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind and Hecke L-functions

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/extended-riemann-hypothesis` (definition).

For a number field K, DedekindERH K is the proposition: every zero s of the continued Dedekind zeta function ζ_K (the Tate continuation identified with NumberField.dedekindZeta on Re s > 1 by this layer) with 0 < Re s < 1 has Re s = 1/2. For a primitive finite-order Hecke character χ of K, HeckeGRH χ is the same proposition for the continued L(s,χ). Both are hypotheses only; they extend the AN.3 register from Dirichlet characters to number fields.

**Hypotheses and scope.** K a number field; χ a primitive finite-order Hecke character of K.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Definition on the continued functions of this layer. The strip condition removes the trivial zeros (Re s ≤ 0) and the pole at 1; zeros with Re s ≥ 1 are excluded by line-one nonvanishing.

**API.**

- `DedekindERH` (data): The proposition defined above.
- `HeckeGRH` (data): The proposition for one primitive Hecke character.
- `dedekindERH_rat_iff` (compatibility): DedekindERH ℚ is equivalent to RiemannHypothesis, since ζ_ℚ = ζ.
- `DedekindERH.of_abelian` (relation): For K/ℚ abelian, ζ_K is the product of the Dirichlet L-functions of the primitive characters of its conductor, so GRH for those characters implies DedekindERH K.
- `HeckeGRH.trivial` (compatibility): HeckeGRH of the trivial character of K is DedekindERH K.

**Unit tests.**

- `dedekindERH_rat_iff` (compatibility): DedekindERH ℚ ↔ RiemannHypothesis.
- `DedekindERH.gaussian` (computation): For K = ℚ(i), ζ_K = ζ · L(·,χ₋₄), so DedekindERH ℚ(i) is equivalent to RiemannHypothesis together with DirichletGRH χ₋₄.
- `DedekindERH.trivial_zero_excluded` (non-example): For a real quadratic K, ζ_K vanishes at s = 0 to order 1 (r₁ + r₂ − 1 = 1); this zero is outside the strip and does not contradict the predicate.

**Uses.** PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO and PAPER-LEMKEOLIVER-WANG-WOOD-25 (conditional remarks): conditional strengthenings of the effective prime-ideal and Chebotarev inputs name this hypothesis. RS-07 (drop of AN.6): conditional general statements attach to AN.4 as visible hypotheses.

**Checks.** No unconditional target uses it; effective Chebotarev bounds under ERH are not claimed here.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.3/plan/generalized-riemann-hypothesis`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-generalized-riemann-hypothesis), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one).

**Source.** Notes on analytic number theory (Kiran S. Kedlaya), §10.3, Remark 10.5, p. 61: Remark 10.5 records that statements conditional on a generalized Riemann hypothesis often require it for L-functions beyond the Dirichlet ones, and that the family must be specified.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-hecke-zero-free-region"></a>

### Zero-free regions for Dedekind zeta and Hecke L-functions

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/dedekind-hecke-zero-free-region` (theorem) · planet: *Zero-free region for Hecke L-functions*.

(i) Let L/K be an abelian extension of number fields, Q = Q(L/K) the maximum of the norms of the conductors of the Hecke characters χ of K attached to L/K, n_K = [K:ℚ] and D_K = |disc(K/ℚ)|. If D_K Q n_K^{n_K} is sufficiently large, the product Π_χ L(s,χ,K) of these continued Hecke L-functions has at most one zero, counted with multiplicity, in σ ≥ 1 − 0.0875/log(D_K Q n_K^{n_K}), |t| ≤ 1 (s = σ + it); if it exists it is a simple real zero and its character is real. (ii) In particular, if D_K n_K^{n_K} is sufficiently large, ζ_K has at most one zero in σ ≥ 1 − 0.0875/log(D_K n_K^{n_K}), |t| ≤ 1, and such a zero is real. The possible zero is the exceptional zero β₁ of the effective Chebotarev theorem.

**Hypotheses and scope.** L/K abelian; “sufficiently large” is an absolute threshold. The L-functions are the continuations identified with the ideal series in this layer.

**Proof.**

1. Zaman, Theorem 4.1.1: for a congruence class group H of K and r ≥ 1, the product over characters of order at least r has at most one zero in σ ≥ 1 − c₀/(log D_K + (3/4) log Q + n_K ν(n_K)), |t| ≤ T⋆, with c₀ = 0.0875 for r = 1; the zero is real with a real character. Class field theory identifies the characters attached to L/K with those of a congruence class group.
2. The proof is a positivity argument (a nonnegative trigonometric polynomial applied to the logarithmic derivative of the product, as in the 3-4-1 inequality) combined with the Hadamard product of each completed Hecke L-function and explicit bounds for its gamma factors.
3. For (ii), apply (i) to the trivial extension L = K, where the product is ζ_K and Q = 1.

**Checks.** K = ℚ, L = ℚ(ζ_q): (i) is the classical statement that Π_{χ mod q} L(s,χ) has at most one zero near 1, a simple real zero of a real character (compare the conductor-uniform Dirichlet region of AN.2). The region contains at most one zero; it is not claimed zero-free, so no unconditional statement may drop β₁.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/hecke-primitive-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-primitive-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), [`AN.4/plan/imprimitive-hecke-factors`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imprimitive-hecke-factors), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one), [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-11-the-global-class-formation-and-global-artin-reciprocity`.

**Source.** Analytic estimates for the Chebotarev Density Theorem and their applications (Asif Ali Zaman), §1.3.2, Theorem 1.3.5 and Corollary 1.3.6, p. 16; §4.1, Theorem 4.1.1, p. 69: Theorem 1.3.5 bounds the zeros of the product of Hecke L-functions of an abelian extension near 1 by one exceptional real simple zero with an explicit constant 0.0875; Corollary 1.3.6 is the Dedekind case; Theorem 4.1.1 is the version for characters of a congruence class group with constants depending on the order of the characters.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-effective-chebotarev"></a>

### Effective Chebotarev density theorem

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/effective-chebotarev` (theorem) · planet: *Effective Chebotarev theorem*.

Let L/F be a finite Galois extension of number fields with group G, n_L = [L:ℚ], D_L = |disc(L/ℚ)|, C a conjugacy class of G, and π_C(x, L/F) the number of primes p of F unramified in L with Frobenius class C and N p ≤ x (the Tau Ceti carrier frobeniusPrimeCount). (i) Unconditionally (Lagarias–Odlyzko) there is an absolute c > 0 with π_C(x, L/F) = (|C|/|G|) Li(x) + O(x exp(−c (log x / n_L)^{1/2})) for x ≥ exp(10 n_L (log D_L)²); the implied constant is ineffective because of a possible exceptional zero of ζ_L, and it becomes effective and absolute after Stark’s bound for that zero is used and the range of x is enlarged. (ii) If DedekindERH L holds, the error term is O(x^{1/2} log(D_L x^{n_L})) for x ≫ (log D_L)². (iii) There is an absolute, effectively computable B₁ > 0 such that some prime p of F of degree one, unramified in L, with Frobenius class C has N p ≪ D_L^{B₁} (Lagarias–Montgomery–Odlyzko); if DedekindERH L holds, N p ≪ (log D_L)² (Lagarias–Odlyzko).

**Hypotheses and scope.** L/F finite Galois; C a conjugacy class of Gal(L/F). (ii) and the conditional part of (iii) assume DedekindERH L. Ineffective and effective constants are distinguished in (i).

**Proof.**

1. Deuring reduction: for g ∈ C, H = ⟨g⟩ and E = L^H, the primes of F with class C correspond, up to the contraction and the ramified and higher-degree primes already estimated in Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layers 8 and 11–12, to the degree-one primes of E with Frobenius g in the abelian extension L/E.
2. Write the weighted count of the abelian problem as an average of −L′/L(s,χ,E) over the Hecke characters χ of Gal(L/E) (class field theory), apply the truncated Perron formula (ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layer 6) and shift the contour; the zeros are those of ζ_L = Π_χ L(s,χ,E).
3. Bound the sum over zeros with the zero-free region of this layer (keeping the possible exceptional zero β₁ apart) and a zero count N(T) ≪ T log(D_L T^{n_L}); choose T in terms of x and n_L to obtain (i), and insert Re ρ = 1/2 for (ii).
4. (iii) needs, besides the zero-free region, a zero-density estimate near 1 and the Deuring–Heilbronn repulsion of zeros from β₁ (Lagarias–Montgomery–Odlyzko, by power sums); this is the recorded gap of this target.

**Checks.** F = ℚ, L = ℚ(ζ_q): (i) is a prime number theorem in progressions with error x exp(−c (log x/φ(q))^{1/2}) for x ≥ exp(10 φ(q) (log D_L)²), much weaker in q than Siegel–Walfisz, as Zaman notes after (1.18). Dropping the error terms recovers Tau Ceti’s tendsto_frobeniusPrimeCount; no qualitative statement is restated. The exceptional zero is named, never assumed absent.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-hecke-zero-free-region`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-hecke-zero-free-region), [`AN.4/plan/extended-riemann-hypothesis`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-extended-riemann-hypothesis), [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-8-the-cyclic-fixed-field-fibre`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-11-the-frobenius-von-mangoldt-coefficient-and-its-summatory-functions`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev#layer-13-ϑ_c-and-π_c`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-9-hecke-and-ray-class-characters`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-11-the-global-class-formation-and-global-artin-reciprocity`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries#layer-6-abel-and-perron-summation`.

**Source.** Analytic estimates for the Chebotarev Density Theorem and their applications (Asif Ali Zaman), §1.2, equations (1.18), (1.20), (1.21), pp. 7–8: Equation (1.18) records Lagarias–Odlyzko’s field-uniform error term and its range, with the remark that its constants are ineffective and become effective through Stark’s results; the GRH form of the error and (1.20) give the conditional statements; (1.21) records the Lagarias–Montgomery–Odlyzko bound D_L^{B₁} for the least prime with given Frobenius class.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-gauss-sum-sign"></a>

### Sign of the quadratic Gauss sum from the Dedekind functional equation

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4/plan/quadratic-gauss-sum-sign` (theorem).

Let D ≠ 1 be a fundamental discriminant, δ = |D|, ε_D the primitive quadratic Dirichlet character of conductor δ attached to ℚ(√D), and κ(D) = 1 if D > 0, κ(D) = i if D < 0. Then (i) DirichletCharacter.rootNumber ε_D = 1; equivalently (ii) the Gauss sum Σ_{n mod δ} ε_D(n) e(n/δ) equals κ(D) δ^{1/2}, and for every integer r, Σ_{n mod δ} ε_D(n) e(rn/δ) = ε_D(r) κ(D) δ^{1/2} (zero when gcd(r,δ) > 1); (iii) if D is odd and gcd(R,δ) = 1, then Σ_{n mod δ} e(Rn²/δ) = κ(D) δ^{1/2} ε_D(R).

**Hypotheses and scope.** D a fundamental discriminant, D ≠ 1; in (iii) D odd (so δ is squarefree) and gcd(R, δ) = 1.

**Proof.**

1. K = ℚ(√D): ζ_K(s) = ζ(s) L(s, ε_D) on Re s > 1 (quadratic zeta factorization of this layer), and both sides continue meromorphically.
2. The completed Dedekind function of K is invariant under s ↦ 1 − s with root number 1 (Dedekind continuation of this layer, from AL.1), and so is the completed Riemann zeta function (Mathlib completedRiemannZeta_one_sub). Their quotient is the completed L-function of ε_D with gamma factor Γ_ℝ(s + a), a = 0 or 1 by parity, so it is invariant as well; comparing with Mathlib’s functional equation IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub, whose factor is rootNumber ε_D (ε_D⁻¹ = ε_D), and using that the completed function is not identically zero, gives rootNumber ε_D = 1. The imaginary case is the root-number target of this layer.
3. By Mathlib’s definition rootNumber χ = gaussSum χ / I^a / N^{1/2}, (i) is the first statement of (ii); the shifted sums follow from gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive, which holds for every residue, unit or not.
4. (iii) For squarefree odd δ, the number of square roots of m modulo δ is Π_{p|δ}(1 + (m/p)); expanding over the divisors of δ, only the full product survives, and it gives the shifted Gauss sum of ε_D at R.

**Checks.** D = −4: Σ_{n mod 4} ε_{−4}(n) e(n/4) = i − (−i) = 2i = κ(−4)·4^{1/2}. D = 5: the Gauss sum is √5 (positive), not −√5. D = −3, R = 1: Σ_{n mod 3} e(n²/3) = 1 + 2e(1/3) = i√3. The sign is the content: Tau Ceti and Mathlib give only the square of the Gauss sum or its modulus.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-zeta-factorization`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-zeta-factorization), [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-zeta-continuation-and-residue), [`AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one), `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.rootNumber`, `mathlib:DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive.completedLFunction_one_sub`, `mathlib:gaussSum_mulShift_of_isPrimitive`, `mathlib:completedRiemannZeta_one_sub`.

**Source.** Heegner points and derivatives of L-series (Benedict H. Gross, Don B. Zagier), Chapter IV, §2, proof of (2.3), p. 275; §3, proof of (3.2), p. 278: Gross–Zagier use the evaluation Σ_{n mod δ₂} e(Rn²/δ₂) = κ(D₂)δ₂^{1/2}ε_{D₂}(R) and the shifted Gauss sum of ε_{D₂}, quoting the usual evaluation of Gauss sums with Gauss’s sign. Reviewed extraction: Heegner points and derivatives of L-series (Atlas extraction and independent review; original authors: Benedict H. Gross, Don B. Zagier), items PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86/196 and /197 and the review REV-PAPER-GROSS-ZAGIER-86: The reviewed extraction routes the sign to AN.4 and records the analytic route: root number +1 for ε_D from ζ_K = ζ·L(s,ε_D) and the two functional equations.

## AN.5 — Multiplicative functions and value distribution

This layer is kept whole by RS-07. Its multiplicative-function theory starts from the pretentious distance and Halász’s mean-value theorem, with uniformity in the function made explicit. Smooth numbers are counted by Ψ(x,y) and compared with the Dickman function; divisor problems run from the hyperbola method to the uniform subpower bound τ(n) ≤ C n^ε and its explicit constants; Landau and Selberg–Delange counts serve Ghosh–Sarnak and Koymans–Pagano; the Möbius and Mangoldt sums of Skorobogatov–Sofos are stated with their truncations. The second and fourth moments of ζ on the critical line are theorems, and the moment conjecture for higher moments is a model with its arithmetic and random-matrix factors, never a theorem. Beurling generalized primes are an indexed system with explicit axioms, kept separate from the ordinary primes.

**Layer acceptance.** Uniformity in function, height and conductor is explicit; averaging weights and exceptional sets cannot be suppressed.

### Explicit divisor subpower bound

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.5/plan/explicit-divisor-subpower-bound` (theorem).

For ε>0 and any natural B≥exp(1/ε), all positive integers n satisfy τ(n)≤max(1,(ε log 2)⁻¹)^B n^ε. Thus the displayed constant is at least 1 and independent of n.

**Hypotheses and scope.** ε>0; B natural with exp(1/ε)≤B; n>0

**Proof.**

1. Set D=max(1,(ε log 2)⁻¹). Apply the local uniform bound to each prime p≤B.
2. For p>B, the assumed cutoff implies exp(1/ε)≤p; apply the large-prime bound.
3. Apply divisor-bound-from-local-bounds. A certified upper integer B is a permitted input: no exact ceiling evaluation is required.

**Uses.** Bennett–Siksek item96; ExponentialSumsAndCircleMethod:ES.0/small-conductor-power-saving: Separate the uniform constant from the eventual size threshold; no squarefree or conductor condition is required..

**Checks.** n=1 is covered. B may be increased without invalidating the estimate. The constant depends only on ε and the chosen certified B, never on n.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:Real.log_pos`, `mathlib:Real.log_le_log`, `mathlib:Real.add_one_le_exp`, `mathlib:Real.rpow_def_of_pos`, `mathlib:Real.le_log_iff_exp_le`, `mathlib:Nat.card_divisors`, `mathlib:Nat.prod_primeFactors_pow_factorization`, `mathlib:Nat.prime_of_mem_primeFactors`, `mathlib:Finset.prod_le_prod`, `mathlib:Real.mul_rpow`, `mathlib:Real.rpow_mul`, `mathlib:Real.rpow_natCast`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.5/prime-power-log-bound`, `AN.5/large-prime-power-bound`, `AN.5/divisor-bound-from-local-bounds`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** The divisor bound (Terence Tao), Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split: Worker refinement of the proof architecture using the cited pinned prime-factorization and real exponential APIs.
