**Source.** Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem (Sergey Neshveyev), Proposition and complete proof, pp.2–3: Ergodicity of positive rationals on finite adeles; the statement fixes the source conventions and the proof leaves below.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-scaling-measure-space"></a>

### All normalized scaling measures

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-scaling-measure-space` (definition).

A β-scaling measure is a positive Radon measure μ on A_f with μ(Ẑ)=1 and μ(qE)=q^(−β)μ(E) for every positive rational q and Borel set E. These two conditions force μ({0})=0. No unit invariance is assumed; the canonical product measure is one element.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. State Radon regularity, normalization and the rational scaling law on the existing finite-adele carrier. Apply the law to the fixed singleton zero with a rational q different from 1; its finite mass must vanish.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.normalized` (projection): The integral-adeles mass equals 1.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.scale` (relation): Every positive rational dilation scales mass by q^(−β).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.zero_atom` (simp): The singleton 0 has zero mass.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.convex` (structure): Convex mixtures at fixed β stay in the space.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.test_zero_measure` (non-example): The zero measure is not normalized.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.test_dirac_zero` (non-example): The atom at 0 is normalized but violates scaling for q=2 and β>0.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.IsScalingMeasure.test_canonical` (compatibility): The product-density measure satisfies the normalized scaling predicate.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence: Is exactly the measure side of the correspondence..

**Checks.** Check the specified domain and normalization before using this result.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/bc-adelic-scaling-measure`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-adelic-scaling-measure).

**Source.** Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem (Sergey Neshveyev), Neshveyev 2000 (1β), p.1: A β-scaling measure is a positive Radon measure μ on A_f with μ(Ẑ)=1 and μ(qE)=q^(−β)μ(E) for every positive rational q and Borel set E. These two conditions force μ({0})=0. No unit invariance is assumed; the canonical product measure is one element.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence"></a>

### KMS states and scaling measures

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence` (comparison).

For β>0 the maps μ↦φμ and φ↦μφ are inverse affine bijections between all normalized β-scaling Radon measures on A_f and completed KMSβ states. Restriction to Ẑ identifies the measure topology with weak convergence of its probability measures; under this topology the bijection is a homeomorphism.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Expectation determines φ on rational terms; its diagonal restriction determines the normalized measure.
2. Compare both compositions on C(Ẑ), then use scaling and density to obtain equality everywhere.
3. Cylinder characters determine weak convergence on compact Ẑ; finite rational terms determine weak state convergence.

**Checks.** Restriction to C(Ẑ) identifies completed KMSβ states with normalized measures on the finite adeles satisfying rational scaling. Off-diagonal dilation components vanish by invariance, and the KMS relation gives μ(nẐ)=n^(−β).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-low-temperature-uniqueness"></a>

### Critical-regime KMS uniqueness

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-low-temperature-uniqueness` (theorem).

For 0<β≤1 every normalized β-scaling measure equals the canonical μβ, and therefore there is exactly one completed KMSβ state. The proof uses the explicit canonical extremality and compact-unit average rigidity, rather than assuming a general Choquet decomposition.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Average an arbitrary normalized scaling measure over the compact unit group; the cylinder calculation identifies its average with the canonical measure (bc-unit-average).
2. The canonical measure is extreme by ergodicity and the Radon–Nikodym argument (bc-canonical-extreme). Apply bc-extreme-average-rigidity to the average: an extreme barycentre forces the continuous orbit of the original measure to be constant.
3. Use the affine KMS/scaling correspondence to transfer measure uniqueness to completed KMS-state uniqueness. The local Fourier-value computation is a separate consequence, not a Choquet premise.

**Checks.** For0<β≤1 the completed Bost–Connes system has a unique KMSβ state. On e(a/b), with gcd(a,b)=1, its value is b^(−β)∏p|b(1−p^(β−1))/(1−p^(−1)).

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity), [`AN.9/plan/bc-scaling-measure-space`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-scaling-measure-space), [`AN.9/plan/bc-adelic-scaling-measure`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-adelic-scaling-measure), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence).

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.9/bc-canonical-extreme`, `AN.9/bc-unit-average`, `AN.9/bc-extreme-average-rigidity`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem (Sergey Neshveyev), Corollary and proof, p.3 (p.4 contains references): Uniqueness in the critical inverse-temperature interval; the statement fixes the source conventions and the proof leaves below.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-completed-barycentre"></a>

### Gibbs barycentre of a probability measure

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-completed-barycentre` (construction).

For β>1 and a Borel probability ν on W=zHat×, define φν(a)=integral_W φβ,u(a)dν(u). The character parameter W≃AddAut(Q/Z) is continuous on every torsion evaluation. The resulting map is a positive norm-one continuous functional and a KMSβ state. It is affine in ν; bijectivity and weak topological continuity are separate results.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Integrate the completed Gibbs evaluations over the probability parameter. Their uniform norm-one bound gives an integrable bounded linear functional. Positivity and normalization pass under integration, and the completed KMS strip identity passes by dominated convergence.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_apply` (characterisation): Evaluation is the stated Bochner integral.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_norm` (characterisation): The functional has norm 1.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_isKMS` (compatibility): Every probability barycentre is KMSβ.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_test_dirac` (computation): A Dirac mass at u recovers the completed Gibbs state u.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_test_projection` (computation): For every ν, φν(μ2 μ2*)=2^(−β).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.completedBarycentre_test_affine` (compatibility): A convex combination of probabilities gives the same convex combination of functionals.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres: Uses this construction with its stated normalization and domain..

**Checks.** Check the specified domain and normalization before using this result.

The character parameter W≃AddAut(Q/Z) is continuous on every torsion evaluation. The resulting map is a positive norm-one continuous functional and a KMSβ state. It is affine in ν; bijectivity and weak topological continuity are separate results.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres"></a>

### High-β extremal states and unique barycentres

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres` (theorem).

For β>1 every completed KMSβ state has a unique barycentre ν on W, characterized by φ(a)=∫W φβ,u(a)dν(u) for each a∈C_Q. Thus the high-beta KMS set is a Bauer simplex with extreme boundary homeomorphic to W. This specialized uniqueness follows from the measure bijection; it does not require an unproved general Choquet decomposition.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Use the KMS–scaling-measure affine correspondence.
2. Identify Dirac masses with the explicit Gibbs formula.
3. Use the probability-measure extreme-point theorem and transport unit multiplication.

**Checks.** Forβ>1 the KMS simplex is affinely identified with probability measures onẐ×; its extreme points are the Dirac-unit Gibbs states. The unit symmetries act freely transitively on those extreme points.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-orbits`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-measure`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-affine-homeomorphism`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-extremes`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives (Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli), Chapter 3, Theorem 3.32, pp.474–475; Proposition 3.8, pp.447–448 supplies the general Choquet statement: High-β extremal states and unique barycentres; the statement fixes the source conventions and the proof leaves below.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-symmetry-action"></a>

### The symmetry group Ẑ^× = Aut(ℚ/ℤ)

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/symmetry-action` (construction).

For v ∈ Aut(ℚ/ℤ) (≅ Ẑ^×) there is a unique K-algebra automorphism θ_v of BCHecke K with θ_v(x_n) = x_n, θ_v(x′_n) = x′_n and θ_v(e(γ)) = e(v(γ)); on the basis, θ_v[class of [1 γ/m; 0 n/m]] = [class of [1 v(γ)/m; 0 n/m]]. It commutes with the time evolution, θ_vθ_w = θ_{vw}, and for K = ℂ it is a *-automorphism with π_u ∘ θ_v = π_{uv}, so φ_{β,u} ∘ θ_v = φ_{β,uv}.

**Hypotheses and scope.** v ∈ Aut(ℚ/ℤ).

**Construction or proof.**

1. The relations (a′)–(f′) are preserved: v is additive and commutes with multiplication by n on ℚ/ℤ, and permutes {δ : nδ = γ} onto {δ : nδ = v(γ)}. By the presentation (B.9/rational-presentation), θ_v is a well-defined algebra endomorphism with inverse θ_{v⁻¹}.
2. θ_v fixes a(X), so it commutes with σ_z; it preserves the involution because v(−γ) = −v(γ).
3. π_u(θ_v(e(γ)))ε_k = exp(2πik·u(v(γ)))ε_k.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry` (constructor): symmetry (v : AddAut (ℚ/ℤ)) : BCHecke K ≃ₐ[K] BCHecke K (AddAut is the additive twin of MulAut).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_e` (simp): symmetry v (e γ) = e (v γ).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_x` (simp): symmetry v (x n) = x n and symmetry v (x' n) = x' n.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_mul` (relation): symmetry (v * w) = (symmetry w).trans (symmetry v).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_timeEvolution` (compatibility): symmetry v (timeEvolution z f) = timeEvolution z (symmetry v f).

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_neg_e` (computation): symmetry (−1) (e γ) = e (−γ).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_one` (degenerate): symmetry 1 = AlgEquiv.refl.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.symmetry_gibbs` (compatibility): gibbsState β hβ u ∘ symmetry v = gibbsState β hβ (u * v).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.no_symmetry_of_double` (non-example): Doubling on ℚ/ℤ is not bijective, and e γ ↦ e (2γ), x n ↦ x n is not an algebra map: it would send x 2 * x' 2 = 1 + e (1/2) both to itself and to 1 + e 1 = 2.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/kms-classification: Acts freely and transitively on the low-temperature extremal states.. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/galois-action-on-ground-states: Intertwines the Galois action on ground-state values..

**Checks.** Only v = ±1 comes from conjugating the pair (by [1 0; 0 ±1]); a general v ∈ Ẑ^× is not rational, so θ_v is defined through the presentation, not by transport of structure.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/rational-presentation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-rational-presentation), [`AN.9/plan/time-evolution`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-time-evolution), [`AN.9/plan/regular-representation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-regular-representation), `mathlib:AddCircle`, `mathlib:MulAut`.

**Source.** Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives (Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli), Ch. 3, §4.3, (3.75), p. 461: The symmetry action of Ẑ^× = Aut(ℚ/ℤ).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification"></a>

### The Bost–Connes phase transition

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/kms-classification` (theorem) · planet: *Bost–Connes phase transition*.

For 0<β≤1 there is exactly one completed KMSβ state; for β>1 its extreme boundary is W and its states are uniquely the barycentres of the Gibbs extremes. The first regime follows from low-temperature-uniqueness, the second from high-beta-affine-homeomorphism; symmetry is a separate torsor theorem.

**Hypotheses and scope.** β > 0; states and KMS condition as in B.9/kms-states.

**Proof.**

1. Restrict a completed KMS state to the commutative C(Ẑ) and use the KMS–scaling-measure correspondence.
2. For 0<β≤1 use the finite-prime projection, character-annihilation and ergodicity chain; for β>1 use the unit-orbit decomposition and barycentre chain.
3. Transport the measure classification back to states and apply the symmetry intertwining.

**Checks.** The β ≤ 1 formula at e(1/2) gives 2^{−β}(1 − 2^{β−1})/(1/2) = 2^{1−β} − 1, the same value as the Gibbs formula, which is consistent at the boundary.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/bc-low-temperature-uniqueness`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-low-temperature-uniqueness), [`AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/bc-adelic-scaling-measure`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-adelic-scaling-measure), [`AN.9/plan/partition-function`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-partition-function), [`AN.9/plan/bc-scaling-measure-space`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-scaling-measure-space), [`AN.9/plan/bc-completed-gibbs`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-completed-gibbs), [`AN.9/plan/symmetry-action`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-symmetry-action).

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-orbits`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-measure`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-affine-homeomorphism`, `AN.9/bc-high-beta-extremes`, `AN.9/bc-kms-symmetry-transitive`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives (Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli), Ch. 3, §4.6, Theorem 3.32, pp. 474–475: The Bost–Connes classification of KMS states, attributed there to [30] = Bost–Connes. Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives (Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli), Ch. 3, §4.6, Theorem 3.32, p. 475: The low-temperature extremal states are indexed by Ẑ^×.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground"></a>

### KMS∞ states and upper-half-plane ground states

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground` (definition).

For the BC system, KMS∞ means a state in the weak closure of KMSβ states along β→∞: every finite set of observables, tolerance ε>0 and threshold B is met by some β>B and KMSβ state. Ground means each correlation has a bounded holomorphic extension to the upper half-plane. These are separate predicates; the general trivial-dynamics matrix test distinguishes them.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the finite-observable weak topology on bounded states.
2. Use the upper-half-plane boundedness definition separately.
3. Prove the implication by compactness/normal-family limits rather than equating the definitions.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.isLimit` (constructor): The finite-observable weak-limit criterion as β tends to infinity.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.isGround` (constructor): The bounded holomorphic upper-half-plane correlation condition.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.limit_isGround` (relation): Every KMS∞ state is a ground state under the completed dynamics.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.test_gibbs_limit` (compatibility): The β→∞ limit of φβ,u is the ε1 vector state.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.test_value_half` (computation): The extremal limit has value−1 on e(1/2).
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.test_different_notions` (non-example): For trivial dynamics on M2(C), the vector state a↦a00 satisfies the same upper-half-plane ground-state predicate but fails the finite-temperature-limit predicate: a01a10 and a10a01 have state values 1 and 0. This tests the generic predicates with which the completed BC predicates are compatible.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9: The downstream proof chains below consume these named operations, identities and normalization tests..

**Checks.** Define KMS∞ states as weak limits of KMSβ states as β→∞. Equivalently in this separable unital system, for every finite set of observables, ε>0 and cutoff B there is a KMSβ state with β>B approximating those values within ε. Ground states instead require φ(aσz(b)) to extend bounded holomorphically to Imz>0, continuously on the boundary. KMS∞ states are ground states; the converse is not built into either definition.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/bc-completed-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-completed-kms), [`AN.9/plan/bc-cstar-completion`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-cstar-completion), [`AN.9/plan/ax-plus-b-hecke-triple`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-ax-plus-b-hecke-triple), [`AN.9/plan/axb-named-matrices`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-axb-named-matrices), `mathlib:Rat.num_div_den`, `tauceti:HeckeCoset.degree_eq_relIndex`, [`AN.9/plan/axb-diagonal-map`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-axb-diagonal-map), `mathlib:lp`, [`AN.9/plan/bost-connes-hecke-algebra`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bost-connes-hecke-algebra), [`AN.9/plan/time-evolution`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-time-evolution).

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-trigonometric-eisenstein"></a>

### First trigonometric Eisenstein function

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-trigonometric-eisenstein` (construction).

For a∈Q/Z and any positive N annihilating a, e1,a=Σ1≤j<N(j/N−1/2)e(ja) in the rational group algebra. The sum is independent of N. Under a torsion character with ρ(a)≠0 it evaluates to cot(πρ(a))/(2i); at ρ(a)=0 it is zero. Higher functions and their polynomial recurrence are separate constructions.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Choose an annihilating level and form the finite rational Fourier sum.
2. The finite Fourier identity proves independence under multiples of a level and hence under a common multiple.
3. Evaluate at torsion characters, retaining the zero value at the trivial character.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.first` (constructor): The first finite rational Fourier sum.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.finite_sum` (characterisation): For every positive N annihilating a, first a is the displayed sum.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.neg` (functoriality): first (−a)=−first a.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_first_zero` (degenerate): first 0=0.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_half` (computation): first (1/2)=0.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_third` (computation): first (1/3)=−e(1/3)/6+e(2/3)/6.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9: The downstream proof chains below consume these named operations, identities and normalization tests..

**Checks.** For a∈Q/Z and N>0 with Na=0, define e1,a=Σ1≤k<N(k/N−1/2)e(ka) in the rational group algebra. The expression is independent of N. ### Eisenstein recurrence polynomials

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-eisenstein-polynomials` (definition).

Define P0=0, P1=X and Pk+1=(X²−1/4)P′k/k for k≥1 in Q[X]. For k≥1, Pk is monic of degree k. The derivative recurrence comes from the normalized cotangent identity; Pk(0) is the prescribed value at a degenerate lattice.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Define recursively in Q[X].
2. The leading derivative coefficient k cancels division by k, preserving monicity while increasing the degree by one.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.polynomial_recurrence` (characterisation): For k≥1, P(k+1)=(X²−1/4)P′k/k.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.polynomial_monic` (characterisation): For k≥1, Pk.Monic.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.polynomial_degree` (characterisation): For k≥1, Pk.natDegree=k.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_polynomial_two` (computation): P2=X²−1/4.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_polynomial_three` (computation): P3=X³−X/4.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.ArithmeticEisenstein.test_polynomial_four` (computation): P4=X⁴−X²/3+1/48.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-eisenstein-higher"></a>

### Higher trigonometric Eisenstein functions

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-eisenstein-higher` (definition).

For k≥0 and a∈Q/Z define ek,a=Pk(e1,a) in the rational group algebra. The value at a character killing a is Pk(0), including e2,0=−1/4. For k≥1, on the nondegenerate locus this agrees with the k-fold normalized cotangent series; k=1 uses the symmetric principal-value convention. The k=0 polynomial P0=0 is an algebraic convention, not a convergent weight-zero cotangent sum.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Apply the rational polynomial Pk to the first function. Evaluate in characters and use the cotangent recurrence on the nondegenerate locus. The degenerate character has first value zero, hence higher value Pk(0), rather than zero in every weight.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation"></a>

### The trigonometric arithmetic algebra equals the BC rational form

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation` (theorem).

The rational subalgebra generated by e1,a for all a is Q[Q/Z]. The finite Fourier formula gives containment in the group algebra, and the root-recovery lemma gives the opposite containment. This is a statement about the diagonal rational group algebra; adjoining isometries and complexification are separate results.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Use the finite Fourier sum for the first inclusion.
2. Use root recovery and the spanning basis e(a) for the reverse inclusion.

**Checks.** The e1,a generate Q[Q/Z]. Together with μn,μn* they generate the arithmetic algebra A1,Q; complexification gives the dense complex algebra. This is BC’s normalized rational form and is compared to the Q-valued Hecke form only through σ−i/2, which is not a star map.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-galois-action-on-ground-states"></a>

### Cyclotomic values and Galois action on extremal KMS∞ states

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/galois-action-on-ground-states` (theorem).

For u ∈ Aut(ℚ/ℤ) the extremal KMS∞ vector state φ_{∞,u}(f) = ⟨ε₁, π_u(f)ε₁⟩ is the limit of φ_{β,u} as β → ∞. On the rational form H_ℚ (the ℚ-valued functions), φ_{∞,u}([X]) = exp(2πi u(γ)) if X is the class of translation γ and 0 otherwise; so φ_{∞,u}(H_ℚ) lies in the cyclotomic field ℚ(μ_∞) ⊂ ℂ. For every field automorphism τ of ℂ, τ ∘ φ_{∞,u} = φ_{∞,χ(τ)u} on H_ℚ, where χ(τ) ∈ Aut(ℚ/ℤ) is the automorphism with τ(exp(2πiγ)) = exp(2πi χ(τ)(γ)); that is, τ ∘ φ_{∞,u} = φ_{∞,u} ∘ θ_{χ(τ)}. This states the extremal KMS∞ result and does not classify all upper-half-plane ground states.

**Hypotheses and scope.** u ∈ Aut(ℚ/ℤ); τ a ring automorphism of ℂ.

**Proof.**

1. π_u(x_n e(γ) x′_m)ε₁ = 0 unless m = 1, and then it is a multiple of ε_n, orthogonal to ε₁ unless n = 1; so φ_{∞,u} kills every basis element except the classes of translations, where it is exp(2πi u(γ)).
2. Limit: φ_{β,u}(e(γ)) = ζ(β)⁻¹Σ k^{−β}exp(2πiku(γ)) → exp(2πiu(γ)) as β → ∞, since ζ(β) → 1 and the tail is O(2^{−β}).
3. τ permutes the roots of unity in ℂ, and the induced map on ℚ/ℤ ≅ μ_∞ is additive and bijective; this defines χ(τ) (the cyclotomic character). Then τ(exp(2πiu(γ))) = exp(2πi χ(τ)(u(γ))), and B.9/symmetry-action gives the intertwining.
4. Prove the KMS∞ limit on the completed state space and then restrict to either rational form; continuity of arbitrary complex field automorphisms is never assumed.

**Checks.** On BC's form A_ℚ the same values arise (B.9/rational-forms-comparison), so the statement does not depend on the choice of rational form.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/regular-representation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-regular-representation), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states), [`AN.9/plan/symmetry-action`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-symmetry-action), [`AN.9/plan/rational-forms-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-rational-forms-comparison), `mathlib:IsCyclotomicExtension`, [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground), [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation), `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields#layer-10-archimedean-characters-infinity-types-and-cyclotomic-arithmetic`, `mathlib:MulAut`, `mathlib:AddCircle`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.9/bc-unit-qmodz-adapter`, `AN.9/bc-cyclotomic-restrictions`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives (Alain Connes and Matilde Marcolli), Ch. 3, §4.6, Theorem 3.32, (3.136)–(3.137), p. 475: Ground-state values on the rational algebra are cyclotomic, and Galois acts through the symmetries.

### Positive-spectrum zeta and heat series

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/spectral-zeta-series` (construction) · planet: *Spectral zeta function*.

For a connected compact hyperbolic surface X=Γ\H with Γ torsion-free and cocompact, genus g≥2, use Δ=−y²(∂x²+∂y²). Import the discrete spectrum0=λ0<λ1≤… with multiplicities. Define ζΔ(s)=Σj≥1 λj^(−s) on Res>1 and H(t)=Σj≥0 exp(−tλj) for t>0. The analytic continuation of ζΔ is distinguished from the totalized infinite sum.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import the compact quotient and positive scalar Laplacian.
2. Index the nonzero spectrum with multiplicities and omit the zero eigenvalue in ζΔ.
3. Use Weyl growth to justify the series on their stated domains.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.series` (constructor): The positive-spectrum complex-power series.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.heat` (constructor): Heat series including the single zero eigenvalue.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.continued` (constructor): The meromorphic continuation agreeing with the positive series for Res>1.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.test_single_eigenvalue` (computation): For a finite spectrum consisting of λ>0, the series is λ^(−s).
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.test_zero_omitted` (non-example): The zero eigenvalue contributes1 to the heat series and contributes no term to ζΔ.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.SpectralData.test_scaling` (compatibility): Replacing each positive λ by cλ for c>0 multiplies the convergent zeta series by c^(−s).

Define ζΔ(s)=Σj≥1 λj^(−s) on Res>1 and H(t)=Σj≥0 exp(−tλj) for t>0. The analytic continuation of ζΔ is distinguished from the totalized infinite sum.

### The scalar Selberg primitive-geodesic product

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-primitive-product` (construction) · planet: *Selberg zeta function*.

For the same compact torsion-free quotient, let PΓ be primitive hyperbolic conjugacy classes, with the orientation/conjugacy convention of Zagier(2). For each p let ℓp=log N(p)>0. Define ZΓ(s)=∏p∈PΓ ∏k≥0 (1−exp(−(s+k)ℓp)) for Res>1; its entire continuation is separate. Primitive conjugacy classes, their inverses and geometric unoriented geodesics are not interchanged without the multiplicity comparison.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Import primitive hyperbolic classes and their length normalization.
2. Use a geodesic-count growth bound to prove absolute local product convergence.
3. Define the continuation only after the trace-formula comparison.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.Selberg.product` (constructor): The displayed double Euler product in Res>1.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.Selberg.continued` (constructor): The entire continuation with the same product on Res>1.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.Selberg.log_derivative` (characterisation): Z′/Z=Σp Σm≥1 ℓp exp(−msℓp)/(1−exp(−mℓp)) in Res>1.

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.Selberg.test_two_lengths` (compatibility): Disjoint primitive class lists multiply their products in the convergence domain.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.Selberg.test_orientation` (non-example): Replacing the source class list by two copies squares the product; it changes the theorem unless its multiplicities are corrected.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-spectral-regularity-zero"></a>

### Spectral zeta is regular at zero

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/spectral-regularity-zero` (theorem).

The positive spectral zeta continues meromorphically, and is analytic at0 because Γ(s)^(−1) has a simple zero there, canceling the possible simple Mellin pole. Its derivative at0 is well defined.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Continue successively using finite heat subtractions.
2. Use Γ(s+1)=sΓ(s) and Γ(1)=1 at0.
3. Differentiate the resulting holomorphic expression, never the divergent original series.

**Checks.** The positive spectral zeta continues meromorphically, and is analytic at0 because Γ(s)^(−1) has a simple zero there, canceling the possible simple Mellin pole. Its derivative at0 is well defined.

**Prerequisites.** [`AN.9/plan/spectral-zeta-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-spectral-zeta-series), `AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.4`, `mathlib:mellin`, `mathlib:Complex.Gamma`.

**Proof ingredients.** `AN.9/compact-spectrum-and-weyl`, `AN.9/spectral-weyl-summability`, `AN.9/heat-mellin-on-right-half-plane`, `AN.9/heat-large-time-tail`, `AN.9/heat-small-time-subtraction`, `AN.9/heat-subtracted-holomorphy`, `AN.9/spectral-continuation-output`; their statements and locators are in the proof-ingredient index.

**Source.** Determinants of Laplacians, heights and finiteness (Peter Sarnak), §1, (1.1)–(1.5), p.603: Spectral zeta is regular at zero; the statement fixes the source conventions and the proof leaves below.

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/spectral-regularized-determinant` (construction) · planet: *Regularized determinant*.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-shifted-entire-determinant"></a>

### Entire shifted determinant

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/shifted-entire-determinant` (construction).

The canonical shifted determinant D is entire in u, agrees with the zeta determinant for Reu>0, has D(u)/u→det′Δ at 0, and includes all eigenvalues with their multiplicities. Its function, rather than a branch of its logarithm, is continued.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. The sum of inverse squared positive eigenvalues converges, so the genus-one canonical product converges normally on all compact u sets. Its exponential prefactor is entire and nonzero. Compare on Re u>0 by integrating the shifted-zeta derivative, fixing the constant at zero.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.entire` (characterisation): The whole shifted family is entire.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.agrees` (compatibility): On Reu>0 it is the exponentiated derivative of the jointly continued ζu.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.zero_mode` (characterisation): D(u)/u tends to det′Δ at u=0, retaining the simple zero mode.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_zero` (degenerate): The actual infinite-family determinant vanishes at u=0, retaining the zero eigenvalue.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_positive_shift` (compatibility): At u=1, the actual genus-one family equals exp(−ζ1′(0)).
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_actual_quarter` (non-example): If eigenvalue λ1=1/4, the actual infinite determinant at −1/4 vanishes; its quadratic pullback multiplicity is governed by the exact zero-divisor lemma.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-functional-equation: Supplies a branch-independent determinant invariant under s↦1−s.. AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison: The exact zero divisor gives the spectral multiplicity..

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-determinant-comparison"></a>

### The compact Selberg determinant comparison

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-determinant-comparison` (comparison).

For the selected scalar compact surface, det(Δ+s(s−1))=ZΓ(s)I_g(s) exp(2(g−1)[2ζ′(−1)−log√(2π)]) for real s>1, extended by the proved analytic continuation. Thus det′Δ=Z′Γ(1)(2π)^(g−1)exp(4(g−1)ζ′(−1)). The sign is the corrected v2 sign; source v1(1.3) has the opposite Euler-characteristic sign.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Combine the hyperbolic and identity Laplace–Mellin derivatives.
2. Determine the additive logarithmic constant from the prescribed large-s expansion.
3. At s=1 remove the simple zero eigenvalue and use Γ(1)=G(2)=1.

Thus det′Δ=Z′Γ(1)(2π)^(g−1)exp(4(g−1)ζ′(−1)). The sign is the corrected v2 sign; source v1(1.3) has the opposite Euler-characteristic sign.

### The compact Selberg functional equation

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-functional-equation` (theorem).

With D_g(s)=I_g(s)exp(2(g−1)[2ζ′(−1)−log√(2π)]), the continued scalar Selberg function satisfies ZΓ(s)D_g(s)=ZΓ(1−s)D_g(1−s) as a meromorphic identity. This formulation fixes all Barnes branches by continuation from real s>1 and avoids an unnormalized path integral.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. The shifted operator Δ+s(s−1) is unchanged by s↦1−s.
2. Use the determinant comparison on its domain and continue.
3. Multiply by the explicit identity factors to obtain a branch-consistent equation.

**Checks.** With D_g(s)=I_g(s)exp(2(g−1)[2ζ′(−1)−log√(2π)]), the continued scalar Selberg function satisfies ZΓ(s)D_g(s)=ZΓ(1−s)D_g(1−s) as a meromorphic identity. This formulation fixes all Barnes branches by continuation from real s>1 and avoids an unnormalized path integral.

Use the scalar identity factor confirmed by the heat derivative, as specified in E48.: Determinant invariance under s↦1−s and the single-valued identity factor give the meromorphic functional equation.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison"></a>

### Selberg zeros and scalar spectral parameters

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison` (comparison).

On 0<Res<1, zeros of the continued scalar ZΓ are exactly the solutions s(1−s)=λ>0. An eigenvalue of multiplicity m contributes order m at each root when λ≠1/4, and order 2m at s=1/2 when λ=1/4. For λ>1/4 the two roots have real part 1/2; for 0<λ<1/4 both are real in (0,1). Separately, the simple zero mode gives order 1 at s=1 and order 2g−1 at s=0 after the identity-factor pole. Other trivial zeros are not called spectral.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

**Proof.**

1. Use the shifted determinant zeros with eigenvalue multiplicity.
2. Separate the explicit identity-factor zeros/poles.
3. Solve the quadratic relation and retain small positive eigenvalues.

**Checks.** The spectral zeros occur at both solutions of s(1−s)=λj, with multiplicities determined by the determinant comparison and the identity factor. For λj≥1/4 they lie on Res=1/2; for 0<λj<1/4 they are real in(0,1). The zero mode gives s=0,1. Identity-factor trivial zeros are separated before calling zeros spectral; no Riemann RH consequence follows.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-ratio-set"></a>

### Ratio set of a nonsingular action

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-ratio-set` (definition).

Let a countable group G act nonsingularly on a nonzero standard sigma-finite measure space (X,μ), and let ρg=d(g_*μ)/dμ with g_*μ(E)=μ(g⁻¹E). RatioSet is the set of λ≥0 such that for every measurable A of positive measure and ε>0 some g has μ({x∈A∩gA:|ρg(x)−λ|<ε})>0. The derivative is evaluated at the target x.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Use the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the pushforward at its target and restrict the witness set to A intersect gA. This definition records positivity and essential approximation; its general orbit-invariance and classification API belongs to OP2-ratio.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.one_mem` (characterisation): The identity transformation puts 1 in the ratio set.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.closed` (characterisation): The ratio set is closed in nonnegative reals.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.orbit_invariant` (compatibility): Equivalent nonsingular orbit relations have the same ratio set. The derivative convention is pushforward at the target.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.test_trivial_one` (computation): For the identity action on a one-point probability space, 1 lies in the ratio set.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.test_trivial_two` (non-example): For that same action, 2 does not lie in the ratio set.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.RatioSet.test_trivial_zero` (non-example): For that same action, 0 does not lie in the ratio set.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/bc-full-positive-ratio-set: States the target on finite adeles with its explicit pushforward derivative..

**Checks.** Check the specified domain and normalization before using this result.

**Prerequisites.** `mathlib:MeasureTheory.Measure.rnDeriv`.

### The critical KMS factors have type III₁

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one` (theorem).

For 0<β≤1, the GNS von Neumann algebra of the unique completed Bost–Connes KMSβ state is a type III1 factor. The proof passes through the full positive ratio set, the ergodic group-measure factor and its nonzero compression by 1Ẑ.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The carrier, domain and normalization hypotheses in the statement are part of the result.

1. Use ergodicity for factoriality.
2. Lift the positive ratio set through the compact quotient, as required by Neshveyev Theorem2.1.
3. Use the nonsingular crossed-product/type classification and preserve type under a full corner.

### Ground state at an invertible lattice

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-vector-ground-state` (construction).

For each unit character u, the representation πu has a continuous extension to C_Q. Its vector functional at ε1 is a normalized positive state φ∞,u. It is the weak limit of Gibbsβ,u as β→∞ and hence a KMS-infinity state. Evaluation on μn eγ μm* is zero unless n=m=1, when it is exp(2πi uγ).

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Extend the bounded core representation to the completion. Its epsilon_1 vector functional is positive and normalized. Dominate the Gibbs tail by the zeta tail to prove pointwise convergence as beta grows, then evaluate the normalized monomial on epsilon_1.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.vectorState_one` (characterisation): φ∞,u(1)=1.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.vectorState_basis` (characterisation): The normalized basis has the stated zero/character values.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.vectorState_isLimit` (compatibility): φ∞,u is KMS-infinity.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.vectorState_test_one` (computation): The vector state sends 1 to 1.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.test_value_half` (computation): It sends e(1/2) to −1.
- `TauCeti.BostConnes.KMSInfinity.vectorState_test_shift` (computation): It sends μ2 to 0.

### Arithmetic values and symmetry intertwining

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry` (theorem).

For an extremal KMS∞ vector state, e(a) evaluates to the corresponding root of unity and every reduced normal-form monomial with(n,m)≠(1,1) evaluates to0. Its rational arithmetic values generate Qcycl. The induced cyclotomic character intertwines field automorphisms with unit symmetries on those values.

2. Use the rational generation theorem and the cyclotomic root image.
3. Invoke the supplied cyclotomic/class-field character and verify the equality on the basis.

**Checks.** For an extremal KMS∞ vector state, e(a) evaluates to the corresponding root of unity and every reduced normal-form monomial with(n,m)≠(1,1) evaluates to0. Its rational arithmetic values generate Qcycl. The induced cyclotomic character intertwines field automorphisms with unit symmetries on those values.

<a id="target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-shifted-finite-determinant"></a>

### Finite spectral determinant benchmark

**Target:** `AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9/plan/shifted-finite-determinant` (construction).

For a finite index set and eigenvalues λj define Dfin(u)=∏j(λj+u). This is the finite-dimensional version of zeta regularization; it includes zero modes. It is a separate constructor from the infinite genus-one determinant and does not substitute for tests of that family.

**Hypotheses and scope.** The hypotheses in the statement.

**Construction or proof.**

1. Multiply the finitely many affine factors, including any zero-mode factor u. Polynomial analyticity and the finite product zero criterion give the API and tests; the empty product equals one.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.finite_empty` (characterisation): The empty determinant is 1.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.finite_zero_iff` (characterisation): Dfin(u)=0 iff λj+u=0 for some j.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.finite_entire` (characterisation): The finite determinant is entire in u.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_finite_empty` (degenerate): For the empty finite spectrum the shifted determinant is 1.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_finite_single` (computation): For one finite eigenvalue λ it is λ+u.
- `TauCeti.SpectralZeta.ShiftedDet.test_quarter_pullback` (non-example): For one eigenvalue 1/4, its pullback u=s(s−1) is (s−1/2)², giving a double zero.

**Uses.** AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.9: Supplies the explicitly named analytic output or arithmetic construction of this layer..

**Checks.** Check the specified domain and normalization before using this result.

### Open proof boundaries in AN.9

Each item is a recorded gap: a named input or proof step that is not yet established. It is not papered over by the targets above.

- **Normalized Haar and canonical adelic component adapters.** The finite-adèle ring is an existing Mathlib carrier, its compact integral subgroup is imported from current Tau Ceti, and probability products already exist in Mathlib. AA.0 must connect normalized additive Haar of Qp to the actual local components and restricted-product exhaustion. Then construct the canonical local density/product/dilation measure on that carrier. The native local density and global Radon scaling predicates are already concrete; this gap is their canonical compatibility, not a missing measure type.
- **OperatorTheory Part II: crossed products and bounded-state completion.** Import existing operator ideals, closed operator algebras and Mathlib C*-GNS; do not replan them. The exact extension requests below cover algebraic bounded-generator GNS, universal C*-completion, semigroup minimal dilation, full-corner covariance, amenability/full=reduced, dense analytic-core KMS extension and expectation/state-measure reconstruction. Laca proves the dilation/corner comparison read here; the general amenability and analytic-strip framework proofs remain unsupplied.
- **OperatorTheory Part II: nonsingular factor classification.** The target-evaluated ratio predicate and the BC prime/cylinder/unit-lifting witnesses are explicit. Supply the standard sigma-finite measured equivalence-relation/asymptotic-ratio interface, group-measure-space von Neumann algebra, ergodic center/factor theorem, ratio-set-to-III1 theorem, and nonzero-corner/GNS compression invariance. Neshveyev states/uses this general theory; its primary proofs are not certified here.
- **Compact scalar geometric spectral and Gaussian trace adapters.** ALS.0 supplies the compact torsion-free oriented surface. AS.4 must identify its actual scalar Laplacian with the concrete monotone heat/spectrum contract (simple zero, Weyl counts, uniform full expansion). AS.6 must extend compactly supported smooth trace tests to the Gaussian and supply geodesic counting and the same primitive orientation convention. The full JSS §5 transform proofs have been read; the generic Mellin and shifted-product signatures do not by themselves establish these geometric suppliers.
- **Barnes G original normalization and asymptotic proof.** AN.7 must extend beyond its Hurwitz/Lerch pass to the normalized Barnes G of JSS §2.5, (2.8)–(2.9), p.9: G(1)=1, functional equation, zeros, logarithmic derivative and the uniform asymptotic used to fix C. JSS cites Adamchik; that primary proof remains unread. The single-valued integer-power identity factor and zero/pole divisor have explicit contracts.
- **Canonical native interfaces and weak state topology.** Canonical cubic orbital unfolding is the separate lemma cubic-adelic-unfolding: its native signature remains omitted pending the actual GL2 adelic quotient measure, Schwartz space, rational orbits and weighted orbital integrals from AA.2/AL.0/ST.1. Every listed definition API now has a native declaration. Other native leaf omissions are itemized individually in nativeOmissions, with exact missing functions or topology. In particular ordinary ξ,ξhat,ρF and class-group/signature indices cannot be replaced by unconstrained function fields; the high-beta homeomorphism uses pointwise weak state topology, not the operator-norm topology of continuous functionals.
- **Current upstream identifiers absent from the historical declaration index.** The separately audited upstreamImports are existing work and are imported, never replanned. The checker only knows its historical atlas/library index, so these edges are also recorded on each affected node as upstreamImports. A package must resolve them to current modules or current upstream roadmap layer ids; this is an integration obligation rather than an assertion that the mathematics is missing.

## Restructuring proposals

- **rescope** (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev, AnalyticNumberTheory). Red-team finding RT-AREA-analytic/1: the arithmetic-scheme form of Chebotarev density (Serre, Lectures on N_X(p), §9: Frobenius classes of closed points of a normal integral scheme of finite type over ℤ are equidistributed in a finite étale Galois cover) has no owner. AN.4 after RS-07 owns number-field analytic comparisons only, and the Tau Ceti Chebotarev roadmap is number-field-only and cannot be changed here. PAPER-ABDURRAHMAN-VENKATESH-25/20 and PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 need it. *Proposal:* New roadmap “Chebotarev density theorem, Part II: arithmetic schemes”, extending tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev: normal integral schemes of finite type over ℤ, finite étale Galois covers, conjugacy-stable Frobenius sets of closed points, the log-norm-weighted natural density of Serre §9, the number-field case recovered in relative dimension zero, density of Frobenius elements in π₁, and triviality of a finite cover split at a density-one set of closed points. It imports the analytic input (Dedekind/Hecke continuation and line-one nonvanishing) from AN.4 and the finite-field Lang–Weil count from its owner. AN.4 keeps its RS-07 narrowing and states in its boundary that the scheme-level theorem lives in that Part II.
- **rescope** (AnalyticNumberTheory, AdditiveCombinatorics). Red-team finding RT-AREA-combinatorics/8: the RS-07 link AN.2 → AdditiveCombinatorics:AC.4 exists only for the Green–Tao 2008 route (correlation condition), which needs the classical zero-free region with growth bounds (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/green-tao-zeta-strip, AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/riemann-zeta-weak-convexity) and the uniform progression theorem (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/siegel-walfisz). The Conlon–Fox–Zhao route named by AC.4’s own text needs only ζ(s) = 1/(s−1) + O(1) near 1 (Mathlib isBigO_riemannZeta_sub_one_div) and Chebyshev bounds. *Proposal:* If the AC.4 owner selects the Conlon–Fox–Zhao route, narrow the link AN.2 → AC.4 to nothing (AC.4 imports Mathlib directly) and drop the three analytic gaps from AC.4’s decomposition. If it keeps the Green–Tao 2008 route, keep the link with the exact contract of the two AN.2 targets named above and of the Siegel–Walfisz target, together with the elementary bound W(N) ≤ (log N)^B for the chosen w(N). The choice is AC.4’s; this packet supplies both contracts.

## Mistakes found in the sources

Each finding is stated in our own words at its locator; targets use the corrected statements.

- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E1** (error; A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums; Published §8.1 p.378 and its reuse on p.379; known source issue E2.). The proposed divisor inequality omits the multiplicative constant required uniformly at small inputs. *Correction:* Use the uniform explicit bound and eventual threshold supplied by the AN.5 chain; retain the constant for all positive n. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* Previously recorded and independently confirmed as PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/E2; no new finding claimed.. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E2** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; Equation(8.3.3), printed p.50, PDF p.66). The gamma logarithmic derivative is evaluated at the wrong shift for the displayed zeta completion. *Correction:* The displayed term must be Γ′(1+s/2)/Γ(1+s/2). Equivalently retain Γ′(s/2)/Γ(s/2) together with the missing 1/s term. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E3** (error; Notes on analytic number theory; Lemma22.1, printed p.127, PDF p.143). The proposed Frobenius condition asks only for a nonzero residue element satisfying the power relation, rather than requiring the action on every residue element. *Correction:* Require a chosen prime P above p and the action of g on every element of O_K/P to be x↦x^p; use NFA2's IsArithFrobAt and then its conjugacy theorem. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E4** (error; Notes on analytic number theory; Equations(7.2.1)–(7.2.2), printed pp.44–45, and proof of Theorem7.7). The reciprocal-ordinate sum uses signed 1/γ while its Stieltjes expression is a nonnegative count over both ordinate signs. *Correction:* Use 1/|γ| in the nonnegative majorant and Stieltjes sum. Choose T away from zero ordinates, or use matching left limits at T. Isolate a finite low-height range and justify a positive lower cutoff. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E5** (gap; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorems7.5/8.8 and use in Theorem7.7, printed pp.45,50–51). The zero-free conclusion allows height one, where the logarithmic denominator degenerates. *Correction:* Retain only Im(s)≥t₀>1 as the direct conclusion; establish bounded heights and conjugation separately before deriving the global PNT error. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* Inherited integrated-decomposition independent review's high-height and low-zero-gap corrections; no new priority claim.. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E6** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem8.7 proof following(8.2.3), printed p.49). The small-factor expansion has the wrong quadratic sign. *Correction:* The expansion is 1−(z/ρ)²/2+O((z/ρ)³). Also the middle range in the three-factor partition is h₂, not a second h₁. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E7** (gap; Notes on analytic number theory; End of Theorem8.7 proof, printed p.49). The proof jumps from an upper bound on the real part of an entire logarithm to the required bound on its modulus. *Correction:* Choose a global holomorphic logarithm of the zero-free entire quotient, then derive a modulus bound for g from its real-part upper bound using Borel–Carathéodory on nested discs (or an equivalent named lemma). *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E8** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem10.2 parity convention, printed p.59). The parity parameter is assigned the odd value to an even character. *Correction:* For the displayed −(1−a)log x and ∑x^(a−2m)/(2m−a), use a=0 for even and a=1 for odd primitive characters. State the primitive restriction; imprimitive local-factor zeros need separate terms. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E9** (error; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem10.11, printed p.63, omitted progression hypothesis). The prime-progression theorem omits the coprimality hypothesis and a quantitative range for its modulus. *Correction:* Require gcd(a,N)=1, x sufficiently large, and state an explicit logarithmic modulus range N≤(log x)^B with fixed B in the standard Siegel–Walfisz formulation. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E10** (gap; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem10.11 following Siegel's theorem, printed p.63). Effectivity is claimed despite the use of an ineffective Siegel estimate. *Correction:* The usual Siegel–Walfisz proof from the stated Siegel theorem has potentially ineffective constants. An effective version needs an additional explicit input or an exceptional-zero term and a revised contract. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E11** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem9.9 proof, printed pp.57–58). The limiting direction for the auxiliary parameter is reversed. *Correction:* The odd positive integer U tends to infinity. The near-endpoint remainder range on p.58 is 3x/4<n<x′, not3/4<n<x′. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E12** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; Remark10.8 zero-repulsion inequalities, printed p.62). A real-part expression subtracts the imaginary coordinate of a zero. *Correction:* Use σ−Re(ρ) when the evaluation point has the same imaginary part as the zero. The principal-character pole occurs at s=1, not at χ=1. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E13** (error; Notes on analytic number theory; Theorem10.6 denominator, printed p.61). The zero-free denominator log N is used also for the primitive conductor-one character. *Correction:* Assume N>1 for this primitive Dirichlet-character formulation; treat the unique conductor-one character through the zeta statement. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E16** (error; Notes on analytic number theory; Lemma8.3 proof, printed p47/PDFp63, author PDF sha7a934fce; parallel current HTML chap-zeroes). The claimed exponential-type growth loses the logarithmic factor produced by the gamma integral. *Correction:* Retain ω(x)≤C₀e^(−πx), and bound the resulting gamma integral by exp(C₁|s|log(2+|s|)). This proves the stated order-one growth but not the claimed exponential-type integral bound. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E17** (misprint; The Lerch zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Preprint arXiv1506.06161v1 Theorem2.3 (2.5),p13; corrected in published RMS3:2(2016),p13 (2.5)). The sign of the Lerch PDE right-hand side is positive in the preprint. *Correction:* The right-hand side is −sΦ(s,z,c), as in the published equation(2.5). *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* Corrected in the published RMS3:2(2016) equation(2.5), DOI10.1186/s40687-015-0049-2.. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E18** (misprint; Notes on analytic number theory; December 2025 author PreTeXt PDF, §3.3, proof of Theorem 3.7, equation (3.3.1), printed p.19 (PDF p.35); SHA256 7a934fce8272cedd36ad609f79bbe79af0056320bb1e0bc690c87af990f305be.). The ray-character logarithmic expansion omits the prime-power denominator. *Correction:* Insert 1/n: log f_N(s) = Σ_{p:(p,N)=1} Σ_{n≥1} (Σ_χ χ(p^n)) p^(−ns)/n. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E19** (misprint; The Distribution of Prime Numbers; Author preliminary PDF, printed p.61 (PDFp72), Exercise5.4(c); Theorem3.4(c)/(3.6), pp.40–41. Published GSM203 text not inspected.). The Euler-constant integral subtracts the cutoff and exponential in the wrong order. *Correction:* Reverse the integrand: κ = ∫_0^∞ u^−1 (1_[0,1](u) − e^−u) du = γ. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E20** (error; Formules explicites et minorations de conducteurs de variétés algébriques; Published §I.2 conditions(i)–(iii), p.212; transform and reflected-contour proof p.213). The general test-function conditions control the positive exponential weight on the signed variable x, without controlling the reflected tail needed for the transform. *Correction:* For general, potentially asymmetric F, require the integrability/BV conditions for both F(x) and F(−x), equivalently use exp((1/2+c+ε)|x|). Chenevier–Taïbi’s even specialization already has this property. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E21** (misprint; The Distribution of Prime Numbers; Author preliminary PDF, printed p.39 (PDFp50), Theorem3.3 proof, first displayed evaluation; published GSM203 not inspected.). The second harmonic strip uses the cutoff x in place of the preceding strip cutoff B. *Correction:* The second strip sum is Σ_(b≤B) x/b. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E22** (misprint; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), p.40, last line of Theorem5.3 proof.). The final recurrence line omits the entire q_(m+1−j)(z) factor from each sum term. *Correction:* Restore q_(m+1−j)(z) in each summand. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E23** (misprint; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), §6 p.40, Bernoulli generating series.). The Bernoulli generating series omits its constant term. *Correction:* The lower index is k=0 with B₀=1. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E24** (error; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), §6 p.40, Riemann special-value formula in the nonpositive-order discussion.). A negative-integer zeta formula includes the order-zero endpoint with an incompatible Bernoulli convention. *Correction:* For k≥0 use ζ(−k)=(−1)^k B_(k+1)/(k+1), equivalently −B_(k+1)(1)/(k+1). The printed formula is valid for k≥1 but not0. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E25** (misprint; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), §6 p.40, introductory periodic-zeta specializations.). The periodic zeta and Lerch specializations omit their normalizing factor of z. *Correction:* Insert the prefactor z=e^(2πia/d): P(a/d,−m)=zΦ(−m,z,1), using the matched continued functions. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E26** (error; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), Theorem6.1(2), (6.2) p.41 and proof p.42.). A nonpositive-order Lerch identity includes order zero, where its initial term survives. *Correction:* Keep the displayed relation for m≥1. For m=0, with z=e^(2πia), F(a,0)=z/(1−z)=q₀(z)−1; equivalently subtract the surviving n=0 term from the c→0 limit of Φ. Part(1) remains correct. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E27** (misprint; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), Theorem6.1(2) proof p.41, integral preceding(6.4).). The periodic Lerch integral lacks the exponential factor required by the selected normalization. *Correction:* For Re s>0 the numerator must be z e^(−t). Prove the entire extension separately by subtracting the kernel Taylor terms near0 and using reciprocal-gamma zeros. *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E28** (misprint; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), p.41 introductory sentence and p.42 last displayed proof chain.). The parameter and exponential notation in a displayed special-value formula have inconsistent labels. *Correction:* Read s=−m, F(a,−m), and Li_(−m)(e^(2πia),0), respectively. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E29** (error; The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values; Published RMS3:2(2016), Theorem3.4(i-b), equation(3.28), p.26; residue definition(3.24), p.26. The same assertion is present in arXiv1506.06161v1/v2 at(3.28).). The stated residue action around z=1 treats every integer index as invariant. *Correction:* For positive powers Z₁^k on the principal residue germs, f₀ continues to e^(2πiks)f₀, whereas f_p for p≠0 is fixed. The c-loop invariance and Z₀ index shift are unaffected. *Affects:* a stated result. *Known:* new. Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E30** (misprint; Geometric invariants for real quadratic fields; Published Annals184(2016), p.970, §7, Euler product immediately after(7.3).). The class-character Euler product drops the character value in each local denominator. *Correction:* Use ∏_p(1−χ(p)Np^(−s))^(−1), with the same ideal-character convention as the preceding series. *Affects:* nothing. *Known:* new; no applicable correction found in the recorded bounded search (no claim of global novelty). Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E31** (error; The Distribution of Prime Numbers; Author preliminary PDF, Theorem3.4(a) proof, printed p.40 (PDFp51); published GSM203 text not inspected.). The floor-removal error for Σ_(n≤x)log n is printed O(1) after replacing floor(x/p^k) by x/p^k. *Correction:* Use O(x) at this step; after division by x the resulting error is O(1). *Affects:* the proof. *Known:* new; no applicable correction found in the recorded bounded search (no claim of global novelty). Review: confirmed.
- **AnalyticNumberTheory/E32** (misprint; Shtukas and the Taylor expansion of L-functions; Published Annals186(2017), AppendixB.1, p.902, displayed definition of entire-function order.). ## Proof-ingredient index

These are the proof-sized steps of the accepted part plans. They are not separate roadmap targets; each is used in the proof of the targets listed.

- `AN.5/prime-power-log-bound` — *Uniform prime-power divisor bound.* For ε>0, integers p≥2 and a≥0, put D=max(1,(ε log 2)⁻¹). Then a+1≤D p^(aε). D is notation for a real expression, not a new carrier. Used by [`AN.5/plan/explicit-divisor-subpower-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-explicit-divisor-subpower-bound). Source: The divisor bound, Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split.
- `AN.5/large-prime-power-bound` — *Large-prime divisor factor bound.* For ε>0, positive integer p and a≥0, exp(1/ε)≤p implies a+1≤p^(aε). Used by [`AN.5/plan/explicit-divisor-subpower-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-explicit-divisor-subpower-bound). Source: The divisor bound, Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split.
- `AN.5/divisor-bound-from-local-bounds` — *Divisor bounds from local factors.* Let ε∈ℝ, D≥1 and B∈ℕ. Suppose for every prime p and a∈ℕ that a+1≤D p^(aε) if p≤B, and a+1≤p^(aε) if p>B. For every n>0, τ(n)≤D^B n^ε, with τ(n)=card(n.divisors). Used by [`AN.5/plan/explicit-divisor-subpower-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-explicit-divisor-subpower-bound). Source: The divisor bound, Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split.
- `AN.5/absorb-divisor-bound-constant` — *Absorption of the divisor-bound constant.* For n>0 and ε,δ,C∈ℝ, if τ(n)≤C n^ε and C≤n^(δ−ε), then τ(n)≤n^δ. Used by [`AN.5/plan/eventual-divisor-subpower-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-eventual-divisor-subpower-bound). Source: The divisor bound, Second proof, exponential estimate and small/large-prime split.
- `AN.4/ray-class-product-nonvanishing` — *Ray-class product has no boundary zeros.* For the finite character group of a ray class quotient, the product of the continued Hecke L-functions has no zeros at regular points of Re s≥1. At s=1 it has meromorphic order ≤0, permitting the principal-character pole. Each Euler logarithmic coefficient is nonnegative by finite-character orthogonality, with bad-prime factors treated separately. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.3, Theorem 3.7 and (3.3.1), printed p. 19.
- `AN.4/mth-root-gluing` — *Gluing m-th roots across the line Re s = 1.* Let f be holomorphic and zero-free on {Re s > 1}, m ≥ 1, and U an open set containing {Re s = 1} ∖ {1} on which a holomorphic, zero-free g is given with g = f^m on U ∩ {Re s > 1}. Then f extends holomorphically (and zero-free) to {Re s > 1} ∪ U′ for an open U′ ⊇ {Re s = 1} ∖ {1}: on each disc D ⊆ U centred on the line there is a unique holomorphic h_D with h_D^m = g agreeing with f on the connected set D ∩ {Re s > 1}, and the h_D agree on overlaps. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5, proof of Theorem 22.4, printed p. 129.
- `AN.4/quadratic-residue-quotient` — *Quadratic Hecke value as residue quotient.* For a quadratic extension E/F, L_f(1,η)=κ_E/κ_F>0, where κ_K is the positive residue of the continued Dedekind function. Here η is the canonical nontrivial primitive quadratic Hecke character attached by global Artin reciprocity. Its holomorphy at 1, the continued zeta factorization, and the two simple positive residues give the quotient; general line-one nonvanishing is not needed for this argument. Used by [`AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-lvalue-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imaginary-quadratic-lvalue-one), [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-hecke-log-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-hecke-log-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/quadratic-hecke-value-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-quadratic-hecke-value-one). Source: Reviewed extraction: The Andre-Oort conjecture for A_g, Quadratic Euler-factor calculation; Thorner-Zaman 2017 equations (2-1)-(2-7); main Corollary 3.3 adapter.
- `AN.5/prime-divisor-integrated-mean` — *Integrated prime-divisor mean.* With a,C as in the prime-divisor mean lemma, ∫_0^T Σ_{1≤t≤x}a(t)dx=Σ_{1≤t≤T}(T−t)a(t)=CT²/2+O_{n,c}(T^(3/2)), T≥1. Used by [`AN.5/plan/prime-divisor-product-mean`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-prime-divisor-product-mean). - `AN.3/two-sided-truncation-error` — *Two-sided error and the zero term.* For y,z≥2 and A>0 the two-sided sum Σ_{|r|≤y}E_z(r)e^(irα) has absolute value ≤2C_A y(log y)(log z)^−A+|E_z(0)|. - `AN.2/canonical-product-log-derivative` — *Logarithmic derivative of the canonical product.* For the order-one factorization of nonzero entire f, away from zero and its zeros, f′(z)/f(z)=m/z+b+Σ_α(1/(z−α)+1/α). - `AN.2/zeta-hadamard-log-derivative` — *Corrected logarithmic derivative of zeta.* For s≠0,1 with ζ(s)≠0 and s/2 not a nonpositive integer, there exist Hadamard constants A,B and a locally finite multiplicity-indexed family of nonzero ξ zeros ρ such that ζ′(s)/ζ(s)=B−1/s−1/(s−1)+(log π)/2−(1/2)Γ′(s/2)/Γ(s/2)+Σ_ρ(1/(s−ρ)+1/ρ). - `AN.2/digamma-right-half-plane` — *Logarithmic gamma bound.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for every complex z with Re z≥1/2 and |z|≥2, |Complex.digamma(z)−Log(z)|≤C/|z|; the logarithm is principal. - `AN.2/zeta-log-derivative-right` — *Bounded right-edge logarithmic derivative.* For every complex s with Re s≥2, |ζ′(s)/ζ(s)|≤Σ_(n≥1)Λ(n)n^−2<∞, with the same absolute constant for every imaginary part. - `AN.2/zeta-pole-log-derivative` — *Pole term near one.* There are absolute δ,K>0 such that for every real1<σ<1+δ, |−ζ′(σ)/ζ(σ)−1/(σ−1)|≤K. - `AN.2/zeta-three-four-one-derivative` — *Zeta three-four-one inequality.* For σ>1 and real t, 3(−ζ′/ζ)(σ)+4Re(−ζ′/ζ)(σ+it)+Re(−ζ′/ζ)(σ+2it)≥0. - `AN.2/single-zero-positive-term` — *A near-one zero forces a positive reciprocal term.* For a ξ zero ρ=β+it and1<σ≤2, 0<β<1 and Re(1/(σ+it−ρ))=1/(σ−β)>0. For every other ξ zero ρ′, Re(1/(σ+it−ρ′))≥0 and Re(1/ρ′)>0. The real parts of the regularized Hadamard summands may therefore be dropped or bounded below by any one retained term. - `AN.2/zero-free-region-constant-selection` — *Uniform selection of the zero-free constant.* There are effective absolute c>0 and t₀>1 such that any ξ zero β+it with t≥t₀ satisfies β<1−c/log t; hence the same high-height nontrivial zeta-zero exclusion holds. Used by [`AN.2/plan/classical-zero-free-region`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-classical-zero-free-region). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §8.3 (8.3.1)–(8.3.6) and final selection, pp.50–51.
- `AN.3/zeta-unit-height-zero-count` — *Local zero count.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for every real T≥2, the number of nontrivial zeta-zero occurrences with T≤Imρ≤T+1 is at most C log(T+2). Used by [`AN.3/plan/riemann-von-mangoldt-count`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-riemann-von-mangoldt-count), [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Lemma9.4 p.54 and Exercise9.6.1 p.58, via Exercise8.4.9 p.52.
- `AN.3/good-height-selection` — *Choosing a contour height.* There are absolute c,C>0 such that for every T≥2 there is T′∈[T,T+1] with |T′−Imρ|≥c/log(T+2) for every ξ zeroρ. For x≥2, changing the symmetric strict cutoff from T to T′ changes Σmρ x^ρ/ρ by at most C x log(T+2)/T; arbitrary weights require their own uniform band bound. Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Remark9.3 p.54 and Theorem9.9 height adjustment p.57.
- `AN.3/zeta-local-log-derivative` — *Local logarithmic-derivative expansion.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for −1≤σ≤2,|t|≥2, and σ+it not a nontrivial zero, ζ′/ζ(σ+it)=Σ_(|t−Imρ|<1)mρ/(σ+it−ρ)+E(σ,t), with |E(σ,t)|≤C log(2+|t|). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Lemma9.6 pp.55–56 and Exercise9.6.2 p.58.
- `AN.3/zeta-left-log-derivative` — *Left-half-plane bound away from trivial zeros.* For every fixed c>0 there is C_c>0 such that for every complex w with Re w≤−1 and |w+2n|≥c for every integer n≥1, ζ(w)≠0 and |ζ′(w)/ζ(w)|≤C_c log(2+|w|).
