Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Lemma9.8 p.56; pinned full functional equation.
- `AN.3/explicit-formula-residues` — *Residues of the Perron integrand.* For x>1, the integrand −(ζ′/ζ)(s)x^s/s has residue x at1, −m_ρx^ρ/ρ at a nontrivial zeroρ, x^(−2n)/(2n) at−2n, and −ζ′(0)/ζ(0) at0. Summing the trivial zeros gives −(1/2)log(1−x^−2). Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §9.2 Lemma9.2 p.54, proof omitted; local analytic-order factorization.
- `AN.3/perron-nearest-prime-power-error` — *Nearest-prime-power remainder.* For real x≥2,T≥2,c=1+1/log x, put δ(x)=infDist(x,{m∈ℝ:m is a natural prime power and m≠x})>0. The Perron remainder for ψ₀(x), after retaining the exact endpoint kernel, is bounded by C[x log²(xT)/T+(log x)min(1,x/(Tδ(x)))], with one absolute C. A prime-power endpoint has half weight only in the infinite-height limit. Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Lemma9.5 p.55; full Theorem9.9 proof pp.57–58; ADS6 endpoint contract.
- `AN.3/explicit-formula-horizontal-bound` — *Horizontal contour bound.* For x≥2, c=1+1/log x and a height T′≥2 separated from every ξ-zero ordinate by at least c₀/log(T′+2), the two horizontal Perron integrals from Re s=−1 to c have norm at most C_(c₀) x log²(T′+2)/(T′log x). Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem9.9 proof, horizontal segments p.57.
- `AN.3/explicit-formula-left-contour` — *Left contour limit.* For every fixed x≥2,T≥2, the Perron vertical integral at Re s=−U tends to0 as U→∞ through positive odd integers. Uniformly in x,T, the two horizontal tails Re s≤−1 have norm O(log(T+2)/(Tx log x)+1/(Tx(log x)²)), with an absolute constant. Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem9.9 proof, remaining segments p.57.
- `AN.3/low-zero-safe-interval-kernel` — *Low-zero-safe interval kernel.* For every real x≥2 and complex ρ with0<Reρ<1, |(x^ρ−(x/2)^ρ)/ρ|≤2x^(Reρ)min(1,1/|ρ|). Positive-real powers use exp(ρ log x); the bound remains finite as ρ approaches0. Used by [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula). Source: A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums, Bennett–Siksek §12 Proposition12.2 p.387, repaired half-interval deduction.
- `AN.3/zero-weight-sum` — *Logarithmic-square sum of zero weights.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for every primitive Dirichlet characterχ of conductor q≥1 and every T≥2, Σ_(nontrivial zeros |Imρ|≤T)mρ min(1,1/|ρ|)≤C log²(q(T+2)). Nontrivial means0<Reρ<1, and multiplicity is analytic order. Used by [`AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-rational-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula). Source: A conjecture of Erdős, supersingular primes and short character sums, Bennett–Siksek §12 Proposition12.2 p.387; Kedlaya Lemma10.3 p.60.
- `AN.4/artin-direct-sum-factor` — *Direct sums of Artin local factors.* For ρ₁,ρ₂, P_p(ρ₁⊕ρ₂,T)=P_p(ρ₁,T)P_p(ρ₂,T) at every prime, including ramified primes. Hence L(ρ₁⊕ρ₂)=L(ρ₁)L(ρ₂) on Re s>1. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.2 p.128 displayed direct-sum identity.
- `AN.4/artin-absolute-convergence` — *Absolute convergence of Artin factors.* For fixed dimension d and ε>0, uniformly on Re s≥1+ε, the local factors satisfy |P_p((Np)^−s)^−1−1|≤C_{d,ε}(Np)^−Re s. Their product converges absolutely and locally uniformly and is nonzero there. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-derivative-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-derivative-one), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/artin-value-one-subpower`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-value-one-subpower), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.2 p.128 absolute convergence paragraph.
- `AN.4/artin-induction-factor` — *Induction identity including ramification.* For H⊆G and a complex finite-dimensional representation σ of H, with F=L^H, L_K(s,Ind_H^G σ)=L_F(s,σ) on Re s>1, including all ramified local factors. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-derivative-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-derivative-one), [`AN.4/plan/artin-value-one-subpower`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-value-one-subpower), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5 Theorem22.4 sketch p.129.
- `AN.4/artin-linear-hecke-comparison` — *Linear Artin factors are Hecke factors.* For L/K finite Galois and a one-dimensional finite-order character χ:Gal(L/K)→C×, composition with the arithmetic global Artin map gives the canonical primitive finite-order Hecke character η. On Re s>1, the full Artin Euler series equals its full Hecke L-function. At p where χ is trivial on inertia both factors are (1−χ(Frob_p)(Np)^−s)^−1; otherwise both are1. The conductor and archimedean signs come from the same local/global reciprocity dictionary. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-derivative-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-derivative-one), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/artin-value-one-subpower`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-value-one-subpower), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5 Theorem22.4 sketch p.129.
- `AN.4/ray-character-log-coefficients` — *Nonnegative ray-character logarithmic coefficients.* For a finite abelian ray-class quotient H and its full complex character group Ĥ, for h∈H and an integer k≥1, Σ_{χ∈Ĥ}χ(h^k) is #H if h^k=1 and 0 otherwise. On Re s>1 the contribution of an allowed prime ideal 𝔭 to log ∏_χL(s,χ) is Σ_{k≥1}(Σ_χχ([𝔭]^k))/k · N𝔭^(−ks). Thus these logarithmic coefficients are nonnegative after norm regrouping, with bad primes omitted consistently. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.3 Theorem3.7 p.19 equation(3.3.1), corrected by E18.
- `AN.4/nonreal-hecke-at-one` — *Nonreal Hecke characters are nonzero at one.* For a finite-order ray character χ with χ≠χ̄, its canonical L(1,χ) is nonzero. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.4 Theorem3.10 p.19 full proof.
- `AN.4/quadratic-auxiliary-positive-factors` — *Positive quadratic auxiliary Euler factors.* For a nonprincipal quadratic Hecke character χ, Ψ(s)=L(s,χ)ζ_K(s)/ζ_K(2s) has, on Re s>1, local factors (1+x)/(1−x) when χ(p)=1, 1 when χ(p)=−1, and1+x at omitted character primes, x=(Np)^−s. Hence its norm-regrouped Dirichlet coefficients are nonnegative. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.4 Theorem3.11 p.20 displayed quadratic auxiliary product.
- `AN.4/quadratic-auxiliary-holomorphy` — *Auxiliary holomorphy under vanishing at one.* If L(1,χ)=0 for the preceding quadratic character, Ψ extends holomorphically to Re s>1/2. Indeed ζ_K(2s) is nonzero there because Re(2s)>1, and the numerator’s zero cancels ζ_K’s pole at1. At s=1/2, Ψ extends with a zero of order at least1. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.4 Theorem3.11 p.20 pole-cancellation paragraph.
- `AN.4/quadratic-landau-contradiction` — *Landau contradiction for a quadratic character.* For a nonprincipal quadratic Hecke character χ, L(1,χ)≠0. If it vanished, the nonnegative Dirichlet series of Ψ from node168 would have abscissa≤1/2 by ADS8 Landau and node169 holomorphy. For every real σ>1/2 its value would then satisfy Ψ(σ)≥1, while node169 gives lim_{σ↓1/2}Ψ(σ)=0, a contradiction. No convergence or sum identity at σ=1/2 is required. Used by [`AN.4/plan/hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-hecke-nonvanishing-on-line-one). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §3.4 Theorem3.11 p.20 complete proof and §2.1 Theorem2.4 p.12 proof.
- `AN.4/analytic-root-on-disc` — *Analytic root on a nonvanishing disc.* Let D=Metric.ball(a,r)⊆C with r>0,F analytic on D and F(z)≠0 there,m∈N with m≥1,z₀∈D and w₀^m=F(z₀). There exists an analytic R on D with R(z)^m=F(z) for every z∈D and R(z₀)=w₀. Any analytic S with the same powers and value at z₀ equals R throughout D. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5 Theorem22.4 p.129 root-gluing sketch.
- `AN.4/boundary-disc-overlap` — *Overlaps of boundary-centred discs.* If two open complex discs centred on Re s=1 intersect, their intersection is connected and contains a point with Re s>1. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5 Theorem22.4 p.129 patching sentence; expanded geometric input.
- `AN.4/dedekind-completed-functional-equation` — *Dedekind completed-functional-equation comparison.* For a number field K with absolute discriminant D_K, r₁ real places and r₂ conjugate pairs of complex places, let Γ_R(s)=π^(−s/2)Γ(s/2) and Γ_C(s)=2(2π)^(−s)Γ(s), the pinned Complex.Gammaℝ and Complex.Gammaℂ. The canonical continuation supplied by Tate has Λ_K(s)=|D_K|^(s/2)Γ_R(s)^r₁Γ_C(s)^r₂ζ_K^cont(s), and Λ_K(1−s)=Λ_K(s) as meromorphic functions. No equality of totalized values at poles is asserted. Used by [`AN.4/plan/dedekind-negative-even-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-dedekind-negative-even-zero), [`AN.4/plan/imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-imaginary-quadratic-root-number-one). Source: Fourier analysis in number fields and Hecke's zeta-functions, §4.5, scan pp.56–59, especially (4.24) on scan p.58; local factors tabulated in §2.5.
- `AN.5/pretentious-product-triangle` — *Triangle inequality for pretentious products.* For |f_j(p)|,|g_j(p)|≤1, D(f₁f₂,g₁g₂;x)≤D(f₁,g₁;x)+D(f₂,g₂;x). If all g_j have unit modulus on the primes, this gives the usual triangle inequality for prime data. Used by [`AN.5/plan/pretentious-distance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-pretentious-distance). Source: Pretentious multiplicative functions and an inequality for the zeta-function, pp.3–4, inequality(5) and the unit-disc weight example.
- `AN.5/beurling-zeta-product` — *Beurling zeta and Euler product.* If Σ_n n^−σ (with generalized-integer multiplicities) converges for every real σ>1, then ζ_P(s)=Σ_n n^−s=∏_j(1−p_j^−s)^−1 on Re s>1, absolutely and locally uniformly. The convergence hypothesis is additional to the prime-system axioms. Used by [`AN.5/plan/beurling-all-log-remainders`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-beurling-all-log-remainders). Source: On general prime number theorems with remainder, §2.1 pp.2–3, (5)–(7) and displayed discrete Euler product.
- `AN.7/lerch-compact-series-bound` — *Lerch compact convergence.* On every compact subset of |z|<1, Re c>0, s∈C, the Φ series and each fixed derivative in z,s,c converge uniformly and absolutely. Used by [`AN.7/plan/complex-hurwitz-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-complex-hurwitz-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-even-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-even-functional-equation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-nonpositive-special-values`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-nonpositive-special-values), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-odd-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-odd-functional-equation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-pde`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-pde), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch zeta function II. Analytic continuation, §2 p.4 (2.1) and §5 pp.20–22 termwise derivative proof.
- `AN.7/lerch-parameter-shift` — *Lerch shift identity.* On the initial convergence domain, Φ(z,s,c)=c^−s+zΦ(z,s,c+1). For an already constructed analytic continuation it transports along matching lifted paths, including the shifted c path, by uniqueness. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch zeta function II. Analytic continuation, §4 p.17, (4.30)–(4.32), specialized to N=0.
- `AN.7/lerch-z-derivative` — *Lerch lowering relation.* On the initial domain, z∂_zΦ(z,s,c)+cΦ(z,s,c)=Φ(z,s−1,c). For an already constructed continuation it transports along matching lifted paths by uniqueness. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-nonpositive-special-values`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-nonpositive-special-values), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-pde`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-pde). Source: The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values, Theorem2.3 p.13 (2.3), §4 Theorem4.1 and proof p.33.
- `AN.7/lerch-c-derivative` — *Lerch raising relation.* On the initial domain, ∂_cΦ(z,s,c)=−sΦ(z,s+1,c), For an already constructed continuation the identity transports along the matching s+1 path by uniqueness. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-pde`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-pde). Source: The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values, Theorem2.3 p.13 (2.4), §4 Theorem4.1 and proof p.33.
- `AN.7/lerch-integral-representation` — *Lerch integral representation.* There exists a jointly holomorphic principal-sheet extension F(s,z,c) on Re s>0, Re c>0, z∈C\[1,∞), agreeing with the defining Φ series for |z|<1, such that F(s,z,c)=Γ(s)^−1∫_0^∞t^(s−1)exp(−ct)/(1−zexp(−t))dt. The integral is absolutely convergent; its formula is not asserted for the totalized series outside |z|<1. Used by [`AN.7/plan/complex-hurwitz-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-complex-hurwitz-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-even-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-even-functional-equation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-odd-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-odd-functional-equation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch zeta function II. Analytic continuation, §2 p.5, (2.2)–(2.4), integral cut-domain paragraph; §4 (4.18)–(4.23).
- `AN.7/lerch-c-monodromy` — *Monodromy around c=−n.* On the principal Lerch-zeta germ ζ(s,a,c)=Φ(exp(2πia),s,c), a positive loop around c=−n (n≥0) changes the branch by (e^(−2πis)−1)e^(2πina)(c+n)^−s, with the same logarithm lift. Loops about positive integer c have zero monodromy. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch zeta function II. Analytic continuation, Theorem4.5 (4.15) p.14, complete finite-shift proof (4.28)–(4.34) pp.17–18.
- `AN.7/lerch-a-monodromy` — *Monodromy around a=n.* For the lifted principal Lerch-zeta branch, a positive loop around a=n∈Z changes it by −(2πi)^s Γ(s)^−1(a−n)^(s−1)e^(−2πic(a−n)), with (2πi)^s defined by log(2π)+iπ/2 and the continued logarithm of a−n. On the fundamental strip0<Re a<1, the logarithm of a−n is cut along the negative imaginary axis with argument in(−π/2,3π/2). Equivalently, for n≥1 replace(a−n)^(s−1) by exp(πi(s−1))(n−a)^(s−1), whose base has positive real part; for n≤0 use the principal logarithm of a−n. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-cover-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-cover-continuation), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch zeta function II. Analytic continuation, Theorem4.5 (4.11) pp.13–14, negative-imaginary cut convention; complete contour/residue proof (4.18)–(4.27) pp.14–17.
- `AN.2/canonical-factor-pair` — *Paired genus-one factors.* E₁(w)E₁(−w)=1−w² for all w∈C. Used by [`AN.2/plan/paired-product-strict-derivatives`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-paired-product-strict-derivatives). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §8.2, Theorem8.7 and its genus-one product, printed pp.48–49.
- `AN.2/xi-entire-and-endpoints` — *Xi is entire with nonzero endpoints.* ξ is entire and ξ(0)=ξ(1)=1/2. Used by [`AN.2/plan/classical-zero-free-region`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-classical-zero-free-region), [`AN.2/plan/green-tao-zeta-strip`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-green-tao-zeta-strip), [`AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-rational-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula), [`AN.3/plan/riemann-von-mangoldt-count`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-riemann-von-mangoldt-count), [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/zeta-zero-multiset`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-zeta-zero-multiset). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §5.1 xi definition, p.35; Lemma8.3 integral display, p.47.
- `AN.5/medium-prime-product-card` — *Distinct-product cardinality.* For x≥2,m≥0, #N_m(x)=binomial(#{p prime:x/2≤p≤x},m). Used by [`AN.5/plan/medium-prime-cardinality`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-medium-prime-cardinality). Source: Irreducibility of random polynomials: general measures, §3.6, definition and (3.4), p.26.
- `AN.5/pretentious-square-nonnegative` — *Squared pretentious-distance formula.* Under the prime unit-disc hypotheses, D(f,g;x)²=Σ_{p≤x}(1−Re(f(p)conj(g(p))))/p≥0. Used by [`AN.5/plan/pretentious-distance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-pretentious-distance). Source: Pretentious multiplicative functions and an inequality for the zeta-function, Weighted norm discussion pp3–4.
- `AN.7/lerch-zero-order-value` — *Lerch at order zero.* Φ(z,0,c)=1/(1−z) for |z|<1, Re c>0. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-boundary-degeneration`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-boundary-degeneration), [`AN.7/plan/lerch-nonpositive-special-values`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-nonpositive-special-values). Source: The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values, Theorem5.1, (5.3) and m=0 proof p.36.
- `AN.2/zero-reciprocal-truncation-bound` — *Truncated reciprocal weights of zeros.* Under the family/count hypotheses there is K>0, depending on α,C,b, such that for R≥2, Σ_{|α_i|<R}|α_i|⁻¹≤K R^(b−1). The sum is finite and counts repeated zeros. Used by [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 8.7 proof, (8.2.4), printed p.49; Exercise 8.4.10, printed p.52.
- `AN.2/zero-reciprocal-square-tail-bound` — *Reciprocal-square tail of zeros.* Under the family/count hypotheses there is K>0, depending only on C,b, such that for R≥1, the reciprocal-square series over |α_i|>R is summable and Σ_{|α_i|>R}|α_i|⁻²≤K R^(b−2). Used by [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 8.7 proof, (8.2.4), printed p.49; Exercise 8.4.10, printed p.52.
- `AN.2/canonical-product-inner-lower-bound` — *Lower bound for inner canonical factors.* Under the family/count hypotheses there is K>0 such that for R≥2, |z|=R and every finite subset S of indices with |α_i|<R/2, Σ_{i∈S}log|E₁(z/α_i)|≥−K R^b. Used by [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 8.7 proof, (8.2.4), printed p.49; Exercise 8.4.10, printed p.52.
- `AN.2/canonical-product-middle-lower-bound` — *Lower bound for middle canonical factors.* Under the family/count hypotheses there is K>0 such that for R≥2 satisfying |R−|α_i||>|α_i|⁻² for every index, |z|=R and every finite S with R/2≤|α_i|≤2R, Σ_{i∈S}log|E₁(z/α_i)|≥−K R^b(1+log(2R)). Used by [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 8.7 proof, (8.2.4), printed p.49; Exercise 8.4.10, printed p.52.
- `AN.2/canonical-product-outer-lower-bound` — *Lower bound for outer canonical factors.* Under the family/count hypotheses there is K>0 such that for R≥2 and |z|=R the unordered outer product P_out(z)=∏_{|α_i|>2R}E₁(z/α_i) is nonzero and log|P_out(z)|≥−K R^b. Used by [`AN.2/plan/order-one-hadamard`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-order-one-hadamard). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Theorem 8.7 proof, (8.2.4), printed p.49; Exercise 8.4.10, printed p.52.
- `AN.2/xi-zero-critical-strip` — *Every xi zero lies in the open critical strip.* For every complex ρ with ξ(ρ)=0,0<Re ρ<1. Used by [`AN.2/plan/classical-zero-free-region`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-classical-zero-free-region), [`AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-rational-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula), [`AN.3/plan/riemann-von-mangoldt-count`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-riemann-von-mangoldt-count), [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/zeta-zero-multiset`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-zeta-zero-multiset). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §5.1 Remark5.2, p.35; §8.3 p.51.
- `AN.3/zeta-poisson-zero-weight` — *Uniform reciprocal-square zero weight.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for every real t, Σ_(ξ(ρ)=0)mρ/(1+(t−Imρ)²) is summable and at most C log(2+|t|), with mρ=analyticOrderNatAt ξρ. Used by [`AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-rational-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula), [`AN.3/plan/riemann-von-mangoldt-count`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-riemann-von-mangoldt-count), [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Exercise8.4.9 p.52; Lemma9.4 and Exercise9.6.1 pp.54,58.
- `AN.3/zeta-trivial-zero-simple` — *Trivial zeta zeros are simple.* For every natural n≥1, analyticOrderNatAt riemannZeta(−2n)=1. Used by [`AN.3/plan/von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-von-mangoldt-explicit-formula-and-pnt-error). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, Remark5.2 p.35; Lemma9.2 p.54, trivial-zero residues.
- `AN.3/primitive-character-unit-height-zero-count` — *Conductor-uniform local Dirichlet zero count.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ of conductor q≥1 and every real u, the nontrivial L-zero occurrences with u≤Imρ≤u+1 number at most C log(q(2+|u|)). Used by [`AN.2/plan/dirichlet-conductor-zero-free-region`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-dirichlet-conductor-zero-free-region), [`AN.2/plan/rational-pnt-error`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-rational-pnt-error), [`AN.3/plan/character-half-interval-formula`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-3-plan-character-half-interval-formula). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §10.2 Lemma10.3 p.60, referring to Davenport§16.
- `AN.4/artin-local-reciprocal-bound` — *Uniform finite Artin factor bound.* For d∈N,0≤m≤d,0≤t≤θ<1 and α₁,…,α_m∈C with |α_j|=1, put A(z)=∏_{j=1}^m(1−α_j z). For |z|=t, A(z)≠0, |A(z)^−1|≤(1−θ)^−d and |A(z)^−1−1|≤d t(1−θ)^−d. The assertion includes d=m=0. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-derivative-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-derivative-one), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-functional-equation), [`AN.4/plan/artin-value-one-subpower`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-value-one-subpower), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.2 p.128 local O(p^−s) estimate.
- `AN.4/artin-ramified-induction-polynomial` — *Ramified local Artin induction identity.* For L/K finite Galois with group G,H≤G,F=L^H and σ a finite-dimensional complex representation of H, at every nonzero prime p of K, P_{p,Ind_H^Gσ}(T)=∏_{q|p in F}P_{q,σ}(T^{f(q/p)}). The right polynomials are defined from Gal(L/F)=H, their own inertia invariants and arithmetic Frobenius modulo inertia. Used by [`AN.4/plan/artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-induction-versus-artin-holomorphy), [`AN.4/plan/artin-log-derivative-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-log-derivative-one), [`AN.4/plan/artin-value-one-subpower`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-artin-value-one-subpower), [`AN.4/plan/brauer-meromorphic-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-brauer-meromorphic-continuation), [`AN.4/plan/heilbronn-simple-real-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-4-plan-heilbronn-simple-real-zero). Source: Notes on analytic number theory, §22.5 Theorem22.4 sketch p.129; full ramified local identity is a required expansion.
- `AN.5/unit-disc-product-distance` — *Unit-disc product distance inequality.* For complex z,w with |z|,|w|≤1, sqrt(1−Re(zw))≤sqrt(1−Re z)+sqrt(1−Re w). Used by [`AN.5/plan/pretentious-distance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-pretentious-distance). Source: Pretentious multiplicative functions and an inequality for the zeta-function, p.4 first paragraph, extension of the η product inequality to the closed unit disc.
- `AN.5/mangoldt-polynomial-mean-square` — *Prime-weighted Dirichlet-polynomial mean bound.* There is an absolute C>0 such that for T≥1, x≥1 and any complex coefficients a(n), the integral from −T to T of |∑_{T²≤n≤x}a(n)Λ(n)exp(−it log n)|² is at most C∑_{T²≤n≤x}n|a(n)|²Λ(n). The finite sums use inclusive real cutoffs. If x<T² they are empty. Used by [`AN.5/plan/halasz-integral-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-halasz-integral-bound). Source: A new proof of Halász’s theorem, and its consequences, §2.3 Lemma2.6 and its complete proof, p.11.
- `AN.5/smooth-largest-prime-decomposition` — *Largest-prime-factor smooth decomposition.* For x≥1,y≥2, Ψ(x,y)+∑_{y<p≤x, p prime}Ψ(x/p,p)=floor x. Each positive non-y-smooth integer has a unique largest prime divisor p>y, and dividing by one copy of p leaves a p-smooth integer. Repeated largest primes are permitted. Used by [`AN.5/plan/dickman-fixed-u`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-dickman-fixed-u). Source: Integers without large prime factors, Introduction, printed p.411 (terminology); p.414 fixed-u formula(1.6); elementary largest-prime partition used for its limiting recursion.
- `AN.5/smooth-finite-euler-series` — *Finite-prime smooth Dirichlet series.* For y≥2 and σ>0, the nonnegative real series ∑_{n≥1, n y-smooth}n^(−σ) is summable and equals ∏_{p≤y}(1−p^(−σ))^(−1). This is a finite-prime identity valid for every positive σ, even σ≤1. Used by [`AN.5/plan/smooth-rankin-bound`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-smooth-rankin-bound). Source: Integers without large prime factors, Introduction, printed p.411 (terminology); p.414 equation(1.3), finite-prime geometric factorization.
- `AN.5/harmonic-euler-remainder` — *Harmonic sum remainder.* For every integer N≥1, 0<H_N−log N−γ<log(1+1/N)≤1/N, where H_N=Σ_{1≤n≤N}1/n and γ is the pinned Euler–Mascheroni constant. Used by [`AN.5/plan/dirichlet-divisor-average`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-dirichlet-divisor-average). Source: The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Theorem1.11 and complete proof, printed pp.15–16; pinned Euler-sequence inequalities.
- `AN.5/divisor-hyperbola-identity` — *Divisor hyperbola identity.* For real x≥1 and M=floor(sqrt x), Σ_{1≤n≤floor x}τ(n)+M²=2Σ_{1≤a≤M}floor(x/a). The equality is exact, including x at a perfect square. Used by [`AN.5/plan/dirichlet-divisor-average`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-dirichlet-divisor-average). Source: The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Hyperbola discussion, printed pp.38–39, (3.4)–(3.5) and Theorem3.3 proof.
- `AN.5/beurling-count-growth` — *Beurling counting growth from summability.* For a Beurling system P, real σ>0 and S=Σ_a norm(a)^−σ with summable nonnegative summands, N(x)≤S x^σ for x≥1, and π_P(x)≤N(x). Thus convergence for every σ>1 gives N(x),π_P(x)=O_ε(x^(1+ε)) for every ε>0. Used by [`AN.5/plan/beurling-all-log-remainders`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-beurling-all-log-remainders), [`AN.5/plan/beurling-zeta`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-beurling-zeta). Source: On general prime number theorems with remainder, §2.1 p.3, growth deduction after (6).
- `AN.5/beurling-prime-power-correction` — *Beurling higher-prime-power correction.* For x≥1, J=floor(log x/log p₁) and Π_P(x)=Σ_{1≤j≤J}π_P(x^(1/j))/j, all later terms are0. For x≥p₁, 0≤Π_P(x)−π_P(x)≤π_P(sqrt x)+π_P(x^(1/3))log x/log p₁. Under convergence for every σ>1, the difference is O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for every ε>0. Used by [`AN.5/plan/beurling-all-log-remainders`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-beurling-all-log-remainders). Source: On general prime number theorems with remainder, §2.1 p.3, (7) and subsequent prime-power bounds.
- `AN.7/lerch-z-monodromy-shift` — *Lerch z-loop monodromy and shifts.* On D={s∈C,z∈C\[0,∞),0<Re c<1}, choose Log z with 0<Im Log z<2π and a=Log z/(2πi). Put f_p=e^(2πipc)z^−c(a−p)^(s−1) for p≤0, and f_p=e^(πi(s−1))e^(2πipc)z^−c(p−a)^(s−1) for p≥1, using principal logarithms of the positive-real-part bases. For the source upper-connector based loops Z₀,Z₁ about 0,1, the principal germ has M_Z₀Φ=0 and M_Z₁Φ=−(2πi)^s f₀/Γ(s). The residue functions analytically continue to the universal cover, and continuation along Z₀^k sends f_p to f_(p−k); positive continuation along Z₁^k multiplies f₀ by e^(2πiks) and fixes f_p for p≠0; c loops fix every f_p. This corrects the published (3.28), as recorded in E29. The vanishing Z₀ identity for Φ concerns its principal germ, not invariance on every sheet. Used by [`AN.7/plan/lerch-solvable-descent`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-7-plan-lerch-solvable-descent). Source: The Lerch Zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values, §3.2 Lemma3.1 pp.21–24; §3.3 Theorem3.4 pp.25–28, (3.24)–(3.35); The Lerch zeta function III. Polylogarithms and special values, Definition3.3 (3.23), (3.24), Theorem3.4 (3.25)–(3.30), arXiv v1 printed pp.26–27.
- `AN.5/divisor-small-prime-log-bound` — *Small-prime divisor logarithm.* For a natural n≥2 and real y≥2, Σ_{p∈primeFactors(n), p≤y} log(v_p(n)+1) ≤ y log(1+log n/log 2). Used by [`AN.5/plan/divisor-maximal-order`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-5-plan-divisor-maximal-order). Source: The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Exercise2.9(b),(e),(f), printed pp.33–34, k=2.
- `AN.5/divisor-large-prime-log-bound` — *Large-prime divisor logarithm.* For a natural n≥2 and real y>1, Σ_{p∈primeFactors(n), y<p} log(v_p(n)+1) ≤ (log 2)log n/log y. - `AN.5/divisor-small-prime-loss` — *Vanishing small-prime contribution.* For real 0<δ<1 and η>0 there is L₀≥e such that for every real L≥L₀, L^(1−δ)log(1+L/log 2) ≤ η L/log L.
