- `AN.9/bc-dynamics-entire-core` — *Entire Hecke orbit maps.* For each f in the finite-support Hecke core, z↦ι(σ_z f) is an entire C_Q-valued map, supported on the same finite set of double cosets. For real t it is implemented in λ by the diagonal unitary with weights a(g)^(−it). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3 §4.2, pp.460–462.
- `AN.9/bc-gibbs-strip-series` — *Gibbs strip correlations.* For β>1 and core a,b, the Gibbs correlation Σk ζ(β)⁻¹k^(−β)⟨ε_k,π_u(a σ_z b)ε_k⟩ converges locally uniformly on C and uniformly on each closed real strip of bounded imaginary height. On the KMS strip 0≤Imz≤β it has the required two boundary values; finite normal-form reindexing supplies the upper boundary. Used by [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, Definition 3.6, p.446; §4.6, (3.139)–(3.141), p.475.
- `AN.9/bc-bounded-state-extension` — *Positive Hecke states extend boundedly.* Every normalized positive complex-linear φ on the BC core has |φ(f)|≤‖λ(f)‖, and therefore a unique norm-one positive continuous extension to C_Q. Its restriction is φ; extensions agree by core density. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry), [`AN.9/plan/bc-completed-coefficient-state`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-completed-coefficient-state), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/bc-vector-ground-state`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-vector-ground-state), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Hecke algebras, type III factors and phase transitions with spontaneous symmetry breaking in number theory, §4, Proposition 18 and complete proof, pp.431–433.
- `AN.9/bc-strip-core-bound` — *Uniform correlation bound on the closed strip.* Let φ be a completed state satisfying the core KMS identity at β>0. For core a,b, F(z)=φ(ι(a σ_z b)) is entire and bounded on 0≤Imz≤β. The two boundary bounds are≤‖ι(a)‖‖ι(b)‖; the three-lines principle gives the same bound throughout the strip. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Definition 3.6, p.446; (3.19), p.450.
- `AN.9/bc-real-dynamics-extension` — *Extending real dynamics to the C*-completion.* The real σt are isometric star automorphisms in the left representation and extend to a point-norm-continuous automorphism group on C_Q. The complex σz is retained only on the entire dense Hecke algebra. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Hecke algebras, type III factors and phase transitions with spontaneous symmetry breaking in number theory, §4, Proposition 18 and complete proof, pp.431–433.
- `AN.9/bc-dynamics-continuous` — *Point-norm continuous completed dynamics.* For every a∈C_Q, t↦σ_t(a) is continuous. Approximate a in norm by a core element, whose orbit is a finite exponential sum, and use the isometry of every σ_t to bound both approximation errors. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground), [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3 §4.2, pp.460–462.
- `AN.9/bc-analytic-core-strip-equivalence` — *The analytic core and the strip KMS condition.* For β>0 a completed state is KMSβ exactly when its restriction to the dense Hecke core satisfies IsKMS β. In the core-to-strip direction, approximate both completed arguments by core arguments; the uniform strip estimate makes their correlation functions Cauchy uniformly on the closed strip. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence), [`AN.9/plan/gibbs-states-are-kms`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-gibbs-states-are-kms). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, Definition 3.6 and entire-element condition (3.17), pp.446–447; the converse analytic-core theorem is an additional source gap.
- `AN.9/bc-finite-prime-projection` — *Finite-prime orbit projection.* For a finite prime set A, NA is its generated multiplicative monoid and WA={x∈Ẑ:xp∈Zp× for p∈A}. On WA the projection to NA-invariant functions is PAf(x)=ζA(β)^(−1)Σn∈NA n^(−β)f(nx), extended along NA-orbits, where ζA(β)=∏p∈A(1−p^(−β))^(−1). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Proposition proof, projection formula (2) and verification, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-local-character-density` — *Local characters form a dense family.* Functions depending on finitely many p-adic coordinates and valuation shells, with characters of local unit quotients, span a dense subspace of L²(Ẑ,μβ). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Proposition proof, local characters and valuation translates, pp.2–3.
- `AN.9/bc-prime-progression-divergence` — *Reciprocal primes in progressions.* Fix N≥1 and a coprime to N. The fixed-progression prime asymptotic π(X;N,a)∼Li(X)/φ(N) implies Σp≤X,p≡a(modN)1/p=(1/φ(N))log log X+o(log log X). In particular Σp≡a(modN)p^(−β) diverges for 0<β≤1. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity), [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Proposition proof, p.3 (Dirichlet input); partial summation is the local refinement.
- `AN.9/bc-nontrivial-character-projection` — *Nontrivial characters are annihilated in the critical interval.* For0<β≤1 and a nontrivial local unit characterχ, the increasing-prime projections P_Aχ tend to0: their product coefficients contain factors (1−p^(−β))/(1−χ(p)p^(−β)), and divergence of the prime reciprocal sum in a suitable character sector forces the product to0. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Proposition proof, nontrivial character product and progression argument, p.3.
- `AN.9/bc-decreasing-projections` — *Decreasing orthogonal projections.* Let Hn be a decreasing sequence of closed subspaces of a Hilbert space and H=intersection Hn. Their orthogonal projections Pn satisfy ‖Pn v−P v‖→0 for every v. In the finite-prime exhaustion, Hn consists of functions invariant under multiplication by all primes in its first n entries. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-critical-ergodicity`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-critical-ergodicity). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Projection exhaustion in the Proposition proof, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-canonical-extreme` — *Ergodic scaling measure is extreme.* For 0<β≤1, if μβ=tμ1+(1−t)μ2 for normalized β-scaling measures and 0<t<1, then μ1=μ2=μβ. The Radon–Nikodym density dμ1/dμβ is bounded by 1/t and Q+×-invariant, hence constant by ergodicity; normalization makes the constant one. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-low-temperature-uniqueness`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-low-temperature-uniqueness). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Corollary proof, p.3; direct measure form of extremality.
- `AN.9/bc-unit-average` — *Unit average of a scaling measure.* For any normalized β-scaling measure μ, its average over W=Ẑ× with normalized Haar measure is again normalized and β-scaling, is W-invariant, and equals the canonical product-density μβ. Equality follows from finite valuation/unit cylinders, then a countable rational-dilate exhaustion of A_f. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-low-temperature-uniqueness`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-low-temperature-uniqueness). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Unique W-invariant measure, p.2; Corollary argument, p.3.
- `AN.9/bc-extreme-average-rigidity` — *Extreme unit average is constant.* Let μ be a normalized scaling measure whose compact-unit average is the extreme μβ. Then u_*μ=μβ for every u∈W. For any finite-measure cylinder test, a nonconstant continuous value in u would split Haar into two positive pieces and give a nontrivial convex decomposition of μβ. Cylinder tests separate measures; setting u=1 proves μ=μβ. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-low-temperature-uniqueness`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-low-temperature-uniqueness). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Corollary conclusion and averaging argument, p.3.
- `AN.9/bc-corner-expectation` — *Diagonal expectation in the full corner.* The reduced crossed product has the positive contractive expectation E(Σq fq Uq)=f1. Its compression to pBp maps to C(Ẑ), preserves 1 and is faithful. The dynamics multiplies the q-term by q^(it). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence). Source: From endomorphisms to automorphisms and back: dilations and full corners, Laca §3.2, p.9; Neshveyev 2000 scaling correspondence, p.1.
- `AN.9/bc-measure-to-kms` — *Scaling measure produces a KMS state.* For β>0 and a normalized β-scaling μ, the functional φμ(a)=∫Ẑ E(a) dμ is a completed KMSβ state. The rational covariance and μ(qE)=q^(−β)μ(E) prove the core KMS identity. It is positive and normalized by the expectation. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Neshveyev 2000 scaling correspondence (1β), p.1.
- `AN.9/bc-kms-to-measure` — *KMS restriction reconstructs a scaling measure.* For β>0, restrict φ to C(Ẑ) and use the existing positive-functional measure representation. The KMS dilation identity implies ν(nE)=n^(−β)ν(E). This extends uniquely to a Radon μ on A_f with μ(Ẑ)=1 and μ(qE)=q^(−β)μ(E). Nonidentity rational terms have zero expectation in φ: use dynamics invariance when q≠1. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-scaling-correspondence`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-scaling-correspondence). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Neshveyev 2000 scaling correspondence, p.1.
- `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-orbits` — *Unit-orbit decomposition above the critical temperature.* Forβ>1, the disjoint sets nẐ× cover a μβ-full subset ofẐ, and μβ(Ẑ×)=∏p(1−p^(−β))=ζ(β)^(−1). Every scaling measure is reconstructed from a probability measure onẐ× by the weighted orbit sums. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres), [`AN.9/plan/kms-classification`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Introduction, unit-orbit decomposition after (1β), pp.1–2.
- `AN.9/bc-high-beta-unit-measure` — *High-beta unit-mass reconstruction.* For β>1 any normalized scaling μ is carried by the disjoint sets qW, q∈Q_+×, W=Ẑ×, and μ(W)=1/ζ(β). Its normalized unit restriction ν=ζ(β) μ|W is a probability measure. Conversely μν=ζ(β)⁻¹Σq∈Q_+× q^(−β)(q_*ν) is the unique scaling measure with that unit restriction. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres), [`AN.9/plan/kms-classification`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Neshveyev 2000, pp.1–2.
- `AN.9/bc-high-beta-affine-homeomorphism` — *Probability measures parameterize high-beta KMS states.* For β>1, ν↦∫W φβ,u dν(u) is an affine homeomorphism from Radon probability measures on the existing compact group W=Ẑ× to completed KMSβ states. The inverse is the normalized unit restriction of the corresponding scaling measure. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres), [`AN.9/plan/kms-classification`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Theorem 3.32, pp.474–476; Neshveyev 2000, pp.1–2.
- `AN.9/bc-high-beta-extremes` — *High-beta extreme states.* For β>1 the extreme KMS states are precisely φβ,u, u∈W; equality of two such states forces equality of their unit parameters. Dirac probability measures are exactly the extremes of ProbabilityMeasure W under the preceding affine homeomorphism. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-high-beta-barycentres`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-high-beta-barycentres), [`AN.9/plan/kms-classification`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, Theorem 3.32(2), pp.474–475.
- `AN.9/bc-unit-qmodz-adapter` — *Profinite units act on rational torsion.* The imported Ẑ× maps to AddAut(Q/Z) by its compatible residues u_N acting on each N-torsion subgroup. This is bijective and continuous in the topology of finite restrictions; every torsion element belongs to one of these finite subgroups. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry), [`AN.9/plan/bc-completed-barycentre`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-completed-barycentre), [`AN.9/plan/galois-action-on-ground-states`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-galois-action-on-ground-states). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, §4.1, pp.457–459; Theorem 3.32, p.474.
- `AN.9/bc-kms-symmetry-transitive` — *Symmetry on the high-beta extreme boundary.* For β>1, pullback by θ_v maps φβ,u to φβ,uv, with composition conventions fixed by the action on Q/Z. Therefore W acts freely and transitively on the high-beta extreme boundary. Used by [`AN.9/plan/kms-classification`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-kms-classification). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, Theorem 3.32(3), pp.474–475.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-finite-fourier` — *Finite cotangent Fourier identity.* For N>0 and ζ^N=1, Σ1≤j<N(j/N−1/2)ζ^j equals (ζ+1)/(2(ζ−1)) when ζ≠1 and equals 0 when ζ=1. The nontrivial value is cot(πt)/(2i) for ζ=exp(2πit). Passing to a multiple of N gives the same value for every N-torsion character; finite Fourier injectivity proves level independence in Q[Q/Z]. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation), [`AN.9/plan/bc-trigonometric-eisenstein`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-trigonometric-eisenstein). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Lemma 3.28 and its finite Abel-summation proof, pp.464–465.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-mobius-divisibility` — *Möbius divisibility identities.* For fn(j)=Σd|j μ(d)(j/d)^n, the projection sum Σd|N fn(d)πd evaluates on a Q-lattice to m^n, where m is the order of its N-torsion kernel. Keep n=1 and n=1−k, including negative exponents. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, equations (3.103)–(3.107), p.466.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-division` — *The Eisenstein division formula.* For k≥1, ΣNa=0 ek,a=γk Σd|N[(2^k−2)f1(d)+N^k f1−k(d)]πd, with γk=(2πi)^(−k)Σy∈Z\{0} y^(−k) in the source normalization (symmetric principal value for k=1; absolute convergence for k>1). For odd k the vanishing is interpreted consistently. Both the arithmetic coefficients and the degenerate-value convention are fixed by the preceding identities. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, Lemma 3.29, (3.108)–(3.109), p.467.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-prime-projections` — *Recovering prime-power divisibility projections.* All projections πp^b belong to the Q-algebra generated by e1,a. For odd p, solve the k=2 division relation inductively in b. For p=2 the leading π2^b coefficient vanishes, so use the relation at N=2^(b+1) to recover π2^b; e.g. π2=3+2Σ4a=0 e2,a. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, proof of Theorem 3.30, prime-power and doubled dyadic level step, pp.467–468.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-corner-power-sums` — *Rational power sums in a prime corner.* Let N=p^b, e=1−πp, and zj=e e1,j/N for 1≤j<N in the unital corner eQ[Q/Z]. The division formula gives Σj Pk(zj)=(N^k−1)γk e for every k≥1, where Pk is evaluated with corner unit e. Since Pk is monic of degree k, triangular induction gives Σj zj^k∈Qe. Zero roots and repeated roots are retained; there are N−1 indices. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, proof of Theorem 3.30, (3.110)–(3.113), p.468.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-newton-rationality` — *Newton identities in the reduced corner.* For the N−1 commuting elements zj in the preceding corner, all elementary symmetric functions σh(z1,…,zN−1) belong to Qe. Hence QN(X)=∏j=1..N−1(X−zj) is a monic degree-N−1 polynomial with rational scalar coefficients in that corner and QN(z1)=0. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, proof of Theorem 3.30, (3.113)–(3.115), pp.468–469.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-cotangent-roots` — *Roots of the reduced polynomial.* At an invertible Q-lattice, QN has multiset of roots cot(πj/N)/(2i), 1≤j<N. A unit character permutes this multiset. These roots are purely imaginary, so 1/2 is never a root. For even N the root at j=N/2 is zero and must be retained. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, proof of Theorem 3.30, (3.113)–(3.115), p.468.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-bezout-cayley` — *Polynomial recovery of the Cayley transform.* Since QN(1/2)≠0, gcd(QN,2X−1)=1 in Q[X]. Bézout yields U,V∈Q[X] with U(2X−1)+VQN=1. In the reduced corner, 2z1−e is invertible with inverse U(z1), and (2z1+e)U(z1)=e e(1/N). Thus this root-of-unity component lies in the Eisenstein algebra. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, proof of Theorem 3.30, (3.113)–(3.117), pp.468–469.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-semigroup-preservation` — *Eisenstein algebra is stable under semigroup endomorphisms.* For αn(f)=μn f μn*, αn(ek,a)=πn ek,a/n, independently of the chosen n-preimage a/n. The projections πn belong to the algebra generated by first functions, so αn preserves that algebra. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, (3.98)–(3.99), pp.464–465; final induction in Theorem 3.30, pp.469–470.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-prime-level-induction` — *Reassembly of the prime-power components.* For N=p^b, the (1−πp)e(1/N) component is supplied by the Cayley lemma. The other component is πp e(1/N)=αp(e(p/N)); the induction hypothesis at p^(b−1) and semigroup preservation put it in the Eisenstein algebra. At b=1 its lower-level input is e(0)=1. Adding the complementary components recovers e(1/N). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, last part of Theorem 3.30 proof, pp.469–470.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-roots-recovery` — *Recovering roots of unity from Eisenstein functions.* Every e(a), a∈Q/Z, belongs to the Q-algebra generated by first trigonometric Eisenstein functions. Prime-power denominators follow from reduced-corner Newton identities, the Bézout Cayley inverse and the explicit lower-level induction. General denominators follow by writing a as a sum of its prime-primary components and using e(a+b)=e(a)e(b). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, proof of Theorem 3.30, (3.110)–(3.117), pp.468–469.
- `AN.9/bc-cyclotomic-restrictions` — *Compatible finite cyclotomic restrictions.* For every field automorphism τ of C fixing Q, the exponents v_N∈(Z/NZ)× defined by τ(ζ_N)=ζ_N^(v_N) are compatible under divisibility. Conversely compatible exponents define an automorphism of Qcycl. The imported finite cyclotomic Galois identifications supply each v_N; the transition verification supplies their inverse-limit element v∈Ẑ×. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry), [`AN.9/plan/galois-action-on-ground-states`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-galois-action-on-ground-states). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Theorem 3.32(4), pp.474–476.
- `AN.8/characters-hadamard-orthogonality` — *Mod-eight character matrix orthogonality.* For H_i,a=ψi(2a+1), i,a∈{0,1,2,3}, H Hᵀ=HᵀH=4I. Thus Hᵀ/4 gives the exact inverse between twist coordinates and residue coordinates. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-functional-system`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-functional-system), [`AN.8/plan/double-reflection-matrix`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-reflection-matrix). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Proof of Lemma 2, character projections in (31)–(35), pp.362–363.
- `AN.8/double-normal-convergence` — *Normal convergence in the first tube.* On each compact K⊂{Res>1,Rew>1}, the odd (n,d) summands have a summable majorant n^(−σ0)d^(−ν0) with σ0,ν0>1. Consequently their double sum is normally convergent on K. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Definition (1), p.356; Lemma 2 proof, p.361.
- `AN.8/odd-double-sum-absolute` — *Absolute convergence in the initial double tube.* For Res>1 and Rew>1 the odd n,d double sum is absolutely convergent, locally uniformly on compact sub-tubes; hence it may be summed in either order. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 proof of Lemma 2, initial expansion (28), pp.361–362.
- `AN.8/odd-squarefree-factorization` — *Unique odd squarefree factorization.* Every positive odd d is uniquely d0k² with d0 positive odd squarefree and k positive odd. The Jacobi symbol χd equals χd0 away from prime divisors of k and vanishes at those prime divisors. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1, before (7), p.358; (29), p.361.
- `AN.8/quadratic-primitive-adapter` — *Quadratic conductor and root number.* For each odd squarefree d0 and twist i identify χd0ψi with its primitive real character of conductor q_i,η d0, parity κ_i and root number +1. Removed prime-2 and square-factor Euler factors agree with L2. Here η=d0 mod8, q and κ are exactly the table defining the reflection block; principal cases use meromorphic germs. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1, (7)–(13), pp.358–359.
- `AN.8/double-denominator-unit` — *Nonzero squarefree-series denominator.* For Re(s+2w)>1 the Euler product of L2(s+2w,χd0ψi) is nonzero. On any closed sub-half-plane Re(s+2w)≥1+δ, its reciprocal is bounded by ζ(1+δ), uniformly in d0 and the twist. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, (29), p.361.
- `AN.8/squarefree-square-decomposition` — *Separating square factors of the discriminant index.* Each odd d has a unique d=d0 d1² with d0 squarefree. In the initial tube, Z=ζ2(2s+2w−1)ζ2(2w)Σd0 odd squarefree L2(s,χd0ψ)ψ′(d0)/(d0^w L2(s+2w,χd0ψ)). Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 equation (29), p.362.
- `AN.8/quadratic-fourth-moment` — *Quadratic fourth moment.* For fixed σ∈[1/2,1] and ε>0, Σχ nonprincipal primitive real,condχ≤Q |L(σ+it,χ)|⁴ ≤ Cσ,ε [Q+(Q(1+|t|))^(2−2σ)](Q(1+|t|))^ε, for Q≥1 and t∈R. The conductor-one principal character is treated separately. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: A mean value estimate for real character sums, Theorem 2, p.238; §10, pp.267–269.
- `AN.8/quadratic-holder-first-moment` — *Primitive quadratic first moment.* On σ=1/2, Hölder and the O(X) count of primitive real characters of conductor≤8X give Σd0≤X,d0 odd squarefree,χd0ψi nonprincipal |L(1/2+it,χd0ψi)| ≤ Cε X^(1+ε)(1+|t|)^(1/4+ε). Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1, (14)–(16), pp.358–359.
- `AN.8/quadratic-square-factor-sum` — *Imprimitive square-factor bound.* For d=d0k² odd, the deleted Euler factors give |L2(s,χdψi)| ≤ |L2(s,χd0ψi)|∏p|k(1+p^(−Res)). On a fixed real strip with Res≥1/2 this product is Oε(k^ε), uniformly in Ims. Summing k≤√(X/d0) transports the primitive first moment to all odd d; the d0=1 principal term uses ζ2(s), off s=1. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1, (13)–(16), pp.358–359.
- `AN.8/quadratic-mean-bound-import` — *The first-moment input for the wider convergence tube.* For every ε>0 and twist i there is Cε>0 such that, for all X≥1 and t∈R, Σ1≤d≤X,d odd |L2(1/2+it,χdψi)| ≤ Cε X^(1+ε)(1+|t|)^(1/4+ε). The principal primitive character is separated before applying the quadratic fourth-moment theorem. A pole-aware strip extension is a separate lemma. Here L2 is oddLContinuation, not the totalized naive LSeries. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1 equation (16), p.359; application to (29), p.362.
- `AN.8/quadratic-pole-aware-strip-moment` — *Pole-aware strip first moment.* Fix a compact real interval I and ε>0. There exist C,N>0 such that for σ∈I, X≥1 and t∈R, Σd≤X,d odd |(σ+it−1)L2(σ+it,χdψi)| ≤ C X^(max(1,3/2−σ)+ε)(1+|t|)^N. At s=1 the term denotes the analytic extension of (s−1)L2(s), not totalized multiplication. Constants depend on I and ε, not X,t or i. The summands are the absolute values of the entire functions H_i,d=DoubleSeries.poleClearL. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §2.1 (16), p.359; Lemma 2 proof around (29), p.361.
- `AN.8/double-R1-convergence` — *Locally uniform convergence in R1.* The pole-cleared squarefree expression is holomorphic on R1={Rew>1,Res+Rew>3/2}; its only possible polar line there is s=1, from the trivial inner twist. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 proof following (29), p.362.
- `AN.8/reciprocity-swap-equation` — *The swap functional equation.* The 16-vector continuation satisfies Z(s,w)=A Z(w,s) wherever defined meromorphically. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 equations (31)–(32), p.362.
- `AN.8/quadratic-reflection-equation` — *The reflection functional equation.* The 16-vector continuation satisfies Z(s,w)=B(s)Z(1−s,s+w−1/2) as an equality of meromorphic germs. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 equations (10) and (33)–(35), pp.358,362–363.
- `AN.8/reflect-holomorphy-and-zero` — *The zero block that removes a false pole.* B(s) is holomorphic on Res<1 and its principal-twist block vanishes at s=0. This cancels the reflected principal w=1 pole where its image would otherwise introduce an extra pole; it does not assert that every block vanishes at zero. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 proof after (35), p.363.
- `AN.8/double-overlap-identity` — *Functional branches agree on overlaps.* On every connected nonempty open overlap of the R1,αR1,βR2,αR3 tube components, both branches have the same meromorphic germ: transport to the original absolute-convergence tube and use the identity theorem after clearing all encountered pole factors. Intersections used here are convex real tubes, hence connected. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, pp.362–363.
- `AN.8/double-reflected-pole-cancellation` — *Cancellation of spurious reflected poles.* During the R2→R3 gluing, the only candidate new pole beyond s=1,w=1,s+w=3/2 is the reflected principal-twist pole through s=0. The principal block B1(0)=0 cancels it. Track pole orders as germs; multiplying totalized zero values is insufficient. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, paragraph following (35), p.363.
- `AN.8/tube-overlap-gluing` — *Gluing the four continued tubes.* R2=α(R1)∪R1; R3=β(R2)∪R2; R4=α(R3)∪R3. The functional equations agree on their nonempty open overlaps and the gluing leaves possible poles only at s=1,w=1,s+w=3/2. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, §3 proof of Lemma 2, tube R1 and its images (36), pp.363–364.
- `AN.8/tube-bochner-extension` — *Bochner tube extension.* For connected open Ω⊆R² and f holomorphic on TΩ, there is a unique holomorphic F on Tconv(Ω) with F=f on TΩ. The imaginary directions are unrestricted. This is a theorem on tubes, not on arbitrary punctured complex domains. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Multiple Dirichlet series and moments of zeta and L-functions, Definition 4.5 and Proposition 4.6, pp.37–38.
- `AN.8/tube-reciprocal-bound` — *Bound survives tube extension.* Under the Bochner hypotheses, if M≥0 and |f(z)|≤M for all z∈TΩ, then its extension F satisfies |F(z)|≤M throughout Tconv(Ω). Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Multiple Dirichlet series and moments of zeta and L-functions, Propositions 4.6–4.7, pp.37–38; bounded-shell application pp.43–44.
- `AN.8/double-affine-dihedral` — *Affine dihedral action.* The two maps α,β satisfy α²=β²=id and (αβ)^6=id. At (2,3), the six iterates of αβ are distinct, so its order is exactly six. These transformations act on the real-part tube bases as well as on C². Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, pp.362–364.
- `AN.8/double-shell-hull` — *Real shell convex hull.* After R4=R3∪αR3, set R5=R4∪βR4 and R6=R5∪αR5. The complement of the real-part base of R6 is the closed twelve-gon Ω with successive vertices (1,1),(1/2,1),(0,3/2),(0,1),(−1/2,1),(0,1/2),(0,0),(1/2,0),(1,−1/2),(1,0),(3/2,0),(1,1/2). It lies in x²+y²≤3, so the connected annulus 4<x²+y²<5 lies in the glued base and its convex hull contains Ω. The earlier R4 alone does not have bounded complement. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof and Fig.1, pp.363–364.
- `AN.8/double-gamma-quotient-growth` — *Gamma reflection block growth.* On each closed strip a≤Res≤b<1, the filled r_i,η(s) and hence entries of B(s) are bounded by C(1+|Ims|)^N. Stirling for the Gamma quotient gives a power of height; the Euler denominator has modulus at least 1−2^(b−1)>0 when e≠0. On a bounded height interval use holomorphy and compactness. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, (32)–(35), pp.362–364.
- `AN.8/double-shell-normalizer` — *Bounded normalization on the shell tube.* On the annular shell 4<Res²+Rew²<5 used in the last continuation step, the cleared branch F=PZ has a bound C(1+|Ims|)^N(1+|Imw|)^N from the R1 estimate and transported reflection estimates. Choose an integer M≥N. Then F/[(3+s)^M(3+w)^M] is holomorphic and bounded on the shell tube, and its denominator has no zero on the full tube Res²+Rew²<5. Bochner bounded extension of this normalized function fills the hole; multiplying the denominator restores F. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Final part of Lemma 2 proof, pp.363–364.
- `AN.8/tube-hull-extension` — *Filling the remaining real twelve-gon.* Let Ω⊆R² be connected and open and let f be holomorphic on TΩ={z:Re z∈Ω}. It has a unique holomorphic extension to Tconv(Ω) (Bochner). If |f|≤M on TΩ, the extension has the same bound. Apply this to the pole-cleared branch on the annular real shell around the omitted twelve-gon. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Multiple Dirichlet series and moments of zeta and L-functions, §4.3, Proposition 4.6, pp.37–38; application pp.43–44.
- `AN.8/local-measure-normalization` — *Self-dual versus integral-normalized measures.* For the alternating binary-cubic pairing [x,y]=x1y4−x2y3/3+x3y2/3−x4y1, self-dual dx=|3|^(−1)∏dxj. If each coordinate self-dual measure gives O mass q^(−e/2), then dx(O⁴)=|3|^(−1)q^(−2e). With dg(GL2(O))=1, bF=|3|^(−1)q^(−2e)(1−q^(−1))(1−q^(−2)). Dividing by dx(O⁴) yields the integral-normalized constant; at residue characteristic 3 the |3| factor cannot be discarded before this conversion. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-global-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-global-functional-equation), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin), [`AN.8/plan/local-density-coefficient-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-local-density-coefficient-comparison). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, (2.1)–(2.4), pp.37–38.
- `AN.8/local-orbit-jacobian` — *Binary cubic orbital Jacobian.* For an open orbit α and representative xα, the map g↦g·xα has covering degree oα. Its measure change satisfies dx/|P(x)|=bF dg along each sheet, with bF as in the local measure normalization. Consequently ∫αΦ dx=bF|P(xα)|/oα ∫G|det g|²Φ(g·xα)dg. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin), [`AN.8/plan/local-density-coefficient-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-local-density-coefficient-comparison). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, (2.4), p.38.
- `AN.8/cubic-adelic-convergence` — *Adelic binary cubic convergence.* For Res>1, the right-quotient binary-cubic integral converges absolutely and locally uniformly in s and is a tempered distribution in Φ. Wright uses exponent |det|^u with Reu>2; here u=2s. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-global-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-global-functional-equation), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. Part I: global theory, Theorem 4.1 and proof, pp.516–517.
- `AN.8/cubic-adelic-unfolding` — *Adelic orbital unfolding.* For Res>1 and a Schwartz–Bruhat Φ, Z(Φ,s)=Σ[x]∈GL2(F)\V(F)^ns |Stab(x)|^(−1)∫GL2(A_F)|det g|^(2s)Φ(g·x)dg. All rearrangements are justified by absolute convergence. Integral lattice restrictions require all class-group components, as the S-integral comparison shows. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-global-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-global-functional-equation), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. Part I: global theory, Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.1, pp.516–518.
- `AN.8/cubic-class-group-components` — *All class-group components in unfolding.* The S-integral adelic zeta decomposes over the full double quotient G(A_S)\G(A)/G(F), not just the identity lattice. Each component uses its associated rank-two lattice, binary-cubic lattice and arithmetic stabilizer. This is the analytic interface needed for the ST extension to nonprincipal locally free modules. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-global-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-global-functional-equation), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. Part I: global theory, Proposition 4.2, p.519; DW (6.8), p.73.
- `AN.8/local-split-orbit-factor` — *Split local factor.* For DW standard Φ1 and u=ω(π), the split auxiliary integral Iα(ω,Φ1)=(1+u)^2/(1−u). Its four disjoint valuation regions have masses 1/(1−u),u²/(1−u),u/(1−u),u/(1−u). Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, Theorem 3.1 proof, pp.43–44.
- `AN.8/local-unramified-quadratic-factor` — *Unramified quadratic local factor.* The standard quadratic auxiliary integral is (1+u²)/(1−u): its two regions have t unit or valuation one, with integral basis coordinates for the unramified quadratic extension. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, Theorem 3.1 proof, p.44.
- `AN.8/local-ramified-quadratic-factor` — *Ramified quadratic local factor.* The ramified quadratic auxiliary integral is (1+u)/(1−u). In an integral basis 1,θ with θ a uniformizer, the field norm valuation gives the two disjoint support regions used in the integral. This formulation does not require residue characteristic odd. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, Theorem 3.1 proof, p.44.
- `AN.8/local-unramified-cubic-factor` — *Unramified cubic local factor.* The unramified cubic auxiliary integral is (1+u²+u⁴)/(1−u³)=(1−u+u²)/(1−u), from three valuation regions t of orders 0,1,2. The numerator records all three regions rather than an unjustified geometric shell law. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, Theorem 3.1 proof, p.45.
- `AN.8/local-ramified-cubic-factor` — *Ramified cubic local factor.* For a ramified cubic extension with integral generator θ a uniformizer, the three support regions give (1+u+u²)/(1−u³)=1/(1−u). Norm(θ) is a uniformizer in the base field, so this valuation computation retains wild discriminant factors in the separate orbital Jacobian. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-orders-generating-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-orders-generating-series), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. II: local theory, Theorem 3.1 proof, p.45.
- `AN.8/local-orbital-euler-factor` — *Five local orbital Euler factors.* For Φ0=1_(O⁴), an unramified quasicharacter ω and a DW standard representative, put u=ω(π). Then Zα(ω,Φ0)=ηα(u)/[(1−qu³)(1−u²)], with η=(1+u)²,1+u²,1+u,1−u+u²,1 for types split, unramified quadratic, ramified quadratic, unramified cubic, ramified cubic respectively. A ramified ω gives zero. Characteristic zero permits residue characteristics 2 and 3; their discriminant and self-dual-measure factors remain in the preceding normalization. - `AN.8/cubic-absolute-convergence` — *Absolute convergence of cubic Shintani series.* Every ξF,α(s) and dual series converges absolutely on Res>1. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The average size of 3-torsion in class groups of 2-extensions, §3.2 Proposition 3.7(1), p.12; The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. - `AN.8/cubic-truncated-entire` — *Entire truncated cubic integral.* Restrict the right-quotient integral to |det g|≥1. The resulting Z+(Φ,u), with exponent u, is entire and a tempered distribution in Φ. On every compact u set its derivatives are dominated by the Siegel-set Schwartz majorant; u=2s is the arithmetic convention. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-global-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-global-functional-equation), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance), [`AN.8/plan/cubic-zero-at-origin`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-zero-at-origin). Source: The adelic zeta function associated to the space of binary cubic forms. Part I: global theory, Proposition 6.1 and proof, p.523.
- `AN.8/cubic-poisson-decomposition` — *Poisson decomposition of the global integral.* On Reu>2, additive Poisson on F^4 gives Z(Φ,u)=Z+(Φ,u)+Z+(Fourier Φ,2−u)+I(Φ,u), where I is the integral over |det|≤1 of the Fourier-transformed singular theta sum minus the original singular theta sum, including the determinant Jacobian |det|^(−2). The singular locus has exactly zero, triple-root and double-root rational orbits. - `AN.9/selberg-laplace-integral` — *Elementary half-order Laplace integral.* For a>0 and Rew>0, integral_0^infinity t^(−3/2) exp(−w²t−a²/(4t))dt=(2sqrtπ/a)exp(−aw), initially on Re(w²)>0 and then by holomorphic continuation in Rew>0. - `AN.9/selberg-transform-normal-convergence` — *Normal convergence of the hyperbolic transform.* For the scalar compact trace, choose Rew>0 and Re(w²)>C with w=s−1/2 and C large enough for the geodesic count. Continuation, not the integral itself, is then used outside this region. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-determinant-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-determinant-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §5 Lemmas 5.1–5.3, pp.16–18, with the explicit safe region.
- `AN.9/hyperbolic-laplace-mellin` — *Hyperbolic transform is the Selberg logarithm.* For real s>1, the Laplace–Mellin transform of the hyperbolic heat contribution in the shifted determinant has derivative at Mellin exponent0 equal to−log ZΓ(s). This is the scalar specialization of JSS Proposition5.4; the integral proof uses the explicit Laplace identity and the compact-uniform geodesic majorant. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-determinant-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-determinant-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §5 Lemmas 5.1–5.3 and Proposition 5.4, pp.17–18; determinant proof §6.
- `AN.9/identity-barnes-transform` — *Identity contribution and Barnes normalization.* Let C=area(X)/(4π)=g−1. The scalar identity factor is I_g(s)=exp(2C[s log(2π)+s(1−s)+logΓ(s)−2logG(s+1)]), where G is the classical Barnes G-function normalized by G(1)=1, G(s+1)=Γ(s)G(s) and the source asymptotic expansion. The full normalization/asymptotic input is required; recurrence alone is insufficient. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-determinant-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-determinant-comparison), [`AN.9/plan/selberg-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-functional-equation), [`AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §6 proof of Theorem 6.1, (6.5)–(6.7) and asymptotic constant, pp.21–24; (2.8)–(2.9), p.9; scalar (8.4), p.27.
- `AN.9/shifted-zeta-holomorphic` — *Two-parameter shifted spectral zeta.* On Reu>0, Rez>1 define ζu(z)=Σj≥0 exp(−z Log(λj+u)) with the principal logarithm. Compact-uniform Weyl bounds give joint holomorphy. Heat subtraction with exp(−ut) continues it meromorphically in z, jointly holomorphic in u, and regular at z=0. It satisfies ∂u ζu(z)=−z ζu(z+1) where both sides are initially convergent, hence as germs. Used by [`AN.9/plan/shifted-entire-determinant`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-shifted-entire-determinant). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §4 Laplace–Mellin continuation, pp.13–15; Theorem 6.1 determinant argument, p.20.
- `AN.9/shifted-genus-one-product` — *Genus-one determinant product.* Let ζ+ be the positive spectral continuation and F(z) its analytic pole clearance (z−1)ζ+(z) near 1. The shifted determinant extends as D(u)=u exp(−ζ+′(0)+F′(1)u)∏j≥1(1+u/λj)exp(−u/λj). The product is normally convergent on all compact u sets since Σλj^(−2)<∞. On Reu>0 it equals exp(−∂z ζu(0)). Used by [`AN.9/plan/shifted-entire-determinant`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-shifted-entire-determinant). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §4 regularization and eigenvalue product (4.4), pp.13–15.
- `AN.9/selberg-identity-germ` — *Branch-independent identity factor.* For integer g≥2, the scalar identity factor has the single-valued meromorphic form I_g(s)=(2π)^(2(g−1)s) exp(2(g−1)s(1−s)) Γ(s)^(2(g−1))/G(s+1)^(4(g−1)). It equals the stated exponential logarithmic formula on a simply connected right-half-plane. Its integer exponents remove logarithm branch ambiguity. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-determinant-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-determinant-comparison), [`AN.9/plan/selberg-functional-equation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-functional-equation), [`AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, Scalar formula (8.4), p.27, checked against §6 (6.5)–(6.7), pp.21–23; the conflicting literal specialization of (6.2), p.20, is recorded in E48.
- `AN.9/shifted-zero-divisor` — *Exact shifted determinant zero divisor.* D(u) vanishes exactly at u=−λj, with order equal to the eigenvalue multiplicity. Around each such u0, D(u)=(u−u0)^m h(u), with h holomorphic and nonzero at u0. The finite factors for that eigenvalue are separated from the normally convergent nonvanishing residual product. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §4 eigenvalue regularized product (4.4), pp.13–15.
- `AN.9/spectral-quarter-double-root` — *Spectral quadratic pullback multiplicity.* For q(s)=s(s−1), if D has order m at u0=−λ and q(s0)=u0, then D∘q has order m when s0≠1/2 and order 2m when s0=1/2 (necessarily λ=1/4). This uses q(s)−q(s0)=(s−s0)(s+s0−1); at s0=1/2 it is (s−1/2)². Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison). Source: New points of view on the Selberg zeta function, Zagier §1 spectral relation, p.2; polynomial pullback refinement.
- `AN.9/selberg-identity-nonvanishing` — *Identity factor at spectral points.* I_g is holomorphic and nonzero on Res>0. At s=0 it has a pole of order 2g−2, because Γ has a simple pole there and G(1)=1; at s=1 it is finite and nonzero. Thus spectral points in 0<Res<1 are unaffected, while ZΓ has order 2g−1 at 0 and order 1 at 1. Used by [`AN.9/plan/selberg-spectral-zero-comparison`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-selberg-spectral-zero-comparison). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §2.5 Barnes zeros, p.9; §8.1, pp.26–27; scalar identity factor.
- `AN.9/bc-prime-pair-ratio` — *Prime pairs with prescribed ratio and divergent weights.* For0<β≤1, λ>1 and ε>0 there are disjoint prime pairs(pn,qn) with |(qn/pn)^β−λ|<ε and Σn qn^(−β)=∞. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, §1 and §2, Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.1, pp.2–5.
- `AN.9/bc-valuation-tail-ratio` — *Valuation-tail cylinder ratios.* For distinct primes p,q, the valuation swap (vp,vq)=(0,1)→(1,0) has target/source cylinder mass ratio (q/p)^β. Under the pushforward-at-target convention, the derivative of this forward map x↦(p/q)x is (p/q)^β; the inverse map has derivative (q/p)^β. Both values enter the ratio-set subgroup. The factors (1−p^(−β))(1−q^(−β)) cancel. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, Theorem 2.1 proof, pp.4–5; §1 convention, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-prime-pairs-congruence` — *Prime pairs with controlled unit residues.* For N≥1, λ>1 and ε>0, fixed-progression PNT supplies disjoint prime pairs p_n,q_n≡1(modN) with q_n/p_n→λ and Σp_n^(−1)=∞. Select primes in two disjoint proportional intervals inside successive geometric blocks, matching their counts with a fixed positive density. For 0<β≤1 the pair-swap source masses also have divergent sum. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, Lemma 2.3 and proof, p.5, with fixed-progression refinement.
- `AN.9/bc-asymptotic-ratio-inclusion` — *Independent tail swaps give essential ratios.* On a product of countable probability spaces, suppose mutually disjoint finite coordinate blocks have bijective swaps with cylinder mass ratios approaching λ>0 uniformly and a divergent sum of source cylinder masses. Then λ belongs to the ratio set of the finite-tail equivalence relation. The pushforward derivative of the inverse swap at its target equals the forward cylinder mass ratio. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, §1 asymptotic ratio definition and inclusion, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-ratio-unit-lifting` — *Ratio witnesses lift through unit cylinders.* For any finite cylinder of integral adeles, choose its congruence level N and all its specified valuation primes. Tail pairs p,q≡1(modN), beyond those primes, act trivially on the cylinder unit residues. Their swaps therefore retain the independent-tail essential-ratio witnesses on the full adele space, rather than only on its quotient by W. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, Theorem 2.1 proof, pp.4–5; specialized congruence-cylinder lifting.
- `AN.9/bc-full-positive-ratio-set` — *All positive numbers belong to the ratio set.* For 0<β≤1 the nonsingular Q+× action on (A_f,μβ) has RatioSet=[0,∞). Its pushforward density is ρq(x)=q^β. Prime pairs with fixed unit congruences give every λ>1 after the β power; inverses give λ∈(0,1), and closure gives 0. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, §1 and §2, Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.1, pp.2–5.
- `AN.9/bc-ergodic-crossed-product-factor` — *Ergodicity makes the group-measure algebra a factor.* For the canonical μβ, the Q+× action is essentially free: qx=x with q≠1 forces x=0, a null point. For a countable essentially free nonsingular action on a standard sigma-finite measure space, the center of L∞(X,μ)⋊G equals L∞(X,μ)^G; ergodicity therefore makes it a factor. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Corollary proof, p.3.
- `AN.9/bc-ratio-factor-type` — *Full positive ratio set determines type III1.* For a countable essentially free ergodic nonsingular action on a standard sigma-finite measure space, RatioSet=[0,∞) implies its group-measure factor has type III1; equivalently its flow of weights is trivial. This is the operator classification input, distinct from the arithmetic ratio witnesses. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Von Neumann algebras arising from Bost–Connes type systems, §1 flow-of-weights/type criterion, p.2; Theorem 2.1, p.3.
- `AN.9/bc-full-corner-type` — *A nonzero full corner preserves factor type.* The GNS algebra of the diagonal-expectation KMS state is p(L∞(A_f,μβ)⋊Q+×)p, where p=1Ẑ and p≠0. A nonzero corner of a type III1 factor is again type III1. The C*-full corner identification and the von Neumann compression identification are separate requirements. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-type-three-one`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-type-three-one). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Corollary proof, p.3; Neshveyev 2009 §1, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-gibbs-tail-limit` — *The Gibbs limit and its uniform tail bound.* For β→∞ the Gibbs states converge weakly to the ε1 vector state, uniformly on each fixed norm-bounded observable set: the difference is at most2||a||(ζ(β)−1)/ζ(β), which tends to0. This supplies completed KMS∞ states. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-values-and-symmetry). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Chapter 3, (3.140)–(3.142), pp.475–476; weak Gibbs limit is the stated elementary consequence.
- `AN.8/double-growth` — *Polynomial growth of cleared double series.* For each compact real rectangle I×J there exist C,N>0 with |Eij(s,w)|≤C(1+|Ims|)^N(1+|Imw|)^N whenever Res∈I,Rew∈J. Here Eij is the entire cleared continuation. Used by [`AN.8/plan/double-series-continuation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-double-series-continuation). Source: Subconvexity for a double Dirichlet series, Lemma 2 proof, pp.363–364.
- `AN.8/cubic-residue-one` — *Cubic residue at one.* With AF=ζF(2)ρF/2^(r1+r2+1), residue at 1 is AF(1+3^(−rα−r2)). Here ρF is the residue of ζF at 1 and rα counts split real cubic factors. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance). Source: The average size of 3-torsion in class groups of 2-extensions, Proposition 3.7(2), p.12; DW Theorem 6.2(i), p.71.
- `AN.8/cubic-residue-five-sixths` — *Cubic secondary residue.* With BF=3^(r1+r2/2)ζF(1/3)ρF/[6·2^(r1+r2)D^(1/2)]·[Γ(1/3)^3/(2π)]^n, residue at 5/6 is BF·3^(−rα/2). All discriminants are absolute norms. Used by [`AN.8/plan/cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-8-plan-cubic-residues-and-entire-clearance). Source: The average size of 3-torsion in class groups of 2-extensions, Definition before Proposition 3.7 and Proposition 3.7(2), p.12.
- `AN.9/bc-kms-limit-ground` — *KMS-infinity limits are ground states.* For a unital C*-system with point-norm continuous dynamics, each KMS∞ state is a ground state. On every finite upper strip the KMSβ correlation functions, for sufficiently large β, are bounded by ‖a‖‖b‖; use normal families and boundary convergence. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Definition 3.7, p.447.
- `AN.9/bc-trivial-dynamics-test` — *Ground and KMS-infinity differ for trivial dynamics.* For M₂(C) with σ_t=id, every state is a ground state, while every KMSβ state is tracial and every KMS∞ state is tracial. The vector state a↦a₀₀ is ground and is not KMS∞: on matrix units it gives φ(E₀₁E₁₀)=1 and φ(E₁₀E₀₁)=0. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-kms-infinity-and-ground`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-kms-infinity-and-ground). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Definition 3.7 discussion, p.447.
- `AN.9/bc-local-density-normalization` — *Normalize the local scaling density.* For β>0 and every integer k, μβ,p({ordp x=k})=(1−p^(−β))p^(−kβ). Summing k≥0 gives μβ,p(Zp)=1; the singleton 0 has mass 0. Multiplication by p^j scales measurable masses by p^(−jβ). Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-adelic-scaling-measure`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-adelic-scaling-measure). Source: Ergodicity of the action of the positive rationals on the group of finite adeles and the Bost–Connes phase transition theorem, Neshveyev 2000 product-density formula, p.2.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-isometry-generation` — *Arithmetic generation after adjoining isometries.* The Q-algebra generated by all first functions and μn,μn* equals the normalized arithmetic form A1,Q spanned by μn e(a) μm*. The comparison to Q-valued Hecke functions is through σ−i/2 and is not a star-algebra identification. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Theorem 3.30, pp.467–470; rational-form convention pp.460–462.
- `AN.9/bc-eisenstein-complexification` — *Complexification of the arithmetic form.* The scalar-extension map C⊗Q A1,Q→H_C is an algebra isomorphism sending 1⊗μn e(a) μm* to the normalized complex normal form. Its image is dense in the completed BC algebra. Rational Hecke and arithmetic forms remain distinct subalgebras until the specified imaginary-time comparison. Used by [`AN.9/plan/bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-bc-arithmetic-algebra-generation). Source: Noncommutative Geometry, Quantum Fields and Motives, Ch.3, Theorem 3.30 and surrounding discussion, pp.460–470.
- `AN.9/spectral-continuation-output` — *Spectral continuation output.* The heat-asymptotic contract yields actual positive and shifted meromorphic functions, regular at z=0, agreeing with their convergent series on Rez>1. It also yields an analytic function F=(z−1)ζ+(z) near 1. These are the fields of SpectralContinuation; existence follows from the Mellin subtraction chain, not from an arbitrary function-valued placeholder. Used by [`AN.9/plan/spectral-regularity-zero`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-spectral-regularity-zero), [`AN.9/plan/spectral-zeta-series`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-9-plan-spectral-zeta-series). Source: Determinants of twisted Laplacians and the twisted Selberg zeta function, §4, pp.13–15; Sarnak §1, p.603.

It is imported, not planned again; the main packet keeps only the comparison to Mathlib vocabulary in AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems.
- `AN.2/fixed-progression-prime-number-theorem` → [`AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-qualitative-prime-number-theorems): Current Tau Ceti main proves this qualitative statement through the Tau Ceti roadmaps ArithmeticDirichletSeries (Layer 10.4, unconditional prime ideal theorem) and Chebotarev (Layers 11-14, with the arithmetic-progression specialization over the cyclotomic field). It is imported, not planned again; the main packet keeps only the comparison to Mathlib vocabulary in AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems.
- `AN.2/chebyshev-prime-count-transfer` → [`AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-qualitative-prime-number-theorems): The ψ→θ→π transfer is ArithmeticDirichletSeries Layers 6.2 and 10.2-10.3; the three conclusions are part of AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems.
- `AN.2/rational-mangoldt-boundary` → [`AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-qualitative-prime-number-theorems): The residue-one von Mangoldt boundary package for K = ℚ is the K = ℚ case of the Tau Ceti export primeIdealVonMangoldtBoundary (ArithmeticDirichletSeries 10.4); this proof ingredient served only the superseded qualitative PNT targets.
- `AN.2/progression-mangoldt-boundary` → [`AN.2/plan/qualitative-prime-number-theorems`](#target-analyticnumbertheory-an-2-plan-qualitative-prime-number-theorems): The progression boundary package is supplied inside Tau Ceti Chebotarev (Layers 5 and 11-12 over the cyclotomic field); this proof ingredient served only the superseded fixed-progression target.
